What excites you about designing and delivering reliable data solutions that improve data quality and drive better decisions across the insurance lifecycle?


Are you motivated by solving complex data challenges, working with modern engineering practices and exploring AI-assisted automation to create meaningful business impact?

About the Business

LexisNexis Risk Solutions is the essential partner in the assessment of risk. Within our Insurance vertical, we provide customers with solutions and decision tools that combine public and industry specific content with advanced technology and analytics to assist them in evaluating and predicting risk and enhancing operational efficiency. Our insurance risk solutions help drive better data-driven decisions across the insurance policy lifecycle, all while reducing risk. You can learn more about LexisNexis Risk at

About the Role

As a Data Engineer, you will design, develop, test and support reliable data solutions that enable high-quality data products and services. Initially focused on Data Management activities, you will play a key role in data profiling, validation, quality management and issue resolution while growing into broader Data Engineering ownership.

Working closely with technical teams and business stakeholders, you will translate data requirements into scalable and maintainable solutions, helping to improve data quality, operational efficiency and customer outcomes across our Insurance business.



Responsibilities

  • Own assigned data transfers and components, including collection, transfer and contributor/customer setup, with responsibility for their ongoing maintainability.
  • Collaborate with technical teams and stakeholders to understand data and product requirements and translate them into effective data solutions.
  • Design, develop, test and maintain efficient, repeatable and maintainable data engineering solutions using established coding and engineering practices.
  • Evaluate technical approaches and recommend solutions that balance delivery, data quality, testing and maintainability.
  • Perform Data Management activities, including data profiling, validation, quality management and investigation and resolution of data issues.
  • Troubleshoot data engineering issues, identify root causes and implement sustainable fixes.
  • Identify opportunities for automation, including AI-assisted engineering and intelligent automation, to improve productivity, troubleshooting and delivery.
  • Contribute to code reviews, technical specifications, database and workflow management, process improvement and adoption of relevant new technologies.

Requirements

  • Experience in Data Management, Data Engineering or a related technical data role.
  • Strong knowledge of data manipulation, profiling, validation and data quality practices.
  • Experience working with data models, data requirements and maintainable data solution designs.

Who We Are:

The Modern Classrooms Project (MCP) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that empowers educators to build classrooms that respond to every student’s needs. Founded by two award winning teachers, we lead a movement of educators in implementing a self-paced, mastery-based instructional model that leverages technology to foster human connection, authentic learning, and social-emotional growth.

To date, we have reached over 70,000+ teachers through our free online course and 20,000+ teachers through our Virtual Mentorship Program from over 200 school, district, and state partners. We are an ambitious, idealistic team led by former classroom teachers, and we are passionate about what we do.

Job Description:

The Educator Support Manager trains educators to use the Modern Classrooms Project instructional approach and mentors them through implementation. This role supports increased quality of teaching, leading to more students learning in responsive, personalized classrooms.

Roles and Responsibilities:

The Educator Support Manager, Math reports directly to the Director of Educator Support and will work on training and supporting approximately 100 educators in an assigned portfolio using our curriculum solutions, which provide educators with HQIM-aligned resources that enable them to effectively implement the Modern Classrooms instructional model with their curriculum.

The support may include:

  • Executing math training (on-site and virtually) for math educators
  • Regular outreach, in various forms, to educators
  • Regular coaching calls
  • Coordinating and facilitating workshops, events, and other professional learning opportunities, both in-person and virtually
  • Responding to educator inquiries
  • Conducting information sessions (in person or virtually)
  • Visiting Modern Classrooms to observe practice, provide feedback, and steward relationships
  • Completing administrative tasks and special projects (as assigned)

Must-Have Skills and Competencies:

  • Experience training educators in professional learning
  • Experience supporting educators with concrete suggestions and specific, effective feedback about instruction
  • Track record of strong communication skills across mediums including public speaking, presentations, writing, and in one-on-one interactions with educators
  • Excellent relationship-building skills, including listening, problem-solving, and following through on commitments
  • Exceptional organizational skills and record of managing a high volume of tasks, meeting deadlines, and fulfilling work obligations
  • Goals-oriented with a high degree of initiative and independence
  • Data-driven decision-maker with the ability to pivot seamlessly when presented with new data
  • Adaptability to work in a start-up environment, including readiness for remote, independent work and flexibility to meet the needs of a growing organization
  • Experience with productivity tools like Asana, Slack, and Google Workspace

Preferred Experiences:

  • Based in a major airport hub city
  • Experience utilizing the Modern Classrooms Project instructional model as an educator or instructional leader
  • Experience teaching or coaching math using Illustrative Mathematics or Eureka Math2 in grades three through twelve.
  • Experience with Salesforce or similar CRM

Compensation and Benefits: We aim to offer a competitive compensation package, as well as the opportunity to work in a fast-growing startup that is on a mission to improve education worldwide. This includes:

As a member of Experian's Global Security Office (EGSO), the Senior Enterprise Security Incident Manager (ESIM) serves as the Cyber Incident Commander for significant cybersecurity incidents, leading cross-functional response efforts across the enterprise

This hands-on technical role coordinates the full incident response lifecycle, from detection and containment through recovery and post-incident analysis, while providing executive-level communications, driving operational decision-making, and ensuring alignment with Experian's Global Information Security Incident Response Plan.

You will report to the CFC Senior Director of Incident Response as part of Experian's Cyber Fusion Center. As an individual contributor, you will partner with technical teams, business leaders, and executives. Your goals will be to minimize business impact, strengthen incident readiness, and improve our cyber resilience.

Must be available to respond to after-hours pages for potentially major security incidents and manage the CFC incident response during assigned nights, weekends, and holidays as part of an on-call rotation.

You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Lead enterprise-wide response to high-risk cybersecurity incidents as Cyber Incident Commander, validating and escalating incidents, directing cross-functional response efforts, and driving containment, eradication, recovery, and resolution.
  • Provide executive incident leadership by delivering updates to senior leaders and stakeholders, coordinating technical and business teams, supporting decision-making, and maintaining accurate incident documentation.
  • Enhance the incident response program through post-incident reviews, root cause analysis, lessons learned, and continuous improvements to response plans, playbooks, and operational processes.
  • Strengthen cyber readiness by leading tabletop exercises, partnering with business and technology stakeholders to validate response capabilities, identify gaps, and improve preparedness.
  • Support Cyber Fusion Center operations by maintaining awareness of emerging threats, collaborating across security and technology teams, participating in the on-call rotation, and contributing to plans that strengthen Experian's security posture.

Your background:

  • 8+ years of experience in security operations or information technology, with 5+ years in information security incident handling or response.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Experience leading/supporting investigations and response to complex cybersecurity incidents, including APTs, ransomware, DDoS, insider threats, web/mobile application attacks, and data exfiltration.
  • Knowledge of cyber incident response, digital investigation methodologies, and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), including incident triage, impact assessment, containment, remediation, and recovery.
  • Broad technical knowledge of enterprise and cloud environments, including operating systems, networking, security controls, enterprise technologies, and detection and response platforms.
  • Experience investigating complex incidents, performing root cause analysis, making risk-based decisions, and communicating technical findings to all audiences.
  • Leadership experience coordinating cross-functional incident response activities, influencing stakeholders, and managing multiple high-priority cybersecurity incidents.
  • Demonstrated initiative, including the ability to identify improvement opportunities, drive security enhancements, and operate effectively while keeping leadership informed.
  • Plus: Industry certifications in cybersecurity, incident response, digital forensics, or ethical hacking preferred (e.g., GIAC, CISSP, SSCP, CISM, EC-Council, Offensive Security).

Executive Assistant (EA)

Executive Support | Calendar Management | Travel Coordination | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a highly organized and proactive Executive Assistant (EA) to provide strategic administrative and operational support to senior leadership.

This is more than a traditional administrative role. You’ll serve as a trusted partner, helping executives stay focused on high-impact priorities by managing calendars, coordinating travel, handling executive communications, preparing meetings, and ensuring projects and follow-ups move forward seamlessly.

If you thrive in fast-paced environments, anticipate needs before they arise, and excel at keeping executives organized and productive, this role is an excellent opportunity.

What You’ll Own

Calendar & Scheduling Management

  • Manage complex executive calendars across multiple time zones.
  • Coordinate meetings, calls, travel, and scheduling priorities.
  • Resolve scheduling conflicts and optimize executive availability.
  • Utilize Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, Calendly, and related scheduling tools.
  • Ensure executives are fully prepared for upcoming meetings and commitments.

Executive Communication & Support

  • Draft, proofread, and send professional emails and executive communications.
  • Manage executive inboxes, prioritizing urgent requests and correspondence.
  • Screen calls, messages, and meeting requests.
  • Serve as a liaison between executives, clients, vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Handle confidential information with professionalism and discretion.

Meeting Preparation & Follow-Up

  • Prepare meeting agendas, briefing documents, presentations, and talking points.
  • Gather and organize supporting materials before meetings.
  • Take meeting notes, document action items, and track follow-ups.
  • Ensure deadlines, priorities, and deliverables remain on schedule.

Travel & Logistics Coordination

  • Coordinate domestic and international travel arrangements.
  • Book flights, hotels, transportation, and complete travel itineraries.
  • Manage last-minute schedule changes and travel adjustments.
  • Track travel expenses and assist with reimbursements.
  • Ensure seamless travel logistics for executives.

Project & Administrative Support

  • Track executive priorities, projects, and ongoing initiatives.
  • Follow up with internal teams to ensure deliverables and deadlines are met.
  • Conduct research and prepare reports, summaries, and briefing materials.
  • Maintain organized digital filing systems and documentation.
  • Support operational initiatives and special projects as assigned.

Requirements

Must-Have Qualifications

Experience

  • 3+ years of Executive Assistant or senior administrative support experience.
  • Experience supporting executives in fast-paced business environments.
  • Proven experience managing complex calendars across multiple time zones.
  • Experience coordinating executive travel and logistics.

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office.
  • Strong experience using calendar and scheduling tools.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Outstanding organizational, multitasking, and time management abilities.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information professionally.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience supporting startups, agencies, consulting firms, or high-growth organizations.
  • Familiarity with Slack, Zoom, Notion, Asana, ClickUp, or similar collaboration platforms.
  • Experience supporting multiple executives simultaneously.
  • Exposure to operations, project coordination, or business support functions.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • Exceptionally organized with outstanding attention to detail.
  • Proactive and able to anticipate executive needs.
  • Strong communicator who builds trust across teams and stakeholders.
  • Calm under pressure and adaptable to changing priorities.
  • Highly dependable with excellent follow-through.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Review executive calendars and prepare daily briefing notes.
  • Manage inboxes, scheduling requests, and executive communications.
  • Coordinate meetings, agendas, and follow-up actions.
  • Arrange travel plans and manage logistics.
  • Track project updates and ensure priorities stay on schedule.
  • Prepare reports, summaries, and next-day planning materials.

In short: You enable executives to operate at peak efficiency by managing schedules, communication, travel, and operational priorities with accuracy and professionalism.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Calendar accuracy and scheduling efficiency.
  • Timely communication and follow-up completion.
  • Executive satisfaction with operational support.
  • Smooth travel coordination and logistics management.
  • Reduction in scheduling conflicts and administrative delays.
  • Accuracy and organization of executive documentation.

Why Join Us?

  • Fully remote opportunity aligned with U.S. business hours.
  • High-visibility role supporting senior leadership directly.
  • Opportunity to work closely with decision-makers and executives.
  • Fast-paced, collaborative, and growth-oriented environment.
  • Exposure to executive operations, strategic initiatives, and business management.
  • Career growth opportunities into Operations, Project Management, Chief of Staff, or Executive Operations roles.

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  3. Practical Assessment (Executive Briefing Memo or Scheduling Scenario)
  4. Client Interview
  5. Offer & Background Verification

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the next step that completes your application and can be recorded whenever it’s convenient for you.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This helps the hiring team evaluate your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation after submitting your application.

Apply Now

If you’re a proactive Executive Assistant who excels at managing executive priorities, coordinating complex schedules, and keeping operations running smoothly behind the scenes, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and become a trusted partner to senior leadership in a dynamic remote environment.

jobs.title: Account Executive, Mid-Market
jobs.excerpt: Somewhere in your career, you closed a deal that wasn't supposed to close.
jobs.description:
Somewhere in your career, you closed a deal that wasn't supposed to close. You read the room before anyone else did. You qualified hard when it would have been easier to keep the deal warm. You pushed when the prospect was drifting and held your ground when they pushed back on price. And when it closed, it closed because of how you ran it — not because the lead was good.

That's the kind of Account Executive we're looking for.

What We Do

Every school district in America runs on service — parents need answers, teachers need support, IT teams need systems that work. Most districts cobble that together with disconnected tools, overwhelmed staff, and no real visibility into what's working.

Onflo built the platform that fixes that. Our unified service platform brings together customer service, help desk ticketing, call center operations, AI chat, and IT asset management — purpose-built for K-12 public education. When a district runs on Onflo, their staff spends less time firefighting and more time serving students.

That's the product you'll be selling. It's a good one. And the people who buy it — superintendents, IT directors, operations leaders — are trying to do something that matters.

The Role

You'll own a territory. Not work it — own it. New business quota, pipeline coverage, and the strategy underneath both. You'll know which districts are ready, which are warming, and which aren't worth your time — and you'll act accordingly. You'll source your own pipeline, run your own cycles, and close your own deals. When Marketing helps, great. When they don't, you still hit your number.

What you'll own:

  • New business quota attainment in a defined K-12 geographic territory
  • Self-sourced pipeline at 3–5x quota coverage
  • Full sales cycle: prospecting, discovery, demo, negotiation, close
  • Forecast accuracy you can defend in any deal review
  • Executive relationships across districts in your territory

Who Thrives Here

We'll be direct with you, because we think you'll appreciate it.

Onflo is a small, entrepreneurial team. We don't have a perfect playbook for everything. Priorities shift. Conversations can be intense. Communication isn't always tidy. Marketing won't always feed you the lead flow you want. Product won't always ship on the timeline you'd hope. We know that — and we're actively working on it. What we do have is a product that genuinely helps schools, clients who trust us, and a team that cares about doing the work well.

The people who do their best work here own their outcomes completely — no waiting, no excuses, no "the leads weren't there." They stay calm when priorities shift, build their own pipeline when the inbound is thin, and hold themselves to a higher standard than anyone else would set for them. They're direct without being harsh, coachable without being passive, and motivated by winning more than recognition. They ask for the meeting, ask for the demo, and ask for the close. They don't reflexively discount when a prospect pushes back on price. And underneath all of it, they genuinely care — about the districts they sell to, about the teammates next to them, and about doing the work right.

If you've spent your career waiting for clear direction, clean territory, and steady inbound flow before you produce — this probably isn't your role. If you've spent it figuring it out and hitting your number anyway — keep reading.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of B2B SaaS sales managing a full sales cycle, with a track record of quota attainment or overachievement
  • Demonstrated ability to self-source pipeline — not just work inbound or SDR-fed leads
  • Comfortable in every part of the cycle, especially the hard parts: qualifying out, holding price, asking for the close
  • Technically curious — you learn new software by getting in and clicking around, and you can hold your own with an IT director without a Solutions Engineer in the room
  • Active Salesforce user and AI tool adopter
  • K-12 or EdTech experience is a plus, not a requirement — we'll teach you the industry if you bring the fundamentals
  • Able to travel 40–50% for client meetings, conferences, and industry events
  • The terrority for this role will be within the Eastern Time Zone.

The right person reading this already knows if they're right for it. If that's you — apply.

Compensation: $110,000 base + $125,000 target variable = $235,000 OTE. Uncapped commission plan.

Explore ourwebsite andLinkedIn to learn more about our work and impact.

Onflo is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a team that reflects the diverse communities our clients serve. All are encouraged to apply. Onflo uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility. Learn more at www.DHS.gov/E-Verify

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.excerpt: gravity9 is a boutique IT consulting company headquartered in the UK with offices in the US, Canada, and Poland.
jobs.description:
gravity9 is a boutique IT consulting company headquartered in the UK with offices in the US, Canada, and Poland. Our team has deep experience in engineering, experience design and product management. We enjoy a challenge and pride ourselves on working with our clients on their most complex problems, finding elegant and flexible solutions that help them transform their businesses.

The Role, Honestly

This isn't a job where you own one clean lane. You'll move between product owner, project manager, business analyst, tester, and support engineer — sometimes within the same hour. If you need a title to tell you what you're allowed to touch today, this isn't the right seat. If you'd rather have real ownership over a messy, high-impact problem than a narrow, well-defined one, it might be exactly right.

How This Role Breaks Down

This is directional rather than a weekly timesheet, but it reflects where the role's energy typically goes:

• 30% Product judgment & direction— customer problems, outcomes, prioritization, roadmap tradeoffs

• 30% Delivery & orchestration— backlog, dependencies, workstreams, and getting decisions to shipped software

• 25% Technical problem-solving— APIs, JSON, logs, data flows, troubleshooting, and getting to answers directly

• 15% Stakeholder leadership & communication— alignment, trust, decision-making, and effective collaboration across Poland and U.S. West Coast time zones

What You’ll Actually Do

• Run point across a multi-vendor ecosystem — several platforms, several teams, no single source of truth — and be the person who can explain how they all connect.

• Understand your users deeply enough to represent them accurately when they're not in the room.

• Own the product direction for your area - connect customer needs, business priorities, and technical realities; define the outcomes that matter; and make the tradeoffs needed to keep the roadmap focused.

• Workshop with users and stakeholders — both to turn vague frustration into a clear problem statement, and to shape new features from the ground up.

• Translate business needs into clear requirements, and stay accountable for them all the way through to a working feature — not just a written spec.

• Build and own the backlog, and work directly with developers to turn requirements into shipped software.

• Dig into raw data (JSON payloads, API responses, logs) across multiple systems yourself when you need an answer faster than waiting on someone else's ticket queue.

• Identify and own dependencies across teams and systems — know what's blocking what, and drive it, rather than waiting for someone else to surface it.

• Maintain a clear view across multiple concurrent workstreams, knowing where the important risks, decisions, dependencies, and blockers are - and be able to explain the real status without having to reconstruct it on the spot.

• Build genuine working relationships with the people you depend on — because when you don't own the system, trust is what gets things unblocked.

• Work effectively across time zones - engineering teams are primarily in Poland while client stakeholders are on the U.S. West Coast. You'll need to be deliberate about handoffs, written communication, and making the overlap hours count.

• Act as a fallback layer of technical support on the product when something breaks and the usual path isn't fast enough.

• Say no when something doesn't serve the roadmap, even when it's an easy yes to give.

You’ll Thrive Here If You

• Learn new domains fast and are comfortable operating in one before you've fully mastered it.

• Can hold a strategic view and get into implementation details in the same conversation.

• Are willing to form and share an opinion before you have complete information — and revise it in public when you're wrong.

• Treat ambiguity as the normal condition of the job, not a blocker to raise up the chain.

• Can bring calm and clarity to stakeholders even when the answer isn't obvious yet - and are comfortable saying what you know, what you don't know, and what you'll do next.

This Probably Isn’t A Fit For You If

• You want a job with a fixed scope and a quiet backlog.

• You'd rather escalate ambiguity than sit with it and make a call.

• You need full system access and a clean data model before you're willing to start solving a problem.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience in Product Management, Product Ownership, or a similar product delivery role, ideally within a consultancy, SaaS, or complex enterprise environment.

  • Proven experience owning products or major features from discovery through delivery, including requirements, prioritization, backlog management, release planning, and post-launch iteration.

  • Strong ability to translate ambiguous business and customer problems into clear product direction, requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and actionable engineering work.

  • Experience working directly with clients and senior stakeholders, including facilitating discussions, challenging assumptions, managing competing priorities, and driving decisions.

  • Demonstrated ability to partner closely with UX/design and engineering teams to shape solutions rather than simply passing requirements between teams.

  • Experience working with distributed, cross-time-zone teams. This role regularly collaborates with engineering teams in Poland and clients across U.S. time zones, including the West Coast, so flexibility and strong asynchronous communication are essential.

  • Strong understanding of Agile product development, including refinement, sprint planning, dependency management, release coordination, and iterative delivery.

  • Ability to use qualitative and quantitative data to evaluate opportunities, prioritize work, define success measures, and assess product outcomes.

  • Comfortable navigating technical conversations involving APIs, integrations, data flows, third-party systems, and complex enterprise environments.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to create clarity across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Highly organized and proactive, with the ability to identify gaps, follow through on commitments, surface risks early, and keep work moving without requiring constant direction.

  • Comfortable operating in a consulting environment where priorities can evolve quickly and where Product Managers are expected to bring structure to ambiguity and actively drive outcomes.

  • Candidates must currently reside in, or be willing to relocate at their own expense to the Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill, NC area prior to their start date.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in a consulting or client-services organization.

  • Experience with consumer-facing digital products, mobile applications, loyalty, hospitality, gaming, e-commerce, or similar customer experience platforms.

  • Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Miro/Mural, Figma, and product analytics platforms.

  • Experience using AI or automation tools as part of product discovery, analysis, requirements development, or delivery workflows.

jobs.description:
Washington Rural Healthcare Case Management, Social Work and Care Coordination Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, and community healthcare organizations throughout Washington to identify experienced leaders and professionals in case management, social work, utilization review, discharge planning, and care coordination.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming case management, social work, utilization management, discharge planning, and care coordination opportunities across Washington.

These opportunities may include positions within Critical Access Hospitals, community hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, public hospital districts, long-term care organizations, and integrated rural healthcare systems.

This Is More Than a Care Coordination Role

In rural healthcare, helping a patient safely move through the healthcare system often requires creativity, persistence, and strong community relationships.

Case management, social work, and care coordination professionals help connect patients and families with the clinical care, resources, education, and support they need. They may address barriers involving transportation, housing, insurance, behavioral health, long-term care, family support, or access to specialty services far from home.

The strongest professionals understand that a discharge plan is more than paperwork. It is a bridge between the hospital, the patient's home, local providers, community resources, and the next stage of care.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Director or Manager of Case Management
  • Case Management Supervisor
  • Hospital Case Manager
  • Social Work Director or Manager
  • Medical Social Worker
  • Care Coordination Director or Manager
  • Care Coordinator
  • Utilization Review or Utilization Management Director
  • Utilization Review Nurse
  • Discharge Planning Manager
  • Discharge Planner
  • Transitions of Care Manager
  • Population Health Manager
  • Community Health Program Manager
  • Complex Care Manager
  • Patient Navigation leadership
  • Senior case management, social work, or care coordination roles

What You May Lead or Support

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Coordinating safe and appropriate patient transitions
  • Developing discharge and follow-up care plans
  • Assessing clinical, social, financial, and community needs
  • Connecting patients and families with local and regional resources
  • Collaborating with physicians, nurses, therapists, behavioral health professionals, and community partners
  • Supporting utilization review, medical necessity, and level-of-care processes
  • Communicating with payers and supporting authorization or denial-management processes
  • Reducing avoidable readmissions and delays in care
  • Supporting patients with complex medical or social needs
  • Coordinating referrals to home health, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, hospice, behavioral health, or specialty care
  • Helping patients navigate insurance, transportation, housing, medication, and other barriers
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and documentation standards
  • Monitoring quality, outcomes, length of stay, and departmental performance
  • Leading, mentoring, and supporting case management or social work teams
  • Building stronger connections between the healthcare organization and the community

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Experience in case management, medical social work, utilization review, discharge planning, care coordination, or population health
  • Previous leadership experience for director, manager, or supervisory opportunities
  • Knowledge of healthcare delivery, payer requirements, medical necessity, and patient transitions
  • Experience working with patients and families facing complex clinical or social needs
  • Strong communication, assessment, advocacy, and problem-solving skills
  • The ability to collaborate across clinical, operational, and community teams
  • Experience with rural hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals, FQHCs, public hospital districts, long-term care, or community healthcare organizations
  • Relevant education, licensure, or certification based on the position
  • A compassionate, resourceful, and relationship-focused approach

Some opportunities may require or prefer credentials such as RN, LICSW, LSWAIC, MSW, ACM, CCM, or another case management, nursing, or social work credential. Requirements will depend on the specific position.

Why Rural Washington?

Washington's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, forests, farmland, rivers, islands, and coastlines. Distance, limited transportation, workforce shortages, and fewer local services can make care transitions especially challenging.

Working in case management, social work, or care coordination in a rural setting offers the opportunity to help patients overcome real barriers, strengthen community connections, and make care feel more coordinated and humane.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming case management, social work, utilization review, discharge planning, and care coordination opportunities that align with your experience, goals, preferred location, and availability.

Please submit your resume and let us know:

  • Which Washington communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation
  • Whether you are interested in permanent, interim, remote, or multiple types of opportunities
  • Which position or community you were viewing on RSSJobs.org

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, position, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

Work Where It Matters.

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Regulatory Affairs Director - Inflammation and Rare Disease

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. Amgen is seeking a Regulatory Affairs Director supporting products in the Inflammation and Rare Disease Therapeutic Area. Global Regulatory Affairs (GRA) provides global regulatory leadership, expertise, and execution for the development, registration, and life cycle management of all Amgen molecules.

In this vital, product-facing role you will lead the Global Regulatory Team (GRT) in the Regulatory Affairs organization. The role of the Regulatory Affairs Director is to lead GRTs within Amgen’s GRAAS organization, develop a comprehensive regulatory strategy that takes into account worldwide regulatory requirements to drive product development, global registration, achievement and maintenance of desired regional labeling, and effective regulatory agency interactions, and to provide regulatory expertise and guidance to product teams.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute the global regulatory product strategy
  • Lead GRTs
  • Represent Regulatory on the product team and other key commercialization governance bodies
  • Develop Global Regulatory Strategic Plan and provide regulatory input into the product’s Global Strategic Plan. Obtain input from the GRT members to develop a global regulatory strategy which supports product development, registration and lifecycle maintenance. Identify and communicate regulatory risks
  • Represent GRA on the product team
  • Develop registration strategies and plans aimed at achieving regulatory approval and product labeling
  • Provide regulatory direction in the development of the core data sheet to align commercial objectives in the context of available and expected scientific data, regulatory guidance and precedent
  • Lead the planning and implementation of global regulatory filings (e.g. clinical trial applications, marketing applications, label extensions, CMC changes)
  • Ensure consistency of evidence-based global product communication (e.g. regulatory submission documents)
  • Monitor and assess impact of relevant global regulations, guidance, and current regulatory environment
  • Ensure guidance on regulatory mechanisms to optimize product development (e.g. expediting FIH studies, Orphan Drug, Fast Track, conditional /accelerated approval, compassionate use and pediatric plan) is assessed and incorporated into the global regulatory strategy
  • Communicate consistently well defined, successful regulatory strategies throughout the organization such that expectation is understood
  • Ensure effective regulatory agency communications by leading core regulatory and cross functional teams (e.g. GRTs, filing teams)
  • Attend key regulatory agency meetings which could impact the global product strategy
  • Represent Amgen Regulatory on external partnership teams at the product level

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The dynamic professional we seek is a leader with these qualifications.

Basic Qualifications:

Doctorate degree and 4 years of regulatory experience in biotech or science

Or

Master’s degree and 7 years of regulatory experience in biotech or science

Or

Bachelor’s degree and 9 years of regulatory experience in biotech or science

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ability to lead and build effective teams
  • Strong communication skills - both oral and written
  • Ability to understand and communicate scientific/clinical information
  • Ability to anticipate and mitigate against future strategic issues & uncertainties
  • Ability to resolve conflicts and develop a course of action
  • Cultural awareness and sensitivity to achieve global results
  • Planning and organizing abilities
  • Able to prioritize and manage multiple activities
  • Ability to make complex decisions and solve problems
  • Ability to deal with ambiguity
  • Negotiation skills

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

jobs.description:
Statut :Régulier, temps plein

Satus : Regular, full-time

(English to follow)


Gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies

Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires, Pfizer Canada | Québec)

Objectif

Joignez-vous à une toute nouvelle fonction au cœur de l’avenir du Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires (SHPBMM) de Pfizer au Canada. Alors que nous élargissons notre gamme de produits multisources et biosimilaires, le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques prend de plus en plus d’importance, et il est essentiel d’entretenir des liens solides avec les pharmacies de détail pour améliorer l’accès des patient·e·s à nos médicaments.

En tant que titulaire de l’un des deux nouveaux postes de gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies, le ou la gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies pour l’Ontario mettra en œuvre nos priorités en matière de vente au détail au niveau des comptes, en commençant par les produits biosimilaires destinés aux soins de soutien, où c’est la décision de la pharmacie quant à la délivrance, et non la prescription seule, qui détermine quel médicament le patient ou la patiente reçoit. Vous travaillerez en complément des gestionnaires – Clients institutionnels, qui continueront de se concentrer sur les établissements, et vous relèverez de votre chef – Affaires régionales.

Le ou la gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies pour l’Ontario relève du ou de la chef – Affaires régionales pour l’Ontario

Fonctions principales

  • Établir et entretenir des relations de confiance à long terme avec les principales parties prenantes responsables de décisions et celles qui exercent une influence au sein des comptes clés de pharmacie au détail, notamment les sièges sociaux et les équipes d’achat, les propriétaires de pharmacies, les pharmacien·ne·s et les membres du personnel des pharmacies.
  • Accroître la présence et la disponibilité des produits de Pfizer dans le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques afin que les ordonnances de produits biosimilaires de Pfizer puissent se traduire par la distribution de produits de Pfizer.
  • Cibler et hiérarchiser les comptes de pharmacies de détail en fonction du volume de délivrance et des possibilités de croissance pour la gamme de produits du SHPBMM, en privilégiant dans un premier temps les produits biosimilaires destinés aux soins de soutien.
  • En collaboration avec les gestionnaires – Clients institutionnels, les autres gestionnaires – Comptes pharmacies et votre chef – Affaires régionales, élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies de compte et des plans d’affaires pour les comptes prioritaires de pharmacies de détail dans votre territoire, conformément avec la stratégie du SHPBMM au Canada et des besoins de chaque compte.
  • Acquérir une compréhension approfondie des objectifs, stratégies et priorités de chaque client·e, notamment ses pratiques en matière d’achat, de stocks, de délivrance et de substitution, et l’appliquer à la planification de comptes afin d’élaborer une analyse de rentabilité convaincante qui se traduira par un plan d’action convenu et mis en œuvre.
  • Élaborer des approches commerciales et des offres de comptes spécifiques pour ce canal qui soient compétitives et réactives, en collaboration avec les groupes Marketing, Contrats, Approvisionnement, Accès au marché, Affaires juridiques et Conformité, tout en respectant en tout temps les politiques de l’entreprise et les réglementations en vigueur.
  • Maintenir une connaissance pratique des milieux des payeurs provinciaux et privés de votre province en ce qui concerne leur incidence sur les pratiques de délivrance des pharmacies de détail et l’adoption des produits biosimilaires pour vous permettre de prendre des décisions commerciales éclairées.
  • Collaborer étroitement avec les représentant·e·s en soins de santé virtuels, le ou la chef – Services de soutien aux patient·e·s sur le terrain, les premier·ère·s partenaires stratégiques, le Marketing, le programme de soutien aux patients, et d’autres collègues sur le terrain et au siège social afin d’assurer une approche coordonnée et sans chevauchement au sein des écosystèmes communautaires, institutionnels et de vente au détail, et d’atteindre les objectifs de vente pour les produits du SHPBMM de la gamme qui lui est attribuée.
  • Recueillir et partager des informations sur les tendances du canal des produits pharmaceutiques de détail, les activités des concurrents dans le marché des produits biosimilaires multisources ainsi que les résultats en matière de ventes et de parts de marché au niveau des comptes, puis transmettre ces informations à la direction des équipes du SHPBMM, du Marketing et des marques.
  • Analyser les activités des comptes, suivre les progrès accomplis par rapport aux plans de comptes et aux objectifs du canal, et ajuster les plans d’action et l’attribution des ressources au besoin.
  • Coordonner et mettre en œuvre des programmes de formation conformes pour la clientèle des produits pharmaceutiques de détail, participer aux congrès et événements pertinents et exploiter les ressources de Pfizer au profit de segments de clientèle clés.
  • Faire des recommandations et contribuer à l’affectation des ressources de Pfizer au sein des différents comptes selon les besoins.
  • Mettre à profit différents canaux et privilégier le numérique, en démontrant une forte capacité et un déploiement efficace des technologies et des canaux numériques, afin d’améliorer l’expérience client, d’optimiser l’efficacité du personnel et de garantir un accès optimal des patient·e·s à nos médicaments.
  • Assurer une conformité complète de toutes les activités commerciales et déclarer les manifestations indésirables et les plaintes relatives aux produits, conformément aux procédures de l’entreprise.

Qualifications

  • Diplôme universitaire en administration ou en sciences, et cinq ans d’expérience au minimum dans la vente de produits pharmaceutiques.
  • Succès éprouvé dans des postes nécessitant des interactions avec la clientèle, de préférence en gestion des comptes de pharmacie de détail.
  • Compétences avérées en gestion de comptes et en vente, assorties de la capacité à cibler des occasions permettant d’atteindre les objectifs de Pfizer et de la clientèle.
  • Solide sens des affaires et capacités de gestion stratégique, avec maîtrise des outils de gestion des relations avec la clientèle et d’analyse ainsi que de Microsoft Office.
  • Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication, la présentation d’exposés, la négociation et les relations interpersonnelles.
  • Réseau établi de parties prenantes clés dans le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques, un atout.
  • Expérience dans le domaine des médicaments génériques, des produits biosimilaires et d’autres produits multisources, un atout.
  • Expérience en matière d’établissement de contrats, de tarification ou de négociation commerciale, un atout
  • Capacité à voyager fréquemment en Ontario et à détenir un permis de conduire valide

Compétences linguistiques

  • Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication orale et écrite en anglais.

Le salaire annuel de base pour ce poste varie de 107,925 $ à 179,875$.

L’échelle salariale fournie s’applique seulement au Canada, et ne s’applique à aucun autre endroit à l’extérieur du Canada.

Pharmacy Key Account Manager (PKAM)


Pfizer GH&B Canada | Quebec


Purpose

Join a brand-new capability at the heart of Pfizer GH&B Canada's future. As we evolve toward a broader multisource and biosimilars portfolio, the retail pharmacy channel is becoming increasingly important, and strong relationships with retail pharmacies are key to increasing patient access to our medications.

As one of two newly created Pharmacy Key Account Managers (PKAMs), the Ontario PKAM will turn our retail priorities into execution at the account level, starting with supportive care biosimilars, where the pharmacy's dispensing decision, not the prescription alone, determines which product the patient receives. You will complement the Institutional Key Account Managers (IKAMs), who remain focused on institutions, and report to your Regional Business Manager (RBM).

The Ontario PKAM reports to the Ontario RBM.

Core Responsibilities

  • Establish and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with key decision-makers and influencers within retail pharmacy accounts, including head office and purchasing teams, pharmacy owners, pharmacists and pharmacy staff.
  • Increase Pfizer's presence and availability in the retail pharmacy channel so that prescriptions written for Pfizer biosimilars can be translated into dispensed Pfizer product.
  • Identify and prioritize retail pharmacy accounts based on dispensing volume and growth opportunity for the GH&B portfolio, with initial focus on supportive care biosimilars.
  • In collaboration with the IKAMs, the other PKAM and your RBM, develop and execute account strategies and business plans for priority retail pharmacy accounts in your territory, aligned with GH&B Canada's strategy and the needs of each account.
  • Build a comprehensive understanding of each customer's objectives, strategies and priorities, including purchasing, inventory, dispensing and substitution practices, and apply it to account planning to create a compelling business case that leads to an agreed and executed plan of action.
  • Develop channel-specific commercial approaches and account offerings that are competitive and responsive, working with Marketing, Contracts, Supply, Access and Value, and Legal and Compliance, and always within enterprise policies and applicable regulations.
  • Maintain working knowledge of the provincial and private payer environments in your province as they affect retail pharmacy dispensing and biosimilar uptake, to support sound business decisions.
  • Collaborate closely with the Virtual Healthcare Sales Representatives, the Field Patient Support Services Manager, Senior Strategic Healthcare Partners, Marketing, the Patient Support Program, and other field and head office colleagues to ensure aligned, non-duplicative engagement across the community, institution and retail ecosystems and to achieve sales objectives for the GH&B products in the assigned portfolio.
  • Gather and share market insight on retail pharmacy channel trends, competitor activity in the multisource biosimilar market, and account-level sales and share performance, and feed it back to GH&B leadership, Marketing and Brand teams.
  • Analyze account activity, monitor progress against account plans and channel objectives, and adjust action plans and resource allocation as appropriate.
  • Coordinate and execute compliant educational programs for retail pharmacy customers, attend relevant conventions and events, and leverage Pfizer resources to benefit key customer segments.
  • Provide input into the recommendation and deployment of Pfizer resources within accounts as required.
  • Operate with a Digital First multichannel mindset, demonstrating high capability and deployment of digital technology and channels to enhance customer experience, maximize colleague efficiency and support optimal patient access to our medicines.
  • Maintain 100% compliance on all commercial activities and report adverse events and product complaints as per corporate procedures.

Qualifications

  • University degree in business administration or science with a minimum of five years of pharmaceutical sales experience.
  • Demonstrated record of success in customer-facing positions, preferably including retail pharmacy account management.
  • Proven account management and selling skills, with the ability to identify partnership opportunities that achieve both Pfizer and customer goals.
  • High level of business acumen and strategic business planning abilities, with proficiency in CRM, analytics tools and Microsoft Office.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation and interpersonal skills.
  • Established network of key stakeholders in the retail pharmacy channel is an asset.
  • Experience with generics, biosimilars or other multisource products is an asset.
  • Experience in contracting, pricing or commercial negotiation is an asset.
  • Ability to travel frequently within Ontario and maintain a valid driver's license.

Language Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $107,925 to $179,875.

The salary range provided applies to Canada only and does not apply to any other locations outside of Canada.

RightMove is redefining how value-based musculoskeletal (MSK) care is delivered. Built in partnership with the Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS)—the world leader in MSK health trusted by elite athletes—we’re creating a new standard of coordinated, expert-led care that gets people moving better and faster.

We partner with PCPs, Orthopedic specialists, and health plans to deliver high-value, patient-centered MSK care. Our value-based care model includes patient engagement, virtual physical therapy, and care navigation to high-value imaging and specialty partners.

Our Mission & Values
We’re a high-performing team driven by one mission: to free people to move and thrive. At RightMove, we move fast, collaborate deeply, and deliver with precision. We’re a startup with enterprise-grade rigor—where talented operators, engineers and clinicians challenge conventions to improve patient outcomes.

We live our values every day:

  • Perform to Win – We bring our best to deliver measurable results, valuing impact over optics.
  • BeDirect with Respect – We communicate clearly, with honesty and care.
  • Move as One Team – We win together, across roles and functions.
  • Act with Agency – Our teams have high trust and high accountability, with the freedom to own and responsibility to deliver.
  • Choose Optimism – We bring energy and perspective, even when the work is hard.

About the Role
We are looking for a Physical Therapist who will be responsible for delivering virtual musculoskeletal evaluation, triage, and care planning. This individual will assess patients, determine the appropriate level of care, initiate and progress conservative management when indicated, identify red and yellow flags, and collaborate closely with Care Coordinators and medical partners to ensure appropriate escalation when needed He or she will report to the VP of Care Delivery.

What You’ll Do

  • Virtual Triage & Care Delivery
  • Conduct virtual musculoskeletal triage and follow-up visits to assess symptoms, functional limitations, and clinical risk.
  • Apply strong clinical reasoning to determine appropriate clinical recommendations within a virtual care model.
  • Deliver evidence-based virtual physical therapy interventions focused on functional improvement and symptom management.
  • Care Planning
  • Develop individualized care plans aligned with patient goals, functional needs, and long-term outcomes.
  • Identify clinical needs requiring care coordination and route tasks to Care Coordinators
  • Partner with Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) and other clinicians when medical escalation or specialty involvement is indicated.
  • Collaboration & Continuity of Care
  • Communicate and coordinate with patients, care coordinators, APPs, and external referral sources to support continuity across the episode of care.
  • Documentation & Compliance
  • Maintain accurate, timely, and compliant clinical documentation in accordance with regulatory, payer, and organizational requirements.
  • Adhere to established clinical protocols, escalation pathways, and quality standards within a value-based care environment.

Must-Haves

  • Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) degree from a CAPTE-accredited program.
  • Active, unrestricted physical therapy license in the state(s) where care will be delivered.
  • Minimum of 3 years of clinical experience, with preference for 5 years.
  • Strong clinical reasoning skills and a patient-first approach to care.
  • Comfort practicing in a virtual environment, including remote evaluations and video-based patient education.

Preferred

  • APTA specialist certification (e.g., OCS, SCS).
  • Residence in PT Compact State
  • Experience delivering care in virtual or telehealth-based models.
  • Experience working in interdisciplinary or integrated care teams alongside medical providers.
  • Spanish language proficiency.

jobs.excerpt: Washington Rural Behavioral Health Leadership OpportunitiesRural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, community health centers, and behavioral health organizations throughout Washington to identify experienced leaders who understand the unique challenges and opportunities of serving rural communities.
jobs.description:
Washington Rural Behavioral Health Leadership Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, community health centers, and behavioral health organizations throughout Washington to identify experienced leaders who understand the unique challenges and opportunities of serving rural communities.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming behavioral health leadership opportunities across Washington.

These opportunities may include leadership within Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, community hospitals, integrated care programs, outpatient behavioral health clinics, substance-use treatment programs, crisis services, and community-based organizations.

This Is More Than a Behavioral Health Role

Behavioral health access can be especially limited in rural communities, making strong leadership essential.

Behavioral health leaders help organizations build programs that are accessible, sustainable, compassionate, and responsive to the needs of the community. They may lead mental health, substance-use, crisis response, social services, or integrated behavioral health programs while working closely with clinical, operational, and community partners.

The strongest leaders understand that behavioral health care does not exist in isolation. It is connected to primary care, emergency services, social needs, housing, transportation, workforce shortages, and the overall well-being of the community.

Rural behavioral health leadership requires creativity, collaboration, cultural awareness, and a genuine commitment to meeting people where they are.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Behavioral Health Director
  • Director of Mental Health Services
  • Behavioral Health Program Manager
  • Integrated Behavioral Health Director or Manager
  • Substance Use Disorder Program Director
  • Crisis Services Director or Manager
  • Community Behavioral Health Manager
  • Psychiatric Services Director
  • Clinical Director of Behavioral Health
  • Social Services Director
  • Counseling Services Manager
  • Care Integration or Population Health leadership
  • Behavioral Health Operations leadership

What You May Lead

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Providing strategic and operational leadership for behavioral health services
  • Developing, expanding, or strengthening mental health and substance-use programs
  • Supporting integrated behavioral health within primary care or hospital settings
  • Leading clinical and nonclinical behavioral health teams
  • Recruiting, developing, and retaining behavioral health professionals
  • Strengthening access to care in rural and underserved communities
  • Supporting crisis response, suicide prevention, and care-transition programs
  • Building relationships with schools, law enforcement, tribal partners, public agencies, and community organizations
  • Overseeing program quality, compliance, documentation, and regulatory readiness
  • Managing budgets, grants, contracts, staffing, and program performance
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and service-delivery models
  • Supporting telebehavioral health and other creative access solutions
  • Tracking outcomes and using data to improve care and program sustainability
  • Advocating for patients, families, employees, and the communities being served

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Progressive experience in behavioral health, mental health, substance-use treatment, social services, or integrated care
  • Previous leadership experience as a director, manager, clinical supervisor, program administrator, or comparable leader
  • Experience developing, managing, or improving behavioral health programs
  • Knowledge of behavioral health regulations, documentation, quality standards, and reimbursement
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams
  • Strong communication, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills
  • Experience working with rural, underserved, or high-need populations
  • Familiarity with hospitals, FQHCs, Rural Health Clinics, community behavioral health organizations, or public agencies
  • Relevant education, licensure, or certification based on the specific position
  • A compassionate, collaborative, and community-focused leadership style

Some opportunities may prefer or require licensure such as LICSW, LMHC, LMFT, SUDP, psychologist, psychiatric nurse practitioner, or another behavioral health credential. Requirements will depend on the specific role.

Why Rural Washington?

Washington's rural communities are surrounded by mountains, forests, farmland, rivers, islands, and coastlines, but distance and workforce shortages can make behavioral health services difficult to access.

Leading behavioral health in a rural setting offers the opportunity to build meaningful programs, form lasting community partnerships, and help ensure people can receive care close to home.

The impact of this work may be felt not only by patients, but also by families, schools, employers, healthcare teams, and the broader community.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming behavioral health leadership opportunities that align with your experience, goals, location preferences, and availability.

Please submit your resume and let us know:

  • Which Washington communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation
  • Whether you are interested in permanent, interim, remote, or multiple types of opportunities
  • Which position or community you were viewing on RSSJobs.org

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, program needs, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

Work Where It Matters.

At a glance:

The Senior Consultant, is someone who has 5+years of end to end NetSuite implementation experience. but also has the knack for excellent customer service. You are leading projects all the way from discovery/requirements gathering to training and deployment. You get the chance to work alongside other leaders of the organization like Managers and Solution Architects. The stakeholders will rely on you for questions regarding their project and you get the chance to do some creative solutioning. This role will also allow you to propel yourself into a Principal consultant role which is the next step to a leadership seat at the table.

Your Role:

  • Ability to lead full-cycle NetSuite implementation projects by translating complex business requirements and processes into NetSuite technical designs in a remote or in-person capacity as requested by the client, including but not limited to video or onsite interaction
  • Solution delivery responsibilities span all project phases, including: discovery, design, build, testing, training, and deployment
  • Perform fit/gap analysis on business requirements en route to system design and execution
  • Develop wireframe and schematic diagrams to support customer requirements gathering and overall business process discovery
  • Lead project management activities such as project planning, creation of work breakdown structures, and change control
  • Collaborate and work closely with in-house development team to implement custom solutions. Develop these custom solutions in a clear and comprehensive Technical Design Documents.
  • Act proactively and as a trusted client advocate during engagements by providing implementation best practices.
  • Contribute to various internal MHI initiatives including resource mentorship and ongoing NetSuite education
  • Willingness to learn and develop NetSuite product skills in all areas as required by customer engagements
  • This role may include travel, and occasional flexibility in working hours, including nights and weekends which may be necessary to meet project deadlines or address unforeseen circumstances during engagements

Your Background:

  • 3+ years of relevant consulting or industry experience
  • Hands-on Functional NetSuite ERP Implementation Experience with 5-8+ end-to-end enterprise or medium-sized NetSuite engagements - OR- has led 8+ small engagements through go-live
  • Undergraduate degree or MBA in field of Business, Finance, Accounting, Software or relevant field
  • Strong background in finance/accounting, consulting and advisory services, general services-specific industry experience
  • NetSuite certifications highly preferred – NetSuite ERP consultant, NetSuite Certified Administrator, and SuiteFoundation
  • Experience and knowledge of best practices surrounding NetSuite technical capabilities such as: SuiteFlow, SuiteScript, and SuiteTalk. Effectiveness in designing end-to-end solutions with these capabilities in mind.
  • Experience with specialized NetSuite process areas and products is preferred, these include: Advanced Manufacturing, Advanced Revenue Management, Demand Planning, Services Resource Planning, OpenAir, and SuiteCommerce Advanced

Your Interests:

  • Ability to lead certain components of projects with minimal supervision and have the ability to be “The Lead” on mid-sized engagements
  • Continuous improvement as you train to be a subject matter expert with NetSuite while working alongside peers and have significant exposure to consultants senior to you
  • Working with people in a career where you will be client facing

Why Become an MHIer

Your Life at Myers-Holum & What you Can Expect:

Do you desire collaboration? Are you ready to shape your future and positively influence change for your customers? If so, then it's time to join the MHI Team where you can own your individuality and collaborate with other curious and thought-provoking minds. Discover what you are capable of by paving your path through MHI using your expertise and discovering your true potential.

Every MHIer is committed to our mission and operating principles; We remain curious as we lead with a genuine interest in people, ideas, and the unknown. We remain humble in knowing we can change how we currently do things and it is our ability to learn and grow that makes us a success. We remain resilient in understanding that success is not linear and that through reflection and a steadfast passion for betterment, we can continue our mindful and purposeful growth.

A little about “Us”

We’ve been around for 40 years. You’ll get stability & growth with us. Myers-Holum is a technology and management consulting firm that was founded in 1981 and continues to grow year after year. Today we have over 400 remote employees sitting across ten countries; United States, Canada, Mexico, Chile, Uruguay, Philippines, Vietnam, India & Pakistan.

The Partnerships we’ve built. Our cutting-edge technology partners include Oracle NetSuite, Stripe, Google Cloud Platform, Zone Billing, Celigo, and Boomi all working with us to provide the best customer experience throughout each implementation.

Our Structure. We’re a boutique firm with a strong internal framework. Our powerful model includes robust Sales, Solution Architecture, Resourcing & Enablement, Consulting, Project Management, Managed Services & Development, and Integration departments with subject matter experts sitting in each function.

Our Employees. We’re a company that recognizes we’re only as strong as our people and each person who joins our firm contributes to our well-being. We strive to ensure all employees have a career path within Myers-Holum for both upward and lateral opportunities while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.

We’re growing and making waves along the way, join us on this journey!

Our Benefits

  • MHI offers a competitive base salary, incentive pay, and comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, retirement plan, and paid time off. Full package offerings are based on the Country in which you reside.
  • Company access to training and full coverage for certification/exam fees in a variety of products and professional skill sets
  • Career growth and upward mobility to meet your long-term career goals with mid-year and annual reviews scheduled on a recurring basis
  • MHI invests in our employee’s health by offering a company medical insurance policy that covers 100% of premiums for the individual employee with a ZERO deductible in the United States
  • Remote working opportunity when not traveling for client requirements with full access to the team through technology

Our Process:

Our interview process is efficient and provides you with an opportunity to showcase your strengths, current abilities and share your future career aspirations while learning whether Myers-Holum would be a good fit for you. You will be paired with a member of our recruiting team who will handle all of the logistics as well as provide thoughtful feedback after each touchpoint to ensure you are kept within the loop from start to finish. Our recruiting timeline can be flexible to align with your circumstances; our typical timeline can take 2-4 weeks to complete however this can be adjusted or expedited depending on your needs. You can expect the following touchpoints when interviewing with MHI

  • 30-minute call with our recruiting team
  • 60-minute video call with a MHI Team Lead, Delivery Manager, or Practice Manager
  • 90-minute interactive “Case Study” session with a Delivery Manager or Practice Manager
  • Executive leadership review and decision making

A reasonable estimated salary range for this position is $105,000 - 150,000 USD. Total compensation for this role also will include a quarterly incentive plan with the potential for an additional $5,000 to $100,000 per year. This position and compensation range is for candidates who reside in the United States. Our compensation ranges and packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate. It is not a common practice or guaranteed for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range and compensation decisions aredetermined using a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to; skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications, and specific location due to cost of living & labor considerations; All of which will be considered during the interview and offer process.Salary ranges and incentive plans will differ in other countries in which MHI pays local currency.

We are dedicated to fostering a workplace environment that upholds and promotes equal employment opportunity, free from discrimination on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status.

Provide expert remote clinical applications support for the Philips Advanced Molecular Imaging product line, combining strong clinical and product knowledge with exceptional multitasking and customer service to deliver efficient, consistent support that positively impacts customers and patients.

Advancing Analyticsarea market leader in delivering bleeding-edge analytical solutions for customers all over the world. To thrive in today's market, businesses need to ride the wave of innovation, implementing the rapidly evolving AI and ML solutions available. We are looking to you to help them build them!

On an average day working with us, you could be helping a customer implement a large language model, geared to solving complex and advanced business challenges. We’re also genuinely active in the wider data and AI community. That means speaking at events, sponsoring major industry moments like Big Data London, and showing up at some of the biggest stages in the space, including Databricks Data+AI Summit, Data+AI World Tour, and the Global AI AgentCon London.

Aside from offering a competitive salary, we have a great set of benefits and perks including, but not limited to:

Our company values define us:

❤️ Come as you are – we are an inclusive company. When you work with us, rest assured you're working in a safe environment.

⬆️ We all level up together – we have each seen the benefit that being part of a community can have, it is transformational.

💡 Transparency– We are big believers that there are no secrets in Advancing Analytics, and we try to live this day to day.

You can read about our values in more detail here -

Equal opportunities for everyone

At Advancing Analytics both diversity and inclusion are a priority. We are all committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected and empowered to be their authentic selves.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer; all applicants will be considered without regard to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity or disability status.

About On Belay Health Solutions

On Belay Health Solutions is a Massachusetts-based physician-led managed services organization (MSO) devoted to supporting independent primary care physicians. On Belay provides enhanced Medicare value-based contracts that empower physicians with the resources necessary to invest in innovative care models and population health management tools. This allows physicians to practice medicine and positively impact the health of their communities in the way they have always dreamed.

About the role

We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Data Analyst to support a critical data integration and validation initiative. In this role, you will partner with analytics teams, business stakeholders, and external vendors to map, validate, and reconcile data across source systems and data warehouse environments.

The ideal candidate has strong SQL and data warehouse expertise, experience validating data and reporting, and a passion for turning complex data into actionable business insights. Success in this role requires strong problem-solving, attention to detail, and the ability to collaborate effectively across technical and business teams.

What you'll do

Data Discovery & Data Warehouse Validation

  • Analyze and document data structures, tables, relationships, and business logic across multiple source systems and data environments.
  • Conduct a comprehensive inventory of available data assets and compare them against existing data warehouse tables and models.
  • Validate the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of data loaded into the data warehouse.
  • Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and alignment issues between source system data and warehouse data structures.
  • Create and maintain documentation related to data mappings, lineage, transformation logic, and validation results.
  • Partner with technical teams to define requirements for new tables, fields, and backend data structures needed to support reporting and analytics.
  • Escalate reporting and data inconsistencies to technical teams to ensure timely remediation and accurate reporting.

Dashboard and Reporting Validation

  • Validate front-end portal reports and dashboards against backend data sources.
  • Ensure reporting calculations, KPIs, and business rules are correctly implemented.
  • Report identified data and reporting discrepancies to the technical team for resolution.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Business Analytics, or a related field; equivalent experience considered.
  • 5+ years of experience in data analysis, business intelligence, data warehousing, or related analytical roles within enterprise data environments.
  • Advanced SQL skills with experience performing data analysis, validation, reconciliation, and source-to-target data mapping.
  • Experience working with data warehouses, reporting platforms, and enterprise data environments.
  • Knowledge of healthcare quality, utilization, cost, and population health metrics used in value-based care reporting and analytics.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with technical and business stakeholders.

Compensation

  • This is a three-month contract position (with potential to expand) requiring 40 hours per week, with an hourly rate of $46.

Come join us on the journey to better and more affordable healthcare!
