jobs.title: Senior Competitive & Market Intelligence Manager
jobs.excerpt: Senior Competitive & Market Intelligence ManagerWEKA is the AI data and memory infrastructure company transforming how organizations build, run, and scale AI.
jobs.description:
Senior Competitive & Market Intelligence Manager

WEKA is the AI data and memory infrastructure company transforming how organizations build, run, and scale AI. NeuralMesh™ combines high-performance data storage and extended GPU memory in a single software platform, providing a foundation for training, inference, and agentic AI workloads that maximizes GPU productivity, accelerates AI outcomes, and improves the economics of AI at scale.

WEKA is a pre-IPO, growth-stage company backed by world-class venture capital investors and AI infrastructure leaders. Our technology is trusted by 30% of the Fortune 50, as well as leading hyperscalers, neoclouds, AI builders, and research organizations. Our team is customer-obsessed, accountable, bold, and collaborative, with a shared focus on helping customers succeed. If we sound like your kind of people, join us!

About The Role

We are seeking a Senior Competitive & Market Intelligence Manager to build and lead the intelligence capability that helps us understand where the market is going, how competitors are evolving, where WEKA has the right to win, and what we need to do about it.

This is a technical, hands-on builder role. You will design and scale the systems, tools, operating rhythms, and feedback loops that turn fragmented competitive, customer, field, and market signals into a trusted intelligence engine for the company. You'll go deep on competitors and market dynamics, develop clear points of view, and translate what you learn into positioning, competitive deal strategies, field tools, technical briefs, training decks, product insights, and recommendations that help WEKA stay ahead in a fast-moving AI infrastructure market.

Reporting to the VP of Product Marketing, you'll work closely with Product, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Marketing, Alliances, GTM Operations, and executive leadership. You'll serve as a trusted source of intelligence across the company, helping teams understand not simply what is changing, but what it means for WEKA and what we should do next.

Who We’re Looking For

You're a senior builder. You've created or materially scaled a competitive or market intelligence capability before, and you understand everything required to make it work: sources, tools, processes, field feedback loops, operating cadence, executive communication, enablement, and measurement. You're comfortable starting with a blank page, deciding what matters, and building a system people actually trust and use.

You're intellectually curious, analytical, and technical enough to go well beyond competitor websites and marketing claims. You can dig into products, architectures, benchmarks, customer experiences, business models, and go-to-market strategies, separate signal from noise, and develop a defensible point of view about where competitors are strong, where they're vulnerable, and where the market is headed.

You also know intelligence only matters if it changes decisions and outcomes. You can turn deep research into a concise executive recommendation, a sharp competitive position, or a field tool a seller can use in a live deal. You stay close to Sales, Product, customers, and the market, and measure success by better decisions and stronger competitive performance, not the volume of research produced.

What You’ll Be Working On

  • Build the Intelligence Engine: Design and scale WEKA's competitive and market intelligence program, including sources, tooling, workflows, taxonomy, operating cadence, governance, distribution, and feedback loops. Create a trusted system of record that stays current as the market evolves.
  • Own Competitive Intelligence: Develop deep intelligence on priority competitors across products, architecture, performance, positioning, customers, partnerships, business models, and go-to-market strategy. Identify strengths, vulnerabilities, strategic moves, and likely next steps.
  • Monitor Competitive Pricing & Packaging: Track competitor pricing, packaging, licensing, consumption models, and commercial changes, and surface meaningful shifts to Product and other stakeholders to inform pricing and packaging decisions.
  • Drive Market Intelligence: Track the forces reshaping AI infrastructure, including technology shifts, market structure, customer requirements, emerging categories and competitors, cloud and neocloud dynamics, ecosystem moves, business models, and buying patterns. Translate those signals into implications and opportunities for WEKA.
  • Turn Intelligence Into Strategy: Synthesize competitive, market, customer, and field signals into clear points of view and actionable recommendations that inform company positioning, product strategy, go-to-market priorities, category strategy, and where WEKA should invest, defend, or differentiate.
  • Create Competitive Positioning & Tools: Develop and continuously improve competitive positioning, battlecards, playbooks, objection handling, comparison frameworks, executive briefs, and other tools that help Sales, Solutions Engineering, partners, and Marketing differentiate WEKA and win.
  • Build the Field Intelligence Loop: Establish scalable ways to capture what sellers, SEs, partners, prospects, and customers are seeing in the market. Partner with Sales and GTM Operations to turn competitive deal data, field feedback, and win/loss insights into intelligence that improves positioning, enablement, and strategy.
  • Support Competitive Deals: Engage directly with Sales and Solutions Engineering on strategic competitive opportunities, helping teams understand the competitor, sharpen the strategy, respond to claims, and apply what is learned back into the broader intelligence program.
  • Deliver Executive Intelligence: Establish a consistent cadence of concise, decision-oriented competitive and market briefings for Product, GTM, and executive leadership, surfacing meaningful changes, emerging threats and opportunities, and recommended actions.
  • Apply AI & Automation: Use AI, automation, and modern intelligence tools to continuously monitor market signals, accelerate research and synthesis, and deliver intelligence in the workflows where teams need it. Apply strong judgment to ensure automation increases signal rather than noise.
  • Influence Product & Marketing: Partner closely with Product and Product Marketing to bring competitive and market insights into roadmap discussions, positioning and messaging, launches, category strategy, campaigns, and thought leadership.
  • Leverage Analyst & Industry Insights: Work with Analyst Relations and other external intelligence sources to incorporate analyst research, industry perspectives, market data, and third-party validation into WEKA's view of the market and competitive landscape.
  • Measure Impact: Establish practical measures of success including intelligence adoption, field engagement, competitive win/loss trends, effectiveness of competitive plays, and demonstrated influence on product, positioning, and GTM decisions.

Qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience in competitive intelligence, market intelligence, product marketing, product strategy, management consulting, industry research, or a closely related role in enterprise technology.
  • Demonstrated experience personally building or materially scaling a competitive or market intelligence program, including the systems, tools, processes, operating cadence, and feedback loops required to make it sustainable. We are looking for someone who has built the muscle, not simply participated in an established program.
  • Strong experience conducting competitive research and analysis and translating complex findings into clear positioning, recommendations, enablement, and executive-level insights.
  • Strong technical aptitude and the ability to independently understand enterprise infrastructure architectures, product capabilities, performance claims, integrations, and technical differentiation.
  • Working knowledge of AI/ML infrastructure, accelerated computing, cloud computing, data platforms, storage and memory technologies, or adjacent enterprise infrastructure technologies.
  • Experience building field intelligence and win/loss programs, working directly with Sales, Solutions Engineering, customers, and GTM Operations to understand real-world competitive dynamics.
  • Strong primary and secondary research skills with the ability to synthesize product research, customer and field feedback, analyst research, market data, public information, and other signals into a clear point of view.
  • Exceptional written, visual, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to move from deep analysis to concise battlecards, executive briefings, presentations, and strategic recommendations.
  • Experience using AI, automation, and competitive or market intelligence tools to improve the speed, scale, and quality of intelligence programs.
  • Proven ability to influence Product, Sales, Marketing, and executive stakeholders without direct authority and turn intelligence into action.
  • Strong business judgment and an outcome-oriented mindset, with the ability to prioritize the competitors, market questions, and intelligence work most likely to influence customers, strategy, pipeline, and revenue.
  • Comfortable operating as a senior individual contributor in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with significant autonomy and evolving priorities.
  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant technical or business field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Located in North America with the ability to travel up to 25%.

How We Work: The WEKA Way

  • We are Accountable: We take full ownership, always, even when things don't go as planned. We lead with integrity, show up with responsibility and ownership, and hold ourselves and each other to the highest standards.
  • We are Brave: We question the status quo, push boundaries, and take smart risks when needed. We welcome challenges and embrace debates as opportunities for growth, turning courage into fuel for innovation.
  • We are Collaborative: True collaboration isn't only about working together. It's about lifting one another up to succeed collectively. We are team-oriented and communicate with empathy and respect. We challenge each other, resolve conflict constructively, and are transparent about our goals and the results we achieve. Together, we're unstoppable.
  • We are Customer Centric: Our customers are at the heart of everything we do. We actively listen and prioritize their success, and every decision we make is driven by how we can better serve, support, and empower them to succeed. When our customers win, we win.

Concerned you don’t meet every qualification? Don’t let it stop you from applying!

Studies have shown that traditionally underrepresented groups may be less likely to apply for jobs if they don’t meet every qualification specified. WEKA is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. If you are excited about this position but are concerned your past work experience doesn’t match up perfectly with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles at WEKA.

WEKA is an equal opportunity employer that prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We provide equal opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Ziply Fiber is a local internet service provider dedicated to elevating the connected lives of the communities we serve. We offer the fastest home internet in the nation, a refreshingly great customer experience, and affordable plans that put customers in charge.

As our state-of-the-art fiber network expands, so does our need for team members who can help us grow and realize our goals.

Our Company Values:

  • Genuinely Caring:We treat customers and colleagues like neighbors, with empathy and full attention.
  • Empowering You:We help customers choose what is best for them, and we support employees in implementing new ideas and solutions.
  • Innovation and Improvement:We constantly seek ways to improve how we serve customers and each other.
  • Earning Your Trust:We build trust through clear, honest, human communication.

Job Summary

The Principal Architect, Technology - Enterprise Security is a senior individual contributor responsible for defining and advancing the enterprise security architecture and technical standards that protect Ziply Fiber's corporate systems, employee infrastructure, and business applications, as well as the network we operate on behalf of 1M+ broadband subscribers.

This role provides architecture-level direction across corporate and network environments — including Zero Trust strategy, threat detection and response architecture, cloud and application security, and identity and access management design. Operation of the security tooling and Security Operations Center (SOC) sits with the Security Operations function, and control governance and approval sit with Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC). This separation of duties is deliberate and keeps architecture and design distinct from the operation and assessment of controls.

The successful candidate brings deep, hands-on security architecture expertise in a broadband ISP, telecommunications, or critical-infrastructure environment, and the demonstrated ability to translate business risk into technical design and to communicate security architecture to both engineering teams and executive stakeholders.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities listed below are a range of duties performed by the employee and not intended to reflect all duties performed.

Security Architecture & Zero Trust

·Define and own Ziply's enterprise security architecture: network segmentation, Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) strategy, micro-segmentation, and identity-based access-control design across corporate and network environments.

·Establish the Zero Trust reference architecture and multi-year roadmap, including policy-decision and policy-enforcement point design, device-posture and conditional-access standards, and the phased migration from perimeter-based to identity-centric access.

·Architect firewall and perimeter strategy: next-generation firewall platform selection (Palo Alto, Fortinet, or equivalent), zone and trust-boundary design, rule-governance and change standards, and policy-lifecycle design.

·Define identity and access management (IAM) architecture: MFA enforcement standards, privileged access management (PAM) design, SSO and federation patterns (SAML/OIDC), directory and service-account governance, and joiner/mover/leaver control design.

·Design secure remote-access architecture: ZTNA/SASE platform strategy, VPN-replacement roadmap, split-tunnel and posture-check standards, and endpoint-security integration.

·Establish and maintain reference architectures, design patterns, and security standards that engineering and operations teams build to, evolving them as threats and technologies change.

Network Security Architecture

·Define network security architecture for Ziply's infrastructure: out-of-band (OOB) management network design, jump-host and bastion architecture, and network-device access-control standards (TACACS+/RADIUS, role-based device access).

·Define enterprise DDoS-protection architecture, including coordination with the Subscriber Edge DDoS/Arbor program and definition of enterprise-facing scrubbing, remotely triggered black-hole (RTBH), and mitigation capabilities.

·Architect DNS security: RPZ (Response Policy Zones), DNSSEC, and DNS-over-HTTPS/TLS strategy for internal and subscriber-facing resolvers, and secure DNS/DHCP/IPAM design.

·Define network monitoring and anomaly-detection architecture: NetFlow/IPFIX analysis for security use cases, IDS/IPS placement and tuning standards, TLS-inspection strategy, and integration with the SIEM.

·Establish system-hardening baselines for network and infrastructure devices (e.g., CIS Controls, DISA STIGs, USGCB) and define secure-configuration standards for routers, switches, and firewalls.

·Define segmentation and trust-zone architecture separating corporate, subscriber, management/OT, and lab environments.

Security Operations & Threat Detection Architecture

·Define SIEM architecture in partnership with Security Operations: platform strategy or optimization, log-source onboarding standards, data-retention and normalization design, and correlation and detection-rule governance standards.

·Define detection-engineering standards, including use-case development mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, alert-tuning and false-positive-reduction practices, and detection-coverage measurement.

·Define SOC tooling architecture: SOAR platform strategy, playbook-automation standards, case-management and ticketing integration, threat-intelligence integration, and escalation-workflow design.

·Define endpoint detection and response (EDR/XDR) architecture: platform strategy, deployment and policy standards, and integration with SIEM and SOC workflows.

·Define vulnerability-management architecture: authenticated and unauthenticated scanning cadence, risk-based prioritization, remediation-SLA standards, and integration with change management and asset inventory.

·Define the architecture supporting incident response, digital forensics, and log and evidence preservation, ensuring detection and telemetry coverage across corporate and network environments.

Cloud & Application Security Architecture

·Define cloud security architecture and control standards across Ziply Fiber’s cloud environments, including AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or equivalent platforms, with emphasis on cloud-native security tooling, CSPM, secure landing-zone design, account/subscription governance, and network-topology standards.

·Define cloud identity and workload-protection architecture: least-privilege IAM, workload identity, key and secrets management (KMS/Key Vault), and CWPP, container, and Kubernetes security standards.

·Define application-security architecture standards: API security and gateway design, secrets management, certificate-lifecycle and PKI management, and secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) integration (SAST/DAST/SCA and threat modeling).

·Architect data-protection controls: data classification, encryption at rest and in transit standards, key management, tokenization and masking, and DLP architecture for sensitive subscriber and business data.

·Define infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD security standards, including policy-as-code guardrails and pre-deployment security validation.

Governance, Risk & Compliance Partnership

·Partner with GRC to translate regulatory and compliance requirements — CPNI, CALEA, FCC telecommunications security obligations, and applicable state-level requirements — into security-architecture control designs.

·Ensure architecture designs are documentable, auditable, and mapped to Ziply's compliance framework and to industry frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and CIS benchmarks.

·Define secure-by-design and architecture-review standards, including reference patterns and control requirements that projects must satisfy at design and review gates.

·Contribute security-architecture review input to the deployment-governance process owned by GRC, ensuring new network and system deployments meet architecture standards before production deployment.

·Maintain segregation of duties: design controls and standards without operating, grading, or approving them — operation sits with Security Operations and governance and approval sit with GRC.

AI & Emerging Technology Security Architecture

·Define the security architecture supporting the secure and responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and machine learning across the organization, in partnership with the enterprise AI governance program.

·Design controls addressing AI-specific risks — model integrity, training-data protection, and defenses against prompt injection, model evasion, and data-poisoning attacks — aligned to frameworks such as NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001.

·Define architecture for the secure use of generative AI and AI-enabled security tooling, including data-handling, logging, and egress controls.

·Evaluate emerging technologies — such as post-quantum cryptography readiness and IoT/OT convergence — and define forward-looking architecture standards to address them.

Other Duties

·Must be available to work regular business hours Pacific Standard Time.

·Must also be available to work on-call, evenings and weekends as needed.

·Performs other duties as required to support the business and evolving organization.

Required Qualifications:

·High school diploma or GED.

·Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a closely related field. Equivalent professional experience may be considered.

·10+ years of progressive experience across security architecture, information security engineering, network security, cloud security, identity security, application security, or related technical fields, including substantial experience defining enterprise architecture standards and influencing complex cross-functional technical decisions.

·Demonstrated senior independent contributor experience mentoring technical professionals, establishing architecture standards, and driving alignment across Security, Network Engineering, IT, Cloud, Application, and GRC stakeholders without direct people-management responsibility.

·Experience in, or supporting, broadband, telecommunications, critical infrastructure, utilities, cloud, large-scale enterprise technology, or another highly regulated and network-intensive environment.

·Deep expertise in enterprise or network security architecture, including firewall and segmentation strategy, Zero Trust design, identity-based access controls, and security controls for complex or highly available network environments.

·Strong security-operations architecture experience, including SIEM/logging architecture, detection coverage, SOAR or workflow integration, telemetry onboarding, and SOC process integration; direct day-to-day SOC operations experience is not required.

·Hands-on experience with IAM and PAM platforms: MFA, SSO, privileged access governance, and service-account management at enterprise scale.

·Cloud security architecture experience in at least one major cloud platform such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, with working knowledge of multi-cloud security patterns, CSPM, identity, workload protection, and secure landing-zone design.

·Experience designing to and implementing security frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, or CIS benchmarks.

·Familiarity with telecommunications or critical-infrastructure security obligations, such as CPNI, CALEA, FCC requirements, or comparable regulatory and compliance frameworks; ability to translate requirements into technical architecture controls.

Preferred Qualifications:

·CISSP, CISM, or comparable cybersecurity certifications.

·Experience with SASE/SSE platforms: Zscaler, Palo Alto Prisma, or equivalent.

·Background in subscriber-facing security: DNS security, RPKI/ROA, and network-level abuse management for broadband operators.

·Familiarity with OT/ICS security in the context of critical network infrastru

Job Title: Associate Medical Director, Global Safety Physician

Job Location: Remote, USA

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Description

The Global Safety Physician will be responsible for global pharmacovigilance for investigational and/or marketed products, including review and analysis of safety data, design of clinical trials, identification and investigation of safety signals, management of benefit-risk profile for assigned compounds and products. The Global Safety Physician will represent Biogen Safety in internal and external meetings. The Global Safety Physician can be appointed as the Global Safety Officer for a specific product. Responsible for keeping upper management informed of safety issues.

The Global Safety Physician will demonstrate the flexibility and capability to function at a high level across multiple disease areas and will be comfortable working in an entrepreneurial environment to advance the safety and biological understanding of compounds through their life cycle. This person will also interact with multiple levels of management within Biogen, external stakeholders in the medical community as well with global regulatory authorities.

Principal Accountabilities:

1. Manage safety surveillance for assigned products

  • Collaborate with PV scientists and other stakeholders
  • Conduct analyses of safety trial data.
  • Ensure adequacy of summarizing and handling of adverse events for investigational and/or marketed Biogen products including decisions on seriousness, expectedness, and causality.

2. Provide safety strategic leadership for clinical development programs

  • Integrate the safety scientific component to build a strategic framework for clinical development plans.

3. Develop and maintain relationships with counterparts in Clinical Development, Pre-Clinical Safety, Research, Regulatory, Clinical Operations, Clinical Pharmacology, Quantitative Sciences, Translational Sciences, Worldwide Medical.

4. Ensure the accurate and timely completion and reporting of periodic and expedited safety reports, in compliance with internal timelines and timelines set by regulatory authorities.

You are a proven leader and strive on developing, executing and advancing successful programs in development. You have experience working / leading high performing teams; providing the necessary guidance and mentoring for all to reach their goals. This position is based in Cambridge, MA (USA).

Qualifications

  • MD required; subspecialty focus in neuroscience, psychiatry, immunology, rare diseases preferred.
  • Minimum 3+ years’ experience in the pharmaceutical industry or clinical care setting; ideally 1+ years of overall experience specific to pharmacovigilance.
  • Prior experience in clinical trials; academic and/or industry.
  • Knowledge of pre- and post- marketing US and EU regulations

Job Level: Management

Base salary offered is determined through an analytical approach utilizing a combination of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills & experience, job location, and internal equity.

Your Opportunity at ARC’TERYX:

As the Senior Quality Specialist - Training, you build consistent quality capability across internal teams, vendors and factory quality personnel. You translate Arc’teryx quality standards and technical product requirements into practical learning, assessment and certification programs. A key focus is strengthening the Factory Certified Auditor (FCA) program with our quality specialists through disciplined preparation, effective facilitation, objective competency assessment and ongoing calibration.

This role can be hired remote. Business operations occur on Vietnam time zone (no relocation/visa sponsorship available for this role)

Meet Your Future Team:

You will join the Global Quality team and work closely with regional quality teams, vendors, factories and cross-functional partners. The team strengthens quality assurance and quality control systems across product development, manufacturing and final product release, while building sustainable capability within the supply base.

If you were in the Senior Quality Specialist, Training role now, here are some of the core activities you would be doing:

  • Develop and implement the Global Quality training strategy and annual capability development roadmap based on business priorities, audit findings, quality risks, recurring defects, and vendor capability gaps.
  • Serve as the lead trainer and subject matter expert for the Factory Certified Auditor (FCA) program, establishing and driving a Train-the-Trainer framework to build training capability within the Quality Specialist (QS) team.
  • Coach, qualify, and certify Quality Specialists as FCA trainers, ensuring consistent training methodology, assessment standards, certification criteria, and governance across all sourcing regions.
  • Manage the end-to-end FCA certification program, including training preparation, curriculum development, candidate readiness assessment, training delivery, auditor evaluation, certification decisions, calibration, recertification, and continuous competency development.
  • Design, develop, and deliver quality training programs for internal teams, Quality Specialists, vendors, factories, and external partners through classroom, virtual, and factory-floor learning environments.
  • Translate quality standards, SOPs, inspection criteria, and product technical specifications into practical training materials, visual learning tools, workshops, and competency assessments.
  • Assess learner competency through knowledge verification, on-the-job evaluations, and certification assessments, providing coaching and development plans where required.
  • Partner with HQ & HKO Quality Specialist teams to identify capability gaps and ensure training content remains aligned with current products, process, and quality requirements.
  • Maintain training governance, including training records, competency matrices, certification status, assessment evidence, recertification requirements, and controlled training documentation.
  • Measure training effectiveness through competency assessment results, defect reduction, first-time yield improvement, repeat finding reduction, and corrective action closure performance, using data to drive continuous improvement.
  • Continuously improve training methodologies, learning content, and certification processes through feedback, benchmarking, root cause analysis, and quality best practices.

Here are some of the things you could be working on in the future:

  • Building a scalable regional quality academy and train-the-trainer framework for internal and external quality partners.
  • Standardizing Factory Certified Auditor (FCA) qualification, calibration, recertification and governance across sourcing regions.
  • Using training and quality-performance data to identify capability risks, prioritize interventions and demonstrate measurable business impact.
  • Supporting onboarding and capability development for new vendors, new factories and new quality team members.

Are you our next Senior Quality Specialist, Training?

  • You have a tertiary qualification in textiles, garment manufacturing, apparel engineering, quality management or a related discipline.
  • You have 7+ years of experience in apparel or technical product quality, including quality assurance, quality control, or manufacturing operations.
  • You have demonstrated experience designing and delivering training to both internal employees and external vendor or factory teams.
  • You have hands-on experience with a Factory Certified Auditor or comparable auditor qualification program, including training preparation, facilitation, practical assessment, competency evaluation, certification and calibration.
  • You can convert complex technical requirements into clear, practical and audience-appropriate learning materials.
  • You have strong knowledge of technical performance products, particularly waterproof, seam sealing or taping, bonding, construction workmanship and functional testing.
  • You communicate confidently and professionally in English, with fluent spoken English and strong written English for training, reports and stakeholder communication.
  • You have excellent facilitation, presentation, coaching, influencing and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work across cultures and organizational levels.
  • You are analytical and comfortable using assessment results, defect data, and quality metrics to evaluate learning effectiveness and prioritize improvement.
  • You demonstrate integrity, objectivity, diplomacy, attention to detail and sound judgment when assessing and certifying auditor competence.
  • You are organized and disciplined in planning, document control, record retention, scheduling and follow-through.
  • You are able and willing to travel to vendors and factories throughout Asia, as required.

    • Optional:

  • Formal train-the-trainer (TTT), instructional design or adult-learning certification.
  • Experience with digital learning platforms, virtual facilitation, survey tools or learning-management systems.
  • Experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, root-cause analysis, FMEA or statistical quality tools in apparel manufacturing.
  • Additional Asian language capability relevant to the vendor base – Vietnam, China, Bangladesh, Indonesia & Sri Lanka.

jobs.excerpt: About GLAD LawThrough strategic litigation, public policy advocacy, and education, GLBTQ Legal Advocates & Defenders (GLAD Law) works in New England and nationally to create a just society free of discrimination based on gender identity and expression, HIV status, and sexual orientation.
jobs.description:
About GLAD Law

Through strategic litigation, public policy advocacy, and education, GLBTQ Legal Advocates & Defenders (GLAD Law) works in New England and nationally to create a just society free of discrimination based on gender identity and expression, HIV status, and sexual orientation.

Summary of Position

GLAD Law seeks at least one senior attorney with a minimum of 10 years of litigation experience, who has a passion for LGBTQ+ and/or HIV work as well as all related social justice issues that impact the LGBTQ+ community, including racial justice. This is a senior leadership role in the Legal Department at a crucial moment for LGBTQ+ rights and civil rights more broadly. Reporting to the Legal Director, and working in collaboration with the legal team, the Senior Staff Attorney will supervise multiple attorneys — both formally and through leading litigation teams — and will handle an active workload of litigation to advance GLAD Law's organizational priorities, including precedent-setting cases against the federal government. The Senior Staff Attorney may also assist on GLAD Law's ongoing policy work.

This position presents an opportunity for a leader to join an experienced and intergenerational legal team, to help create and lead strategies using legislation, litigation, policy, and public education to advance justice on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and HIV status, and to exemplify commitment to racial justice.

Location & Work Arrangement

This is a fully remote position, and GLAD Law welcomes applicants nationwide. The legal team is fully virtual and gathers in person one day per month. Preference may be given to candidates based on the East Coast or within commuting distance of Boston, but GLAD Law will make a nationwide arrangement work for the right candidate. Office space at the GLAD law office is available for those interested.

Compensation & Benefits

Positions include comprehensive training and competitive benefits including health insurance, 401K, and opportunities for professional growth. GLAD Law's salary ranges for attorneys are tied to years of experience since law school graduation. The salary range for an attorney with 11–19 years of experience is $145,000 to $170,000; for an attorney with 20–29 years of experience, the range is $170,000 to $200,000.

What You Bring

The below list is not a checklist. If you are passionate about our work, and meet some of these qualifications, we encourage you to apply.

  • J.D. degree and admission to practice law in at least one state in the United States.

  • Minimum of 10 years of litigation experience, including motion practice, trial practice and/or appeals, and proven ability to lead complex litigation.

  • We recognize that excellent preparation for this role comes from many paths. Candidates whose litigation experience is readily transferable including deep experience in constitutional, civil rights, or administrative law litigation, even if not focused specifically on LGBTQ+ issues are strongly encouraged to apply.

  • Demonstrated commitment to working on LGBTQ+, HIV, or related social justice issues that impact the LGBTQ+ community, including racial justice, and familiarity with the current legal landscape affecting these communities.

  • Knowledge of LGBTQ+ law and/or policy, anti-discrimination, health care, education, family, administrative, and/or constitutional law.

  • Ability to conduct complex legal research; to draft briefs, memos, and advocacy materials to the highest standard; and to present arguments clearly in court, legislative, or public settings.

  • Experience supervising, mentoring, or managing attorneys or other legal staff, including responsibility for reviewing work product and supporting professional development. This experience may include supervision exercised through leading cases or litigation teams.

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills including in the context of client interactions and client development, all aspects of litigation, lobbying or advocacy with government officials, and public persuasion.

  • Commitment to a culture of collaboration and support: being a thoughtful colleague and approaching conversations with grace and an assumption of good intentions.

  • Actively engages in continuing legal education, seeks feedback, and has shown progression in responsibility or expertise over the course of their career.

  • Experience collaborating on cross-functional projects, both internally and externally with diverse stakeholders.

  • Independence, as well as the ability to work as part of an integrated team.

What You'll Do

The Senior Staff Attorney works collaboratively with the Legal Department and other GLAD Law staff to:

  • Contribute to the legal department's decision-making strategy, help identify and assess matters for impact litigation, and lead cases in state and federal court and other disputes.

  • Lead litigation teams, including being involved in case and client development, legal research, pleadings and brief drafting, discovery and motion practice, hearings, trials, and appeals.

  • Lead and support amicus curiae efforts through brief writing and coordination.

  • Supervise several staff attorneys and delegate work to more junior staff as appropriate, including policy work.

  • Assist, as appropriate, on legislative or other policy matters that further GLAD Law's strategic priorities.

  • Provide technical expertise and support to private litigators and organizations facing complex LGBTQ issues in state and federal courts and government agencies.

  • Provide support for GLAD Law Answers, GLAD Law's legal information and referral service, including by working up legal intakes and providing individual support or legal referrals, where appropriate, to people who seek legal help.

  • Serve on internal working groups and committees as may be needed.

How to Apply

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and candidates may advance in the process at any time, early applications are encouraged. The position will remain open until filled.

Our mission is simple: End Cyber Risk. We’re looking for a Manager, Incident Reponse to be part of making this happen, based in the UK.

About the Role

The Senior Incident Response Forensic Analyst is a highly technical member of Digital Forensics and Incident Response (“DFIR”) team. The Senior Forensic Analyst is responsible for conducting forensic investigations of traditional network intrusions in Active Directory environments along with Business Email Compromises (“BEC”). The Senior Analyst assists with technical initiatives that further the business while taking opportunities to mentor junior analysts.

Primary Responsibilities and Duties

Technical Competencies

  • Conduct forensic investigations for organizations that have suffered an attack from targeted threats, such as Advanced Persistent Threats, Organized Crime, and politically motivated groups, or from commodity threats such as ransomware groups.
  • Perform host forensic analysis on Windows, Linux, and Mac OS based systems.
  • Perform network analysis using a variety of tools and log sources to include firewall logs, NetFlow, and logs generated from a variety of network intrusions detection/prevention tools.
  • Assist with/conduct the forensic acquisition and analysis from Azure, Amazon Web Services (“AWS”), and Google Cloud Platform (“GCP”) environments.
  • Leverage applicable tooling to contain and eradicate a threat actor’s presence from a client’s network when responding to live intrusion events.
  • Understand the capabilities of malicious binaries and scripts through basic static and dynamic analysis efforts.
  • Make tactical recommendations for compromised client organizations.

  • Scope new cases and lead update calls when needed.

  • Mentor junior analysts on technical and soft skills

General

  • Conduct audits and peer review of incident reports.
  • Fosters information sharing and collaboration.

  • Analysis of disparate forensic artifacts
  • Ability to draw sound conclusions despite gaps or ambiguity with evidence
  • Written and verbal communication
  • Team mentorship and knowledge sharing

Minimum Qualifications

  • Three or more years professional experience with digital forensics and incident response or other similar cybersecurity roles
  • Ability to respond to inquiries and work beyond normal business hours, as needed
  • Advanced knowledge of host-based forensic, network analysis, and data breach response
  • Advanced knowledge of current attack vectors and trends in cybersecurity
  • Ability to identify indicators of compromise (“IOC”) from newly released exploits that have little to no community documentation
  • Experience with IR and forensic tools, such as Magnet Axiom, Encase, FTK, X-Ways, SIFT, and other open-source forensic tools
  • Experience with commercial Endpoint Detection and Response (“EDR”), network monitoring, and Security Information and Event Management (“SIEM”) tools

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Information Security, Digital Forensics, Computer Science, or other related field
  • Certifications: GCFA, GCFE, ACE, EnCE, or similar training and certification
  • Prior consulting experience
  • Prior experience presenting at industry conferences and events

You are joining our growing AWS practice, focusing on North America growth across multiple industries where you have the unique opportunity to be part of driving the pre-sales motion, and being a key leader in building the delivery standards and support to effective delivery. Across clients in Fortune 1000 and Private-equity backed businesses, you work with Blend experts and Client Development leaders to be a strategic advisor to clients and shape engagements to create real business value. Internally you work across architects and engineers globally to help drive architecture standards, team support and accelerator development.

You are a passionate AWS advocate that loves data and AI — someone who lights up talking about the technology, earns instant credibility with AWS engineers and client architects alike.

Responsibilities

Platform Architecture/Approach Pre-Sales Efforts:

  • Partner with Blend Client Partners and Business Development Leaders across North America to drive sales efforts around data platform and AI Application architectures and approach, supporting proposals, workshops, and other sales activities.
  • Lead technical discovery sessions, architecture workshops, and solution demonstrations that connect client challenges to AWS-based outcomes
  • Engage directly with AWS field technical teams (SAs, Specialist SAs) to co-develop solutions and strengthen joint co-sell motions
  • Ensure smooth pre-sales to delivery handoffs, maintaining solution integrity and client confidence through the engagement lifecycle, and delivery activities where needed.

Technical Leadership and AWS Community

  • Serve as Blend’s primary AWS advocate in North America client-facing engagements, articulating the business and technical value of cloud-native, data, and AI architectures on AWS.
  • Work across regions with Blend’s architects and AI Engineers to establish best practices recommendations and help create a community around AWS to provide support to teams and ensure we stay at the cutting edge of AWS approaches.
  • Work with appropriate AWS counterparts to align on relevant upskilling and collaboration.
  • Contribute to thought leadership through case studies, blog posts, and speaking engagements at AWS and industry events

Executive Presence & GTM Alignment

  • You will regularly participate and lead leadership touchpoints within Blend and with AWS
  • Frequently lean in with client CTO and CIO’s to whiteboard solution design, and simplify and standardize to communicate complex concepts with confidence to less technical executive audiences
  • Apply creative thinking on where is there opportunity for Blend to drive more client value using AWS – translating technical capabilities into business opportunities.
  • 15+ years of experience in data or platform architectures, with at least 5 in cloud architecture, solution engineering, or technical pre-sales with a deep focus on AWS
  • Strong understanding of AI and deep usage experience.
  • Hands-on expertise across core data and AI services including compute, storage, networking, databases, analytics, ML/AI (SageMaker, Bedrock), and serverless
  • Strong understanding of real-time and batch architectures and the implications on solution design across analytical and agentic systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to work shoulder-to-shoulder with sales teams in a pre-sales or solution engineering capacity
  • Strong track record of designing and presenting AWS-based solutions to enterprise audiences at both technical and executive levels
  • Experience engaging with AWS field teams and navigating co-sell processes, partner programs, and AWS Marketplace
  • Genuine passion for AWS technology and a drive to be a credible, enthusiastic advocate for cloud transformation
  • Exceptional communication skills with fluency in both technical architecture discussions and business value storytelling
  • AWS certifications required; Solutions Architect Professional or specialty certifications (Data, ML, Security) strongly preferred
  • Experience with data engineering, generative AI, or agentic AI workloads on AWS is a strong differentiator
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree preferred

The starting pay range for this role is $260k - $275k. Actual compensation within the range will be dependent on several factors including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, certifications, training, and location. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range and determining factors for compensation are considered for each individual circumstance. BLEND360 offers a competitive benefits program designed to support the health and financial well-being of our team members and their families. Benefits vary by role and eligibility and may include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan, paid time off, paid holidays, commuter benefits, flexible spending accounts, life and disability insurance, and employee assistance programs.

Blend360 is a high-growth, AI-forward company at the forefront of data science, analytics, technology, and agentic AI solutions. We partner with leading enterprises to transform business performance by combining consulting expertise, world-class talent, and scalable technology solutions. Our mission is to fuel bold visions and deliver measurable transformation through the seamless alignment of human expertise and artificial intelligence.

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Growth & Operations
jobs.excerpt: About Care AccessCare Access is working to make the future of health better for all.
jobs.description:
About Care Access

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.

With programs like Future of Medicine, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit .

How This Role Makes a Difference

The Director, Strategic Growth & Operations for Global Study Operations serves as a central operations integration leader connecting Global Study Operations with the rest of Care Access. This role aligns priorities across functions, turns strategic goals into executable plans, and drives follow-through on the operating rhythms, process design, analytics, and cross-functional initiatives required to scale study delivery. The Director partners closely with senior leaders across departments to surface decisions, remove blockers, coordinate interdependencies, and ensure key programs move from concept through implementation.

How You'll Make An Impact

  • Lead central operations integration across Global Study Operations and partner functions, aligning priorities, owners, timelines, and handoffs across departments so key initiatives move forward without gaps.
  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leaders by shaping priorities, evaluating growth and operating-model opportunities, preparing executive-ready materials, and translating decisions into clear action plans for the organization.
  • Build and run governance for priority workstreams, including project plans, milestones, risk and issue tracking, budget and resource coordination, meeting cadence, action-item follow-through, and concise status reporting for leadership.
  • Design and improve operating processes, playbooks, and roles-and-responsibilities models; map workflows across teams; and support capability-building through tools, analytics, training materials, and implementation support.
  • Define and monitor KPIs, dashboards, and business-performance insights to measure initiative success, identify bottlenecks, recommend adjustments, and support continuous operational improvement.
  • Other Responsibilities:
    • Prepare content for leadership meetings, business reviews, decision forums, and strategic planning sessions.
    • Support cross-functional program design or relaunch efforts, including delivery, site network, and market-expansion initiatives tied to Global Study Operations.
    • Facilitate recurring operating reviews and track decisions, risks, and action items to completion across departments.
    • Contribute to system, workflow, and change-management efforts that improve visibility, accountability, and execution.

The Expertise Required

  • Strong strategic planning, PMO, and business operations leadership in complex, matrixed environments.
  • Ability to act as a central integrator across functions, ensuring alignment, follow-through, and clear decision-making on shared priorities.
  • Experience preparing executive presentations, briefing materials, and decision support for senior leaders.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills across executive leaders, operations teams, external partners, and community or government stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience with process mapping, playbook development, governance cadences, and accountability structures that improve execution.
  • Strong analytical skills, including KPI design, dashboard interpretation, and translation of findings into action plans.
  • Comfort coordinating multiple workstreams simultaneously, including budgets, timelines, resourcing, risks, and dependencies.
  • Fluency with Microsoft Suite, Business Intelligence platforms (Power BI, Tableau, etc.) and project/reporting platforms (MS Project, SmartSeets, ClickUp, Monday, Asana, etc.) required.
  • Experience in healthcare, public health, global health, provider operations, or clinical research is strongly preferred.

Certifications/Licenses, Education, and Experience

  • Minimum Education:
    • Preferred: MBA, MPH, MHA, or related advanced degree(s); PMP or similar certification; and experience with partnership development, change management, process design, market expansion, or multi-country and clinical research environments.
  • Minimum Experience:
    • 8+ years in strategy, operations, program management, business transformation, healthcare consulting, global health operations, or related leadership roles; and success leading complex cross-functional initiatives with measurable operational outcomes.
  • Licenses:
    • Valid passport and ability to travel.

How We Work Together

  • Location: Remote within the United States. This role requires 100% of work to be performed in a remote office environment.
  • Travel: This role requires up to 30% international travel requirements, further explained below. Length of travel will depend upon study requirements, staff needs, and company initiatives.
  • Physical demands associated with this position Include: The ability to use keyboards and other computer equipment.

The expected salary range for this role is $150,000 - $200,000 USD per year for full time team members.

Benefits & Perks (US Full Time Employees)

jobs.title: VP, Business Development and Earned Revenue
jobs.excerpt: Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people.
jobs.description:
Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people. For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions.

Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most.

With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact.

At Code for America, you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Our compensation and benefits are holistic and thoughtfully curated to represent our employees and our mission. Help us drive real generational change that lasts.

Code for America is looking for a talented VP of Business Development and Earned Revenue who will establish evidence-backed earned-revenue models that advance Code for America's mission and contribute to its long-term financial sustainability. Impact will include paying customers, viable delivery economics, disciplined investment decisions, and a practical path to growing the strongest offerings.

About the role:

The VP of Business Development and Earned Revenue will build and prove Code for America’s earned-revenue strategy, from identifying promising business models to testing them with paying customers and growing what works. Code for America is a nonprofit with an approximately $40 million annual budget, funded primarily through philanthropy. This leader will identify which mission-aligned offerings, buyers, and business models can strengthen that funding base, test them with paying customers, and guide decisions about where to invest and grow.

This is a hands-on executive role for someone who has built a new line of business from an uncertain starting point. Working with the CEO and across Product, Programs, Engineering, and Finance, the VP will translate ideas into focused commercial experiments, personally secure early paid engagements, and turn the strongest opportunities into repeatable offerings. Those offerings may include products, standardized services, implementation support, or a combination. As a member of the executive leadership team, the VP owns Code for America’s earned-revenue strategy, makes portfolio decisions within an agreed investment threshold, and brings larger investment decisions to the CEO and Board. The VP leads in a matrixed environment, partnering with Delivery and Enablement teams.

The Strategic Partnerships team will continue to own ongoing government partnership development within Code for America's existing strategy. The VP will collaborate with that team when testing paid government offerings. Ownership of government buyer relationships, commercial testing, and customer commitments will be defined in a shared agreement with Strategic Partnerships leadership before outreach begins.

Specific revenue and learning targets will be agreed with the CEO. Success in the first year will include:

  • A prioritized earned-revenue strategy grounded in customer discovery, mission value, and business cases with explicit assumptions.
  • A small number of paid tests that generate revenue and credible evidence about buyer demand, pricing, procurement, and delivery economics.
  • Clear recommendations – made in close partnership with the CEO – about which models deserve further investment, which need refinement, and which should stop, with a practical growth and staffing plan for the strongest opportunities.

This role will report to the CEO and is expected to travel no more than 25% of the time.

Code for America is based in California and can employ those who reside full-time within the United States. This is a remote position.

In this position you will:

  • Earned revenue strategy and opportunity selection
    • Lead the development of Code for America’s earned-revenue strategy in partnership with executive leadership, identifying the offerings, buyers, and business models most likely to generate sustainable revenue and meaningful mission impact.
    • Conduct customer and market discovery to understand buyer needs, budgets, willingness to pay, alternatives, and purchasing processes.
    • Assess opportunities with Product, Programs, Engineering, and Finance, considering Code for America's capabilities, differentiation, delivery capacity, mission value, and financial potential.
    • Develop business cases that make assumptions explicit, including pricing, acquisition and delivery costs, ongoing support needs, potential demand, and the time and investment needed to reach sustainability.
    • Prioritize a manageable set of hypotheses and decide, in close partnership with the CEO, which opportunities to test, defer, or decline. Potential buyers may include government agencies, healthcare organizations, nonprofits, and private-sector companies.
  • Paid experiments and business model validation
    • Translate promising ideas into bounded commercial experiments with a defined offering, buyer, price hypothesis, resource commitment, timeline, and criteria for continuing, changing, or stopping.
    • Personally identify and cultivate early customers, shape paid pilots or initial engagements, and negotiate commercial terms in partnership with relevant contracting and compliance staff.
    • Develop and test pricing and payment models suited to the offering and buyer. Establish whether customers will pay enough to support a viable delivery model.
    • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Programs to define pilot scope and learning goals, and confirm staffing –in coordination with department leads, Resource Management, and People Operations– technical feasibility, and delivery commitments before agreements are signed.
    • Evaluate actual customer value, willingness to pay, procurement feasibility, cost to deliver and support, and potential for repeat purchases or renewals. Identify which elements can be standardized and where customization is justified.
    • Turn results into clear recommendations to expand, refine, or stop an opportunity. Adapt direction as evidence emerges and communicate what changed, why, and what the organization should do next.
  • Repeatable offerings and commercial growth
    • Turn validated opportunities into repeatable offerings with clear buyer segments, value propositions, pricing, purchasing pathways, delivery models, and financial expectations.
    • Build a focused sales approach and pipeline for prioritized offerings. Work with MarComms and Product Marketing on positioning and lead generation, and pursue distribution or implementation partnerships where they improve adoption or economics.
    • Work with the Strategic Partnerships team on government buyers, aligning relationship ownership, commercial testing, and customer commitments.
    • Recommend the staffing and investment needed to grow proven models. Build, lead, and develop an earned-revenue team as approved, with its structure shaped by the work and evidence.
  • Investment decisions and operational readiness
    • Set revenue and learning goals with executive leadership and report progress against both. Track paid conversion, revenue, delivery costs and margins, renewal or repeat demand, and customer concentration as appropriate to each model.
    • Provide executive leadership and the Board with clear business cases, forecasts, risks, and recommendations for investment. Distinguish promising experiments from models ready for larger commitments.
    • Partner with Finance, Product, Programs, Engineering, and contracting and compliance staff to establish the invoicing, procurement, payment, security, support, and reporting arrangements needed for selected offerings.
    • Coordinate with Philanthropy to align earned revenue with Code for America's overall funding approach, including any investment needed to develop or validate offerings and a clear understanding of ongoing philanthropic support needs.
    • Represent Code for America with prospective customers, partners, and funders on earned revenue, and help define how Code for America talks about its paid offerings with government partners.
  • Other duties as assigned
    • Engage in ad hoc projects and initiatives as required by the organization's evolving needs.

About you:

This role is suited to a commercial leader who can create direction through customer discovery and testing, then build the discipline needed to grow a viable business. Experience may come from products, standardized services, implementation work, or a combination.

  • At least 12 years of experience in business development, commercial strategy, new business creation, or related work, including executive-level responsibility.
  • A demonstrated record of building a new line of business from an early stage: identifying what to sell and to whom, personally securing early paying customers, and establishing a repeatable model.
  • Experience designing and running commercial experiments, evaluating evidence, and making decisions to invest, change direction, or stop. Ability to create practical structure without requiring certainty before acting.
  • Strong financial and commercial judgment, including pricing and packaging, financial modeling, full delivery and support costs, margins, forecasts, and investment tradeoffs.
  • Experience working closely with product, technology, and program or delivery teams in a matrixed organization to shape feasible offerings and connect customer demand to organizational capabilities.
  • Hands-on customer development, sales, and contract negotiation skills, with the ability to build trust, navigate complex stakeholders and purchasing processes, and secure early agreements without an established sales team or proven offering.
  • Experience building and leading teams, coaching staff, and coordinating cross-functional work. Ability to shape staffing around validated needs and lead through influence before a dedicated team is in place.
  • Executive-level communication skills: clearly explain assumptions, results, risks, and recommendations to leadership, the Board, colleagues, and prospective customers.
  • Ability to navigate complex stakeholders and purchasing processes, and establish clear ownership and commitments across organizational boundaries.
  • A collaborative, curious leadership approach that welcomes feedback, changes course with new evidence, and values the expertise of colleagues and people closest to the problem.
  • A deep commitment to Code for America's mission of making government services work well for the people who need them most.
  • Sound judgment about which commercial opportunities fit Code for America's mission, and willingness to decline those that don't.
  • Curiosity about emerging AI tools and a commitment to using them responsibly and effectively.
  • Ability to work effectively in a remote environment and willingness to travel up to 25% of the time.

It’s a bonus if you have:

  • Experience with healthcare, managed care organizations, nonprofits, or other buyers relevant to Code for America's work.
  • Experience with government procurement or selling technology or services to government agencies.
  • Familiarity with SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, TANF, EITC, or other public benefits programs.
  • Experience developing earned-revenue models in a nonprofit or social-impact organization.
  • Experience commercializing technology or working with product teams through iterative development.

What you’ll get -

Salary:

Code for America’s salary bands are transparent as a part of our commitment to transparency and fairness. As part of our hiring practices, we aim to target the midpoint of the 2nd quartile of the range for all new hires.

Offer targets vary based on market / geographic location. The offer targets for this role range from $172,975 to $211,750,annually. Your Recruiter will discuss compensation in more detail & answer any related questions, during the initial Recruiter phone screen.

Benefits and perks:

This role includes a comprehensive benefits package including the following:

  • Values:
    • Leadership and teammates who share a strong work ethic and values, and who respect and care for one another
    • A collaborative, cross-functional, hardworking, and joyful environment
  • Employee Enablement Support:
    • Laptop provided
    • A one-time $700 payment for remote environment setup; $200 stipend (in first paycheck) and up to $500 reimbursement, in accordance with our equipment policy
    • Cell phone and/or internet reimbursement of $50 per month
  • Professional Development:
    • $500 annual (per calendar year) stipend towards professional development; prorated at time of hire
    • Up to $500 of professional development funds can be rolled over each year, up to a maximum of $1000
    • Training / guidance for staff required to utilize AI as part of their role, plus opportunities for employees to gain AI-related skills to support job and career growth
  • Retirement & 401k Plans:
    • Employees receive a 100% employer match on the first 3% of contributions.
    • Employees with 3+ years of service receive an additional 50% match on contributions between 3% and 5%, for a maximum employer contribution of 5%
  • Medical:
    • At least one no cost health insurance option for full-time employees for employee-only coverage
    • A minimum of 80% of the cost of dependent coverage
  • Remote Work:
    • Code for America employees may work remotely across the US
    • Code for America employees main residence must be within the US
    • Full-time employees work 40 hours per week, Monday - Friday
    • Collaborative working hours: we aim to hold all internal meetings between 10 AM - 3 PM PT. We expect all Code for America staff to be available during these set working hours
  • Time Off:
    • Open personal time off (subject to manager approval), a minimum of 14 paid holidays, and an org-wide closure from Christmas Day through New Year's Day
    • Paid sick time; up to 96 hours annually
    • 17 weeks of paid parental and family leave
    • 3 weeks of paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

Timeline:

From the time you are contacted by a Recruiter, you can expect a 1-2 month, or longer, hiring process. The specific hiring process and timeline goals for this role will be covered during the initial Recruiter phone screen. Code for America's standard interview process details are also available on our careers page.


Equal Employment Opportunity:

Code for America is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, citizenship status, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws.

Code for America Workers United:

This position is not covered by a Collective Bargaining Agreement between Code for America and Code for America Workers United, affiliated with OPEIU, Local 1010. The agreement was ratified on January 14, 2026, and is currently in effect.

jobs.excerpt: About Reserv Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims.
jobs.description:
About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

About the role

We are seeking highly organized and customer-focused Commercial Auto Claims Adjusters to join our team in support of rideshare-focused auto physical damage claims. In this role, you'll manage claims involving commercial auto ride share exposures including driver and third-party incidents unique to the rideshare ecosystem. You’ll interact directly with rideshare drivers and affected third parties, ensuring a smooth, empathetic, and timely resolution of claims.

This role is ideal for someone experienced in the rideshare who can balance high-volume claims with top-tier customer service. You’ll also be instrumental in helping us refine our claims processes and tools for this unique line of business by collaborating with our product and engineering teams.

Who you are

  • Highly motivated and growth-oriented. You're excited by the prospect of building a tech-driven claims org.
  • Experience in commercial auto ride share claims a plus.
  • Passionate claim professional who cares about the customer and their experience.
  • Empathetic. You exercise empathy and patience towards everyone you interact with.
  • Sense of urgency - at all times. That does not mean working at all hours.
  • Creative. You can find the right exit ramp (pun intended) for the resolution of the claim that is in the insured’s best interest.
  • Conflict-enjoyer. Conflict does not have to be adversarial, but it HAS to be conversational.
  • Curious. You have to want to know the whole story so you can make the right decisions early and action them to a prompt resolution.
  • Anti-status quo. You don’t just wish things were done differently, you action on it.
  • Communicative. (we'd love to know what this means to you)
  • And did we mention, you have a sense of humor. Claims are hard enough as it is.

What you'll do

  • Provide prompt, courteous and high-quality customer service to all policyholders and claimants by answering customer calls, filing claims, and resolving customer requests
  • Gather necessary information from customers to initiate the claim and explain policy, coverage, and appropriate course of action
  • Manage an inventory of claims, establish initial reserves for all potential exposures, and adjust as appropriate throughout the claim
  • Coordinate the repair of damaged vehicles and assist with rental reimbursement
  • Recognize recovery opportunities in regards to subrogation and salvage, as well as total loss
  • Ensure compliance with specific state regulations, policy provisions, and standard operating procedures
  • Communicate with involved parties and negotiate appropriate settlements with claimants, insureds, and attorneys within approved payment authority
  • Provide input for continuous development of claims guidelines, best practices, and process improvements
  • Oversee and direct outside investigative service providers and work closely with the client and client counsel and investigative services to resolve the claim
  • Engage in learning opportunities to build knowledge of personal lines claims, court decisions impacting the claims function, current guidelines in claims function, and policy changes and modifications

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree (lack of one should not stop you from applying if you possess all the other qualifications)
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience on point and concentrated in Ride Share APD claims adjusting, ideally with:
    • First-party comp & collision
    • Third-party property damage and bodily injury
    • Total loss and liability investigations
    • Experience with Ride Share (or TNC/Livery) is required.
  • Active adjuster license: resident-state license where available, otherwise a Designated Home State (DHS) license. Willing to obtain any additional required licenses within 60 days, including state testing.
  • Knowledge of state regulations, policy provisions, and standard operating procedures
  • Commercial experience preferred
  • Ability to analyze and evaluate complex data and make sound decisions based on established guidelines, policies, and procedures
  • Curious and motivated by problem solving and questioning the status quo
  • Desire to engage in learning opportunities and continuous professional development
  • Willingness to travel for client and claims needs

Benefits

  • Generous health-insurance package with nationwide coverage, vision, & dental
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching
  • Competitive PTO policy – we want our employees fresh, healthy, happy, and energized!
  • Generous family leave policy after 8 months of continuous work
  • Work from anywhere to facilitate your work life balance
  • Apple laptop, large second monitor, and other quality-of-life equipment you may want. Technology is something that should make your life easier, not harder!

At Reserv, we value diversity in backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences and believe that diversity in viewpoints and critical thinking drives innovation, first-principles thinking, and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage those from all walks of life to apply. If you believe you are a good fit for this role, we would love to hear from you!

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help turn PAM roadmap priorities, customer needs and technical initiatives into successful product outcomes.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at .

As a Senior Technical Program Manager for KeeperPAM, you will drive execution across product initiatives, customer-impacting issues and roadmap commitments throughout the broader Privileged Access Management portfolio. This role is focused on turning product priorities into coordinated execution. You will work closely with Product Management, Engineering, QA, Support, Solutions Engineering and customer-facing teams to manage dependencies, resolve blockers, track delivery and ensure high-priority initiatives move from planning through release. The ideal candidate is highly technical, comfortable working directly with engineers and able to bring structure, accountability and visibility to complex initiatives without owning the underlying product strategy.
