jobs.excerpt: Satus : Regular, full-time Statut :Régulier, temps plein(Version française à la suite) Pharmacy Key Account Manager (PKAM) Pfizer GH&B Canada | OntarioPurposeJoin a brand-new capability at the heart of Pfizer GH&B Canada's future.
jobs.description:
Satus : Regular, full-time

Statut :Régulier, temps plein

(Version française à la suite)

Pharmacy Key Account Manager (PKAM)


Pfizer GH&B Canada | Ontario

Purpose

Join a brand-new capability at the heart of Pfizer GH&B Canada's future. As we evolve toward a broader multisource and biosimilars portfolio, the retail pharmacy channel is becoming increasingly important, and strong relationships with retail pharmacies are key to increasing patient access to our medications.

As one of two newly created Pharmacy Key Account Managers (PKAMs), the Ontario PKAM will turn our retail priorities into execution at the account level, starting with supportive care biosimilars, where the pharmacy's dispensing decision, not the prescription alone, determines which product the patient receives. You will complement the Institutional Key Account Managers (IKAMs), who remain focused on institutions, and report to your Regional Business Manager (RBM).

The Ontario PKAM reports to the Ontario RBM.

Core Responsibilities

  • Establish and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with key decision-makers and influencers within retail pharmacy accounts, including head office and purchasing teams, pharmacy owners, pharmacists and pharmacy staff.
  • Increase Pfizer's presence and availability in the retail pharmacy channel so that prescriptions written for Pfizer biosimilars can be translated into dispensed Pfizer product.
  • Identify and prioritize retail pharmacy accounts based on dispensing volume and growth opportunity for the GH&B portfolio, with initial focus on supportive care biosimilars.
  • In collaboration with the IKAMs, the other PKAM and your RBM, develop and execute account strategies and business plans for priority retail pharmacy accounts in your territory, aligned with GH&B Canada's strategy and the needs of each account.
  • Build a comprehensive understanding of each customer's objectives, strategies and priorities, including purchasing, inventory, dispensing and substitution practices, and apply it to account planning to create a compelling business case that leads to an agreed and executed plan of action.
  • Develop channel-specific commercial approaches and account offerings that are competitive and responsive, working with Marketing, Contracts, Supply, Access and Value, and Legal and Compliance, and always within enterprise policies and applicable regulations.
  • Maintain working knowledge of the provincial and private payer environments in your province as they affect retail pharmacy dispensing and biosimilar uptake, to support sound business decisions.
  • Collaborate closely with the Virtual Healthcare Sales Representatives, the Field Patient Support Services Manager, Senior Strategic Healthcare Partners, Marketing, the Patient Support Program, and other field and head office colleagues to ensure aligned, non-duplicative engagement across the community, institution and retail ecosystems and to achieve sales objectives for the GH&B products in the assigned portfolio.
  • Gather and share market insight on retail pharmacy channel trends, competitor activity in the multisource biosimilar market, and account-level sales and share performance, and feed it back to GH&B leadership, Marketing and Brand teams.
  • Analyze account activity, monitor progress against account plans and channel objectives, and adjust action plans and resource allocation as appropriate.
  • Coordinate and execute compliant educational programs for retail pharmacy customers, attend relevant conventions and events, and leverage Pfizer resources to benefit key customer segments.
  • Provide input into the recommendation and deployment of Pfizer resources within accounts as required.
  • Operate with a Digital First multichannel mindset, demonstrating high capability and deployment of digital technology and channels to enhance customer experience, maximize colleague efficiency and support optimal patient access to our medicines.
  • Maintain 100% compliance on all commercial activities and report adverse events and product complaints as per corporate procedures.

Qualifications

  • University degree in business administration or science with a minimum of five years of pharmaceutical sales experience.
  • Demonstrated record of success in customer-facing positions, preferably including retail pharmacy account management.
  • Proven account management and selling skills, with the ability to identify partnership opportunities that achieve both Pfizer and customer goals.
  • High level of business acumen and strategic business planning abilities, with proficiency in CRM, analytics tools and Microsoft Office.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation and interpersonal skills.
  • Established network of key stakeholders in the retail pharmacy channel is an asset.
  • Experience with generics, biosimilars or other multisource products is an asset.
  • Experience in contracting, pricing or commercial negotiation is an asset.
  • Ability to travel frequently within Ontario and maintain a valid driver's license.

Language Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $107,925 to $179,875.

The salary range provided applies to Canada only and does not apply to any other locations outside of Canada.

Gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies

Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires, Pfizer Canada | Ontario

Objectif

Joignez-vous à une toute nouvelle fonction au cœur de l’avenir du Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires (SHPBMM) de Pfizer au Canada. Alors que nous élargissons notre gamme de produits multisources et biosimilaires, le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques prend de plus en plus d’importance, et il est essentiel d’entretenir des liens solides avec les pharmacies de détail pour améliorer l’accès des patient·e·s à nos médicaments.

En tant que titulaire de l’un des deux nouveaux postes de gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies, le ou la gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies pour l’Ontario mettra en œuvre nos priorités en matière de vente au détail au niveau des comptes, en commençant par les produits biosimilaires destinés aux soins de soutien, où c’est la décision de la pharmacie quant à la délivrance, et non la prescription seule, qui détermine quel médicament le patient ou la patiente reçoit. Vous travaillerez en complément des gestionnaires – Clients institutionnels, qui continueront de se concentrer sur les établissements, et vous relèverez de votre chef – Affaires régionales.

Le ou la gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies pour l’Ontario relève du ou de la chef – Affaires régionales pour l’Ontario

Fonctions principales

  • Établir et entretenir des relations de confiance à long terme avec les principales parties prenantes responsables de décisions et celles qui exercent une influence au sein des comptes clés de pharmacie au détail, notamment les sièges sociaux et les équipes d’achat, les propriétaires de pharmacies, les pharmacien·ne·s et les membres du personnel des pharmacies.
  • Accroître la présence et la disponibilité des produits de Pfizer dans le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques afin que les ordonnances de produits biosimilaires de Pfizer puissent se traduire par la distribution de produits de Pfizer.
  • Cibler et hiérarchiser les comptes de pharmacies de détail en fonction du volume de délivrance et des possibilités de croissance pour la gamme de produits du SHPBMM, en privilégiant dans un premier temps les produits biosimilaires destinés aux soins de soutien.
  • En collaboration avec les gestionnaires – Clients institutionnels, les autres gestionnaires – Comptes pharmacies et votre chef – Affaires régionales, élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies de compte et des plans d’affaires pour les comptes prioritaires de pharmacies de détail dans votre territoire, conformément avec la stratégie du SHPBMM au Canada et des besoins de chaque compte.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Associate Consultant, Regulatory Science and Strategy

Job Location: Falls Church, Virginia, United States of America

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Overview


The Regulatory Science & Strategy (RSS) team is a specialized regulatory consulting group that supports pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device companies across the product lifecycle. The RSS team helps clients navigate complex regulatory challenges, develop evidence-generation strategies, engage health authorities, and evaluate innovative approaches including real-world evidence (RWE), regulatory intelligence, AI-enabled regulatory technologies, and novel development pathways.


The Associate Consultant plays a key supporting role in the delivery of strategic regulatory engagements. Working alongside senior RSS team members, epidemiologists, and former regulators, this individual contributes to regulatory research, landscape assessments, evidence-generation planning, client deliverables, and business development support activities.


Essential Functions


Project Delivery

  • Support the execution of regulatory science and strategy consulting engagements across drugs, biologics, medical devices, diagnostics, and combination products.
  • Perform literature reviews, regulatory precedent analyses, and landscape assessments across global regulatory agencies.
  • Conduct reviews of regulatory guidance, policies, public health authority communications, and scientific publications to support client objectives.
  • Assist in the development of evidence-generation strategies involving RWE.
  • Support assessments of real-world data sources, patient registries, natural history studies, and external control strategies.
  • Contribute to regulatory intelligence deliverables that summarize evolving regulatory expectations, precedents, and emerging trends.

Analysis & Insights

  • Synthesize scientific, clinical, and regulatory information into concise, decision-oriented insights.
  • Support benchmarking activities across products, therapeutic areas, and regulatory jurisdictions.
  • Assist with policy monitoring and horizon scanning activities.
  • Analyze publicly available regulatory documents, advisory committee materials, approval packages, and guidance documents.

Client Deliverables

  • Develop high-quality PowerPoint presentations, reports, briefing materials, and strategic recommendations.
  • Support meeting preparation, note taking, action-item management, and project coordination activities.
  • Contribute to client-facing discussions and internal working sessions.
  • Ensure deliverables meet quality, scientific, and regulatory standards.

Business & Practice Support

  • Support proposal development, opportunity assessments, and thought leadership initiatives.
  • Assist with preparation of conference presentations, publications, white papers, and marketing content.
  • Contribute to internal knowledge management activities and methodology development.
  • Participate in practice-wide initiatives focused on regulatory innovation, regulatory intelligence, and AI-enabled solutions.

Qualifications


Required

  • Master’s degree or equivalent advanced degree in Regulatory Affairs or Regulatory Science, Epidemiology, Public Health, Health Outcomes Research, Pharmacy, Biomedical Sciences, Life Sciences, or a related discipline; OR
  • Bachelor’s degree with demonstrated experience in regulatory affairs, consulting, evidence generation, life sciences research, or related fields.

Preferred

  • Experience interpreting regulatory authority guidance.
  • Knowledge of clinical development, regulatory pathways, and evidence-generation principles.
  • Exposure to regulatory intelligence, real-world evidence, epidemiology, or medical writing.
  • Familiarity with emerging topics such as artificial intelligence in healthcare, rare disease development, digital twins, and external controls.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to synthesize complex scientific and regulatory information.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Ability to work effectively within cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.
  • Curiosity and willingness to learn in fast-paced, evolving scientific and regulatory environments.
  • Comfort working in ambiguity and supporting innovative client challenges.

Career Progression Expectations


At the Associate Consultant level, individuals are expected to:

  • Build foundational expertise in regulatory science and strategy.
  • Independently execute defined workstreams with limited oversight.
  • Develop client-facing consulting skills.
  • Contribute to thought leadership and knowledge development activities.

Summary

You’ll join Guidewire’s Product Strategy organization, helping make complex insurance technology easier to understand, adopt, and use. The team supports operational excellence, transformative innovation, customer-centricity, and the adoption of AI, cloud, and data capabilities across Guidewire’s products and developer experiences.

As Manager, Information Experience, you’ll lead a distributed team that creates connected, user-centered information across technical documentation, developer content, in-product guidance, tutorials, video, and other channels. You’ll shape trusted, structured, AI-ready knowledge that improves customer and developer outcomes while partnering across Product, Engineering, Design, Learning, and subject-matter teams. This is an opportunity to help Guidewire transform how the world’s property and casualty insurers do business while contributing to a culture grounded in determination, collaboration, continuous improvement, and bravery.

Job Description

What you’ll do


  • Lead, coach, and develop a distributed team of technical writers and information professionals, creating an inclusive environment where people can grow, contribute, and do meaningful work.
  • Set priorities and guide delivery across technical documentation, developer and API content, in-product assistance, UI content, tutorials, video, walkthroughs, and related information experiences.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Learning, and subject-matter experts to plan content around user needs, product goals, customer adoption, and measurable outcomes.
  • Champion persona- and task-based information experiences for business and technical audiences, helping users understand, implement, and realize value from Guidewire products.
  • Guide the evolution of content into trusted, structured, reusable, and AI-ready knowledge through information architecture, content models, metadata, taxonomies, governance, and content reuse.
  • Promote practical and responsible use of AI in content planning, creation, review, evaluation, and maintenance, with appropriate human oversight and attention to quality.
  • Use analytics, search and assistant insights, user feedback, and research to evaluate effectiveness, improve findability and retrieval, and prioritize enhancements.
  • Improve authoring, review, publishing, and maintenance workflows; lead cross-functional initiatives, manage competing priorities, and remain hands-on when needed.

At Guidewire, we foster a culture of curiosity, innovation, and responsible use of AI—empowering our teams to continuously leverage emerging technologies and data-driven insights to enhance productivity and outcomes.


What you’ll bring

Required

  • Seven or more years of experience in technical writing, information development, content design, or content strategy for enterprise software or SaaS, including at least three years managing teams.
  • Strong people leadership, coaching, feedback, and team-development skills.
  • Ability to think critically about user journeys and create holistic information experiences across multiple formats and channels.
  • Experience with information architecture, structured or modular content, content strategy, metadata, reuse, taxonomy, or governance.
  • Strong technical aptitude and the ability to learn cloud platforms, APIs, developer workflows, and software technologies quickly.
  • Experience using analytics, user feedback, research, search data, or other evidence to improve content and user outcomes.
  • Familiarity with generative AI concepts such as prompting, retrieval, grounding, evaluation, and human oversight.
  • Demonstrated ability to embrace AI and apply it to your current role as well as data-driven insights to drive innovation, productivity, and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to prioritize, lead change, navigate ambiguity, and work effectively across distributed, cross-functional teams.
  • Excellent communication, leadership, project-management, and organizational skills.

Preferred

  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical, communications, or related field preferred, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Background in developer documentation for data and analytics solutions.
  • Experience supporting search, conversational assistants, retrieval-augmented generation systems, or other AI-enabled information experiences.
  • Proficiency with DITA, Markdown, Git or GitHub, OpenAPI or Swagger, static site generators, docs-as-code, and continuous integration and delivery workflows.
  • Knowledge of automated quality checks, taxonomies, and large structured content sets.
  • Experience with UX writing, accessibility, localization, video, diagrams, or interactive walkthroughs.

Your Impact

We believe in clarity and setting you up for success. During your first six months, you’ll build relationships across Product, Engineering, Design, Learning, and subject-matter teams; understand the needs of key user personas; assess current content, workflows, and measurement practices; and establish priorities for improving the information experience. You’ll define practical measures for findability, content quality, reuse, user satisfaction, search and assistant effectiveness, and delivery efficiency, then use those insights to guide improvements and demonstrate progress. Your work will help customers and developers adopt Guidewire’s cloud, data, and AI capabilities, support product growth and customer success, and influence how trusted knowledge is created and used across the company.

What’s in it for you

The people we employ give their all, and in return, we offer flexibility wherever we can, such as:

  • Flexible work environment
  • Health and wellness benefits
  • Paid time off programs, including volunteer time off
  • Market-competitive pay and incentive programs
  • Continual development and internal career growth opportunities


Guidewire is committed to customer success and combines digital, core, analytics, and AI to deliver its platform as a cloud service. In this role, you’ll contribute to that wider mission by helping insurers modernize and thrive through clearer, more accessible, and more effective product experiences.

Guidewire embraces a culture of in-person interviews for all applicants and onsite orientation for all new hires. We welcome candidates who bring different perspectives and experiences and evaluate qualifications based on the requirements of the role.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $123,000 - $218,000. Your base pay will depend on your experience, skills, education, training, and location among other factors. All full-time positions or part-time roles working 30 hours or more a week at Guidewire are eligible for benefits that support their health and well-being including health, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, and a company sponsored retirement plan. In addition, some roles may be eligible for the annual company bonus plan, commissions, and/or long term incentive awards which are contingent on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, company and employee performance.

About Guidewire


Guidewire is the platform P&C insurers trust to engage, innovate, and grow efficiently. We combine digital, core, analytics, and AI to deliver our platform as a cloud service. More than 540+ insurers in 40 countries, from new ventures to the largest and most complex in the world, run on Guidewire.

jobs.excerpt: Customer Facing Title: Director of School Operations Job Overview The Director of School Operations (DSO) is a senior, enterprise-level leadership role responsible for operational excellence across a portfolio of Connections Academy schools.
jobs.description:
Customer Facing Title: Director of School Operations

Job Overview

The Director of School Operations (DSO) is a senior, enterprise-level leadership role responsible for operational excellence across a portfolio of Connections Academy schools. The DSO focuses on strengthening the effectiveness of school leaders and leadership teams through hands‑on partnership, coaching, and operational problem‑solving. This role directly manages the primary school leader and at each school will work directly with principals, directors, and school leadership teams to ensure schools are operationally strong, well‑supported, and positioned to serve students successfully.

The DSO uses a multi-layer leadership model to ensure alignment and execution of school operations to PVS standards and values. This is accomplished by supporting operational systems, compliance structures, and leadership accountability through school-based leadership teams. The scope of this role is inherently complex and high-impact, requiring a majority of time spent working directly with schools, the ability to lead leaders, operate at scale, and balance competing priorities across multiple schools and PVS simultaneously.

The DSO works in a number of cross-functional teams identified as key members to accomplish school goals. This includes close partnership with the School Success Partner (SSP), who holds overall accountability for school/account success and continuity of operations. In addition, they provide critical support to operationalize and hold leaders accountable for academic improvement strategies identified by the Academic Outcomes Teams.

Role Purpose

  • Lead operational execution across multiple schools and leadership teams.

  • Ensure compliance with regulations and contract requirements, operational efficiency, and sustainability at scale.

  • Strengthen school leader effectiveness, stability, and succession

  • Enable enrollment growth through operational readiness while maintaining a focus on student experience and success.

  • Partner with SSP to translate account strategy into disciplined, scalable execution

  • Support academic improvement by holding school leaders accountable to initiatives established by the Academic Outcomes team who holds academic accountability.

  • Ensure Connections Academy model is implemented with fidelity and overall alignment to Pearson values.

Core Responsibilities

  1. Portfolio-Level School Operations Leadership

  • Directly manage and coach multiple school leaders across a portfolio of schools.

  • Indirectly support and influence entire leadership teams and school staff through strong systems, expectations, and execution discipline.

  • Establish consistent operational expectations across schools while allowing for local nuances where required.

  • Hold school leaders accountable for execution of:

  • Academic action plans and initiatives

  • Compliance and charter/SOA requirements

  • School year cycle milestones and operational deliverables

  • Monitor operational health, engagement trends, and compliance indicators across schools to identify risks and required interventions.

  • Provide structured, data-informed coaching to leaders to improve execution at scale.

2. Operational Sustainability & Enrollment Enablement

  • Work closely with schools to ensure they are operationally prepared to support enrollment growth.

  • Validate leadership capacity, staffing structures, onboarding processes, scheduling, and systems readiness at each school.

  • Identify school operational constraints that could limit growth, persistence, or staff sustainability.

  • Strengthen retention-supporting school practices that indirectly impact student and staff experience.

  • Identify risks to charter stability and renewal readiness and work across PVS departments to mitigate risks.

3. School Year Cycle & Operational Readiness at Scale

  • Ensure consistent execution of school year cycle activities across multiple schools, including:

  • Calendar and handbook alignment

  • Annual policy and process reviews

  • Summer school planning

  • Identify strain points affecting leaders and staff and coordinate mitigations across the portfolio of schools.

4. Leadership Management & Capacity Building

  • Serve as a leader of leaders, managing school principals responsible for large, complex organizations.

  • Establish clear performance expectations tied to operational excellence, compliance, and execution of strategic (academic, financial, etc.) initiatives.

  • Conduct performance evaluations and manage development plans for school leaders.

  • Lead hiring and onboarding of school leaders.

  • Drive succession planning to ensure leadership stability across schools.

  • Facilitate leadership development that cascades through leadership teams and school staff.

5. Board, Authorizer & External Partner Support

  • Establish and maintain working relationships with boards, authorizers, districts, and other key partners as a key account team member, supporting the school leader and SSP by reinforcing trust, continuity, and effective communication—without assuming primary ownership of those stakeholder relationships.

  • Support school leaders in effectively engaging with boards, authorizers, districts, and other key partners.

  • Partner with school leaders to prepare for board, authorizer, and key partner meetings by supporting agenda development, data review, school performance narratives, and follow‑up actions.

  • As the School Leader’s manager, support and contribute to the delivery of formal performance reviews of the school leader to the board, ensuring reviews are evidence‑based, clearly articulated, and aligned to agreed‑upon goals and governance expectations.

6. Change Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Support operational change across multiple schools and leadership teams as PVS launches new products and services.

  • Ensure adoption of enterprise systems, processes, and initiatives while working to minimize disruption to all stakeholders.

  • Contribute to continuous refinement of the School Operations operating model.

Key Competencies

  • Ability to lead leaders across multiple organizations

  • Enterprise-scale operational judgment

  • Cross-functional influence and alignment

  • Capacity planning and sustainability thinking

  • Accountability-driven coaching

  • Risk identification and mitigation

  • Executive communication and partnership

Success Indicators

  • Multiple schools operate compliantly and sustainably year over year

  • School leaders demonstrate strong execution discipline and stability

  • Leadership teams and staff experience improved clarity, consistency, and predictability

  • Enrollment growth is supported by strong operational readiness

  • Operational risks are identified and mitigated before impacting continuity

  • SSP and DSO partnership results in aligned, scalable account success

Requirements

  • 3-5 years proven leadership experience as a Principal or equivalent level required

  • Advanced degree in Education or Management is required

  • Virtual school leadership required

  • Flexible

  • Innovative

  • Comfortable with technology

  • Strong communications skills

  • Data-driven and results-focused

  • Ability to travel frequently

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by factors including skill set, experience, and location.

The full-time salary range for this role is $130,000 - $140,000

.

This position is eligible for Pearson’s annual incentive program. Information on benefits can be found here.

Applications will be accepted through 11/13/26. This window may be extended depending on business needs.

jobs.title: Senior Research Manager for Sponsored Research
jobs.excerpt: For over 35 years, Youth Villages has transformed the lives of children and families nationwide through innovative, research-based programs focused on preserving and restoring families.
jobs.description:
For over 35 years, Youth Villages has transformed the lives of children and families nationwide through innovative, research-based programs focused on preserving and restoring families.

As a national leader in children’s mental and behavioral health, we serve more than 47,000 youth, young people, and their families annually across 29 states and Washington, D.C. Our proven treatment models drive long-term success in child welfare, juvenile justice, and mental health systems. At Youth Villages, we do what works — partnering with others to expand our impact and advocate for meaningful, lasting change.

We're seeking purpose-driven individuals who are passionate about making a difference. With a dedicated team of more than 5,000 staff, Youth Villages is committed to investing in and supporting our employees by offering opportunities to build a fulfilling career through professional growth, personal development, and a mission that matters— helping children and families live successfully.

For more information, please visit

Program Overview:

Youth Villages is seeking a strategic, highly organized Senior Research Manager for Sponsored Research to lead complex research and evidence-building initiatives that support program improvement, service expansion, and child welfare system change. Reporting to the Director of Research, the person in this role will provide scientific and project leadership across multi-partner research initiatives, working with Youth Villages teams, external research partners, and state and local child welfare agencies. This role will help ensure that research and administrative data are used to answer meaningful strategic questions, inform decisions, and strengthen the use of evidence across Youth Villages and its public-sector partnerships. The Senior Research Manager for Sponsored Research will have primary responsibility for coordinating Map2Impact, a multi-state partnership with the Center for State Child Welfare Data at Chapin Hall, while also supporting connections between this work and Youth Villages’ broader research, evaluation, implementation, and scaling priorities.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities:


I. Provide Strategic and Scientific Leadership

  • Develop and manage learning agendas for sponsored research projects; identify priority questions, analyses, evidence needs, and major milestones in collaboration with internal and external partners.
  • Ensure initiatives in their portfolio are designed to inform specific strategic, programmatic, policy, or practice decisions.
  • Provide scientific guidance on research questions, analytic approaches, interpretation, and appropriate use of findings.
  • Critically evaluate analytic methods, assumptions, findings, and limitations and facilitate resolution of methodological questions with research partners.
  • Review reports, dashboards, visualizations, and other products to strengthen their clarity, usability, and relevance for decision-makers.
  • Identify emerging evidence needs and opportunities to refine, expand, or standardize analytic approaches.
  • Provide research partners with relevant context about Youth Villages services, implementation, organizational priorities, and the policy and practice environments in which programs operate.

II. Support Evidence Use and Public-System Partnerships

  • Work with Youth Villages teams and state and local partners to identify strategic questions that research and administrative data can help address.
  • Facilitate interpretation of findings, incorporating relevant policy, practice, service, implementation, and jurisdictional context.
  • Maintain a clear understanding of partner priorities, available evidence, key findings, decisions informed by the evidence, open questions, and next steps.
  • Support data-sharing processes and help address organizational or relationship barriers that affect research partnerships.
  • Support onboarding and engagement of new jurisdiction partners and opportunities to expand evidence-building initiatives.
  • Facilitate cross-jurisdiction learning, including communities of practice and other opportunities to share findings, approaches, and lessons learned.
  • Coordinate dissemination of findings through presentations, reports, publications, conferences, and other forums in collaboration with Communications and other teams as appropriate.

III. Lead Complex Sponsored Research Partnerships and Projects

  • Coordinate work across Youth Villages teams, external researchers, public-system partners, and other collaborators.
  • Manage project plans, timelines, deliverables, dependencies, decisions, and communications across multiple workstreams and jurisdictions.
  • Maintain shared project-management systems that provide visibility into priorities, responsibilities, decisions, deliverables, barriers, and next steps.
  • Ensure partners receive timely feedback, decisions, contextual information, and access to appropriate Youth Villages staff and external stakeholders.
  • Maintain continuity of decisions and commitments across teams, meetings, and workstreams.
  • Proactively identify competing priorities, barriers, and delays and assess implications for commitments, staffing, budgets, and timelines.
  • Lead regular partnership check-ins and contribute to assessment of partnership effectiveness and progress toward shared goals.

IV. Strengthen Organizational Capacity to Use Evidence

  • Develop learning opportunities, facilitation, coaching, tools, and resources that strengthen the ability of Youth Villages staff and partners to use evidence systematically in decision-making.
  • Help teams distinguish observations from hypotheses, identify potential drivers of outcomes, select strategies responsive to those drivers, and define measurable expected results.
  • Support use of the EDGE (Evidence-Driven Growth & Excellence) framework and other structured approaches to evidence-informed decision-making where appropriate.
  • Help teams interpret evidence, formulate testable explanations, select appropriate responses, and assess whether strategies are producing expected results.
  • Integrate evidence-use practices into communities of practice and other opportunities for shared learning and continuous improvement.

V. Connect Evidence Across Organizational Priorities

  • Build connections across research, evaluation, implementation, scaling, and system-change initiatives so that relevant evidence is shared and used across portfolios.
  • Work closely with colleagues responsible for Intercept and other program scaling and evaluation efforts to identify where administrative data and other research findings can inform expansion, implementation, practice, and policy.
  • Coordinate research questions, timelines, evidence products, interpretation, and dissemination when initiatives intersect.
  • Identify opportunities to synthesize findings across projects to inform broader organizational strategy and learning.

Qualifications:

  • Doctorate in psychology, public policy, public administration, social work, epidemiology, or a related social or behavioral science field is required, with 5+ years of related experience.
  • Strong expertise in quantitative research methods, study design, statistical analysis, and interpretation of complex observational data required.
  • Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate research questions, analytic approaches, and the strength and limitations of evidence required.
  • Experience working with large administrative or longitudinal datasets preferred.
  • Understanding of implementation science, applied research methods, program evaluation, and/or continuous improvement required.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex, multi-partner initiatives involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities required.
  • Excellent project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously required.
  • Ability to build productive relationships with researchers, organizational leaders, practitioners, and government or public-system partners required.
  • Experience teaching, training, mentoring, or facilitating learning for adult audiences preferred.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills, including the ability to translate complex quantitative findings for non-technical audiences required.
  • Experience working with child welfare or other public human-services systems strongly preferred.

Work Environment

Work must be performed from a secure, private home office workplace with a reliable high-speed internet connection. Environment should have moderate noise level consistent with a standard home office


Physical Demands

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary seated position for an extended period
  • Frequent and continuous use of hands, wrists, and fingers to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other standard office equipment
  • Continuous near vision required for reading computer screens and documents. Constant ability to hear and speak clearly during meetings (including virtual meetings) and phone calls
  • Occasional moving about workspace
  • Occasional lifting or carrying of light office supplies, files, or laptop equipment, typically weighing less than 15 pounds

Youth Villages Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Prescription Drug Coverage and Vision

  • 401(k)

  • Time off:

    • 2 week paid vacation (full-time) / 1 week paid vacation (part-time)

    • 12 paid sick days per year

    • 11 paid holidays

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • Mileage & Cell Phone Reimbursement (when applicable)

  • Tuition reimbursement and licensure supervision

  • Growth & development through continuous training

  • Clinical and administrative advancement opportunities

*Benefits are excluded for variable status employees.

Youth Villages is an equal opportunity employer and provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Youth Villages is committed to not only advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace but also in our work with children and young adults. We know that children, families and young people of color can face inequity in child welfare and justice systems, and we train our employees to build the skills they need to work with the communities that we serve, as well as, other employees from different cultures and backgrounds. Youth Villages is opposed to racism in any of its forms and is committed to inclusion, equity, and diversity. We believe that respect for each other is crucial in the work that we do each day.

jobs.description:
VIDIZMO is looking for a Sales Development Representative to help us build new pipeline across the United States. If you have 1 to 3 years of outbound sales experience, communicate in English with clarity and confidence, and enjoy starting conversations with new prospects every day, we'd like to meet you. You'll generate new business by engaging end customers directly and by working alongside our channel partners. You'll book meetings with the right decision-makers, validate that there is a genuine need, and hand well-qualified opportunities to our account team, using AI tools to speed up your research, preparation and follow-up.

About VIDIZMO
VIDIZMO is an AI software company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Tysons, Virginia. Our four products, Nexus, AI Intelligence Hub, AI Live Insight, and Redactor, help organizations store, search, analyze, redact and share every type of unstructured data, from video and audio to images, documents and text, treating each format as equally important.

More than 100 organizations run VIDIZMO in production across public safety and justice, government, healthcare, financial services, education, legal, manufacturing and energy. Many deploy it on-premises, in air-gapped networks, or in FedRAMP High environments, and our architecture aligns with the CJIS Security Policy.

We go to market directly and through channel partners worldwide, so this team works with both end customers and partners every day. VIDIZMO holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, is a Microsoft Solutions Partner for Data & AI, and is an NVIDIA Inception partner. Customers can buy through GSA, Carahsoft, and state and cooperative contract vehicles.

AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot are part of our daily work, and we expect you to use them effectively. You are accountable for checking anything AI helps you produce for accuracy, completeness and compliance, and you own the final output.

What You'll Do

  • Engage end customers and partners every day by phone and message, working through a prioritized call list.
  • Dedicate at least two hours each day to live conversations with new prospects and partners.
  • Book meetings with key decision-makers and confirm there is a genuine need.
  • Turn qualified interest into opportunities and hand them to the account team with a clear summary.
  • Register partner opportunities the same day you identify them, and onboard a new partner when a deal calls for one.
  • Log every call, email and meeting in HubSpot on the day it takes place.
  • Use Claude or a comparable AI assistant every day to research prospects, prepare for calls, draft outreach and follow up.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field.
  • Clear, confident spoken and written English that US buyers can easily follow on calls.
  • 1 to 3 years of experience in outbound business development, sales development, lead generation or inside sales, or strong evidence that you can do the job.
  • Comfort with high call volumes and with hearing "no."
  • Hands-on experience with HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Apollo or similar tools.
  • A habit of logging every call and meeting the same day.
  • A track record of using AI to automate your own routine work, such as reusable prompts, Claude Projects, AI-assisted workflows or simple scripts. Please share an example of something you've automated.
  • Experience selling a SaaS product or service to US buyers, including outbound cold calling, is strongly preferred.
  • Able to make this a full-time commitment, without concurrent freelance work or outside business ventures.
  • Current US residence and authorization to work in the United States without visa sponsorship.

What Sets You Apart
A "no" doesn't slow you down; you pick up the next call with the same energy. You listen carefully, can tell genuine interest from politeness, and keep your pipeline and CRM consistently organized. You use AI to prepare faster and follow up without dropping anything, and you take ownership of your results without needing close supervision.

jobs.description:
Technical Recruiter

Location: Mt. View, CA / Hybrid / Remote

About Unconventional AI

Unconventional AI is rethinking the very foundations of computing to optimize energy efficiency for the AI era. Founded by experts across AI systems, analog circuits, computing theory, and neuroscience, we are building a completely new compute substrate for artificial intelligence. By designing hardware specifically for probabilistic AI workloads, we are bringing biology-scale efficiency to AI—without the biological baggage.

Backed by top-tier investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Jeff Bezos, we are a fast-growing, exceptionally well-capitalized team on a mission to break free from traditional GPU constraints and power the future of AGI.

About the Role

We are looking for an exceptional Technical Recruiter to join our Talent team. Because we are building an entirely new paradigm of AI hardware—combining neuromorphic engineering, analog circuitry, and advanced software—the talent we need is rare, multidisciplinary, and highly sought-after.

As a Technical Recruiter at Unconventional AI, you will partner directly with our founders and engineering leaders to design sourcing strategies, attract world-class talent, and close exceptional candidates. This isn't a standard software recruiting role; you will be mapping entirely new talent pools across deep tech, hardware architecture, AI research, and neuroscience. You will act as a strategic advisor, helping to build the recruiting engine from the ground up while maintaining an uncompromisingly high talent bar.

In this role, you will:

  • Own Full-Cycle Recruiting: Manage the end-to-end hiring process for highly specialized technical roles (e.g., Analog Circuit Design, AI Infrastructure, Machine Learning Research, and Systems Engineering), from initial scoping to offer negotiation and closing.
  • Partner with Leadership: Work closely with technical leaders to deeply understand hiring needs, define role requirements, and translate business priorities into actionable talent plans.
  • Build Pipeline: Design and execute creative, proactive sourcing strategies to identify and engage top-tier passive candidates in highly competitive and niche technical markets.
  • Elevate the Candidate Experience: Ensure every interaction reflects Unconventional AI's bold mission and values, providing a high-touch, seamless journey from outreach to onboarding.
  • Architect Recruiting Operations: Help build and refine our internal hiring processes, interview loops, and ATS workflows to scale efficiently without sacrificing quality.
  • Evangelize our Mission: Serve as a brand ambassador, representing Unconventional AI within the academic, scientific, and deep-tech communities to attract pioneers who want to build the next generation of computing.

You might be a good fit if you have:

  • 5+ years of technical recruiting experience, ideally within a high-growth startup, frontier AI lab, or specialized deep-tech/hardware environment.
  • A proven track record of sourcing and closing exceptional talent in complex technical domains (e.g., AI/ML research, semiconductors, embedded systems, or high-performance computing).
  • Deep technical curiosity. You don’t just match keywords; you have a genuine interest in understanding novel computing architectures, hardware-software co-design, and the future of AI.
  • Strategic advisory skills. You are comfortable challenging assumptions, utilizing market data to influence hiring decisions, and guiding senior stakeholders through ambiguity.
  • A builder’s mindset. You thrive in fast-paced, dynamic startup environments where you are expected to operate with high agency, autonomy, and a sense of urgency.
  • Exceptional communication skills. You can authentically and compellingly articulate a highly technical, visionary company mission to top-tier candidates.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience hiring talent at the intersection of hardware and software (e.g., AI accelerators, neuromorphic computing, or advanced silicon).
  • Experience with academic recruitment and deep ties to top-tier research communities.

Logistics & Benefits

  • Compensation: Highly competitive base salary, generous early-stage equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Healthcare: Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents.
  • Time Off: Flexible PTO to ensure you stay rested and energized.
  • Culture: A collaborative, intellectually rigorous, and mission-driven environment in our San Francisco headquarters.

Unconventional AI is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

Vollzeit | Remote möglich | 4.000–4.700 Euro brutto pro Monat

Wir unterstützen mittelständische Unternehmen im deutschsprachigen Raum bei der Prozessautomatisierung und beim Einsatz von KI.   • Du klärst Rückfragen mit Kunden und dem Entwicklungsteam und hältst die Dokumentation aktuell.

  • Du prüfst umgesetzte Funktionen anhand der vereinbarten Anforderungen und unterstützt bei Kundenterminen und Abnahmen.

  • Du übernimmst eigene Themenbereiche und baust deine Verantwortung mit zunehmender Erfahrung aus.

Requirements

Das bringst du mit

  • Du kannst dich in neue Abläufe einarbeiten und erkennst, wenn Informationen fehlen oder nicht zusammenpassen.

  • Du hörst aufmerksam zu, fragst konkret nach und kannst Ergebnisse verständlich auf Deutsch formulieren.

  • Du interessierst dich für Software, Automatisierung und KI und möchtest verstehen, wie diese im Arbeitsalltag eingesetzt werden.

  • Du arbeitest sorgfältig und behältst Vereinbarungen und offene Aufgaben im Blick.

Programmieren gehört nicht zu deinen Kernaufgaben. Technische Detailfragen klärst du gemeinsam mit unseren Entwicklern. Für den Einstieg ist uns wichtiger, wie du denkst und kommunizierst, als wie viele Werkzeuge du bereits kennst.

Das erwartet dich

  • 4.000–4.700 Euro brutto pro Monat in Vollzeit.

The Airframe Design Engineering organization is seeking a highly motivated individual with an engineering degree and related experience to fill the role of Airframe Design Engineer in the area of airframe design. Keystone Financial Group is growing, and we are looking for an Associate Managing Director (AMD) to join our leadership team. This is a highly visible leadership opportunity for someone who is passionate about attracting experienced financial advisors, developing and coaching talent, and helping advisors build stronger, more successful businesses. Working alongside the Managing Director, the AMD will play an important role in driving the growth of the firm, strengthening advisor engagement and retention, and helping position Prudential Wealth Advisors as a destination for experienced advisor talent.


The Associate Managing Director(AMD) serves as a strategic partner to the Managing Director and is responsible for driving advisor growth, development, and retention within the firm. As a key member of the leadership team, the AMD plays a pivotal role in attracting experienced financial advisors, supporting successful advisor transitions, and helping advisors maximize their long-term success and productivity with Prudential Advisors.

Working closely with recruiter partners, the AMD cultivates relationships with experienced advisor candidates and teams, helping them evaluate growth opportunities and understand the value of affiliating with Prudential Advisors. Beyond recruiting, the AMD serves as a trusted coach and business consultant to advisors, providing guidance on practice growth, wealth management capabilities, teaming strategies, and business development. Through leadership, influence, and execution, the AMD helps strengthen advisor engagement, improve productivity, and contribute to the overall growth of the firm.

Key Responsibilities

Advisor Growth & Acquisition - The AMD is a critical partner in the firm's experienced advisor recruiting efforts. Working in collaboration with recruiting professionals, the AMD engages prospective advisors and teams, builds trusted relationships, and helps candidates evaluate the strategic and economic benefits of joining Prudential Advisors. Through executive presence, credibility, and deep industry knowledge, the AMD influences advisor decision-making, supports due diligence discussions, and plays a key role in converting high-quality opportunities into successful hires. The AMD contributes to the growth of the firm through the acquisition of experienced advisors and teams aligned with the firm's long-term business objectives.

Advisor Development and Coaching - The AMD provides leadership, coaching, and business consulting to advisors throughout their careers. About the Role

As Salesforce’s marketing platforms evolve, our customers need guidance on both sides of the transition: optimizing and modernizing Marketing Cloud Account Engagement (formerly Pardot), and adopting Marketing Cloud Next. The Solution Architect designs and implements technical solutions across both products, helping customers decide what belongs where, how the pieces connect to Salesforce CRM and Data 360, and how to get there with minimal disruption.

This role leads solution design and oversees build work and quality assurance. A high-performing Solution Architect leads both technical and business consulting work and is a trusted advisor to marketing and sales leaders.

Lead the engagement

  • Mentor consultants and help them build skills on both platforms
  • Contribute to pre-sales conversations, scoping, and statements of work when needed

What You’ll Need

Requirements

  • Working knowledge of the Salesforce CRM data model and how marketing data syncs with Sales Cloud, including campaigns, leads, contacts, and opportunities

  • Strong business acumen and excellent technical ability
  • Strong presentation, documentation, and communication skills, with the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to business leaders
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple projects in a remote consulting environment
  • Consulting or partner firm experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Salesforce Certified Account Engagement Consultant and/or Account Engagement Specialist
  • Salesforce Administrator certification, plus additional certifications such as Data 360 Consultant or Sales Cloud Consultant
  • Experience with Data 360 (formerly Data Cloud), including unification, segmentation, and activation
  • Experience with Flow, Agentforce, or AI-driven marketing capabilities
  • Experience planning or leading migrations from Account Engagement or other marketing platforms to Marketing Cloud Next
  • Interest in or experience with Claude and AI-assisted delivery

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Property Management Coordinator to support the day-to-day operations of a growing self-storage portfolio.

This is a highly organized, customer-focused operations role that serves as the backbone of daily property management activities. You’ll ensure customer inquiries, rentals, move-ins, move-outs, billing issues, delinquency management, and administrative workflows are handled accurately and efficiently.

Working closely with leadership and on-site teams, you’ll help deliver exceptional customer service while maintaining organized systems and improving operational processes.

If you enjoy creating structure, solving problems, and keeping operations running smoothly, this role is built for you.

Customer Service & Tenant Support

FreedUp places talented Executive Assistants with founders and executives at growing US companies. We free leaders up by saving them time and effort so they can focus on the work only they can do. About the role

We're looking for a PR Specialist with real marketing experience to support the US-based founder of a PR firm. This is more than a traditional marketing role: you'll be the founder's operations partner and "second brain", someone he can brainstorm with, trust with his clients, and rely on to keep his marketing, calendar and priorities on track.

You'll own the firm's marketing in-house, from LinkedIn and social content to ad and email campaigns, and oversee any freelancers or agencies that support it. Over your first 60 to 90 days, you'll also grow into managing client communication directly. The founder wants someone who knows marketing fundamentals well enough to plug in from day one.

What you'll do

Marketing (Main Priority)

  • Own social media and content: post content on LinkedIn and other platforms such as TikTok, and make sure the overall strategy is sound and focused on growing leads.
  • Manage LinkedIn: learn the founder's voice from his posts (at least three a week), write and schedule posts, manage automated DM campaigns, and comment on other people's posts on his behalf.
  • Run campaigns: plan and run ad campaigns (LinkedIn, Meta) and outbound email campaigns, write the copy, and track results against KPIs.
  • Oversee marketing vendors: manage outsourced marketing teams and freelancers, hold them accountable for deliverables, and give the founder an honest view of how they're performing.
  • Support PR and media outreach: help draft pitches and materials and track outreach.

Client management

  • Send clients their weekly activity trackers and become a familiar point of contact.
  • Follow up with clients by email on action items.
  • Ramp up to full client communication within 60 to 90 days, and eventually take client calls on the founder's behalf.

Calendar, tasks and planning

  • Clean up and organize the founder's long-running to-do list, separating real tasks from ideas, and hold him accountable to his priorities.
  • Time-block his calendar in half-hour blocks, plan the next day's schedule based on open tasks and priorities, and adjust it after his review.
  • Manage his Outlook calendar and inbox, prepare meeting briefs and keep follow-ups organized.
  • Send a short end-of-day check-in covering what you did, plus any concerns or wins to flag.
  • Keep HubSpot up to date and help recruit freelance contractors when needed.

Requirements

Must-haves

  • A background in marketing, communications, PR or advertising, through a degree or work experience. A marketing degree is a strong plus.
  • Proven, hands-on marketing experience: you know the fundamentals of social media, content and campaigns and can plug in right away.
  • At least 3 years of experience as an Executive Assistant, Operations Manager, Virtual Assistant or in a similar support role.
  • Excellent written and spoken English (C1 or above).
  • Strong writing skills and the ability to adapt to someone else's voice and tone.
  • Experience managing calendars, to-do lists and competing priorities.
  • Professional, client-facing communication skills, with confidence on calls.
  • Personable and conversational, open to brainstorming, hardworking and reliable about deadlines.
  • Responsive and timely during US Eastern Time business hours.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience working at a marketing or PR agency (strongly preferred).

  • Experience managing freelancers, agencies or contractor teams.
  • Media relations or PR experience, such as pitching journalists or writing press releases.

Intec Automation, Inc. is an established (25+ years of business), custom automation company based in Rochester, NH that specializes in the design and build of custom automation equipment. JOB DESCRIPTION

Business Development Manager, Intec Automation Americas

Territory Ownership, Disciplined Prospecting, and Predictable Personal Bookings

Reports to

Sales Director, Intec Automation Americas

Job profile

Business Development Manager

Location

Field-based / remote within the Americas

Function

Commercial – Intec Automation Sales

Travel

Domestic travel up to approximately 50% or more, dependent on territory

Team

Individual contributor; partners with Applications Engineering, Sales Operations, and channel partners

Position Summary

The Business Development Manager, Intec Automation Americas is a territory-owning seller responsible for generating and closing qualified custom-automation opportunities in an assigned geography, in support of the Intec Automation Americas fiscal-year operating plan. The role carries personal bookings accountability and is expected to grow a durable, expanding pipeline through disciplined, protected prospecting and strong selling execution, whether that growth comes from new accounts or existing relationships.

Reporting to the Sales Director, Intec Automation Americas, the Business Development Manager operates as a hunter and account owner: qualifying new opportunities, quarterbacking the win plan, and working alongside the Applications Engineering team through concept development, costing, and proposal development. The role centers on two things: prospecting for new opportunities, and managing and winning the opportunities already in front of us.

The Business Development Manager is accountable for two connected outcomes: generating personal bookings against the assigned territory today, and building the qualified pipeline, account plans, and CRM discipline that make future bookings more predictable. Selling activity should build durable, growing account relationships across the territory.

Primary Responsibilities

Territory Ownership and Personal Bookings

  • Own monthly, quarterly, and annual personal bookings performance against the assigned bookings target within the Intec Automation Americas operating plan.
  • Plan, manage, and implement the sales process from prospecting through close, including disciplined post-sale follow-up.
  • Grow a defined territory, aligned with the Americas account-mapping and territory structure, while continuing to support and grow the accounts already assigned to you, including those that may fall outside that territory.
  • Balance new account development with account-expansion work on existing relationships, growing both in parallel.

Protected Prospecting and Pipeline Creation

  • Build and grow a qualified pipeline sufficient to support quarterly and annual personal bookings commitments, combining proactive outbound prospecting into net-new accounts with continued growth from existing relationships and territory.
  • Maintain a defined outreach cadence with clear persistence criteria for how many touches an opportunity receives before it is reprioritized.
  • Use the Ideal Customer Profile, account-mapping, and prospecting tools established under the Commercial Operating System to identify and qualify net-new targets.
  • Identify new sales opportunities within existing accounts and report market and competitive intelligence back to the Sales Director and broader commercial team.

Applications Engineering Partnership

  • Qualify opportunities and work alongside the assigned Applications Engineer to ensure the win strategy carries through concept generation, solution generation, and proposal development.
  • Quarterback the opportunity throughout the quoting cycle, keeping the Applications Engineer aligned to customer pain points, requirements, and competitive position.
  • Stay engaged with the opportunity through revisions, negotiation, and close, maintaining clear ownership from qualification to signed order.
  • Understand the customer's technical requirements well enough to shape a clear, qualified opportunity alongside Applications Engineering.

Commercial Operating System Adoption

  • Maintain accurate, current Salesforce opportunity data, including stage, value, close date, contacts, source, next action, and forecast classification.
  • Use Blue Sheet planning to structure and lead strategic or competitive opportunities.
  • Participate in coaching-centered deal and pipeline reviews with the Sales Director, bringing specific, dated customer next actions rather than status updates alone.
  • Apply funnel-stage discipline consistently, including timely movement of stalled opportunities and defined follow-up.

Forecasting and Account Planning

  • Create a quarterly sales forecast for the assigned territory and maintain an ongoing revenue-growth plan.
  • Own forecast honesty - surface timing and execution risk early, validating any committed opportunity against real customer evidence.
  • Maintain account plans for named strategic or expansion accounts, identifying whitespace and additional product lines or contacts beyond the current point of engagement.

Customer Value and Competitive Selling

  • Understand the competitive landscape on active opportunities, including price and lead-time position, to compete effectively on value.
  • Participate in structured win/loss reviews that capture competitor, price gap, and decision driver at the time of loss.
  • Monitor the external market and internal environment for new market segments, and contribute to business-case development for new opportunities as needed.

Measures of Success

  • Personal bookings meet or exceed the assigned annual target with disciplined quarterly execution.
  • Qualified pipeline grows steadily, combining new prospecting with continued growth from existing accounts.
  • Applications Engineering owns concept development, costing, and technical proposal writing on assigned opportunities, with the Business Development Manager selling and quarterbacking the opportunity throughout and contributing to selling points in the proposal.
  • Salesforce, Blue Sheet, and funnel-stage discipline become durable habits, with accurate, current opportunity data at all times.
  • Forecasts are timely, evidence-based, and reliable enough to support territory, capacity, and business planning.
  • Quarterly Commercial Excellence objectives are completed with documented evidence.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Business Management, with two or more years of related experience and/or training, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Three or more years of experience in thecustom automation, capital equipment, or industrial manufacturing industry.
  • Ability to understand customer technical requirements and translate them into a clear, qualified opportunity alongside Applications Engineering.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical and commercial documentation, and to respond professionally to customer, regulatory, or business-community inquiries.
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions from CRM and pipeline data.
  • Willingness and ability to travel domestically, approximately 50% or more depending on territory.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Engineering or medical-device manufacturing background.
  • Prior experience in a hunter-style, quota-carrying sales role with personal prospecting accountability.
  • Formal sales training.

Leadership Profile

  • A hunter mindset - energized by prospecting and new-account creation, as much as by growing accounts already in hand.
  • A disciplined commercial operator who keeps Salesforce, Blue Sheet, and forecast data current and trustworthy.
  • A collaborative partner to Applications Engineering, working alongside the team to carry the win strategy from concept through proposal.
  • A competitive seller who evaluates each opportunity's real strengths and weaknesses to compete on value.
  • A member of the commercial team who helps set the tone for the organization — bringing a genuine "can-do" attitude toward winning and selling, paired with an honest, clear-eyed view of where we are and where we need to be. We lead with honesty.

Company, Culture, and Benefits

Intec Automation, a Machine Solutions Inc. company, is a custom integrator focused on medical device, diagnostics, drug delivery, life sciences, and high-end consumer products. Our why is helping our customers succeed by creating innovative solutions to their manufacturing needs.

In alignment with Machine Solutions and Barry-Wehmiller values, team members are expected to care for people and perform with excellence through effective communication, customer focus, results, trust, and optimized work processes.

Eligible team members receive a competitive benefits package that may include medical, dental and vision coverage; a 401(k) retirement plan with company match; paid time off and sick time; health savings and spending accounts; short- and long-term disability; life and AD&D insurance; parental leave; and adoption and fertility benefits, subject to applicable plan terms and eligibility.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

This position spends time standing, sitting, walking, using hands to feel, handle, or finger, and reaching with hands or arms. Significant time is spent talking and listening with customers and internal partners. Minimal time is spent lifting weight, but when weight is lifted — for example, equipment demonstrations or site visits — up to 30 lbs may be required. Some time is spent near moving mechanical parts and with risk of electrical shock while on customer sites. The ability to read and interpret body language is important for this customer-facing role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

With over four decades of expertise, we partner with some of the world’s most influential companies to design and optimize environments that demand precision, scalability, and resilience.

Join us and be part of a team where your voice matters, your work makes an impact, and your growth is a shared priority.

Position Title: SeniorSubstation Commissioning Specialist

Position Location: Remote with up to 75% travel to project sites, this may include travel to any or all 50 US states .Must have a valid driver’s license and ability to rent vehicles.

JOB SUMMARY

The Senior Substation Commissioning Specialist is responsible for overseeing the full life-cycle commissioning of electrical substations, ensuring that newly constructed or upgraded substations are fully operational and meet industry standards. This role includes reviewing design documents, coordinating with construction and engineering teams, and performing detailed testing and validation of substation systems, including power transformers, breakers, relays, and control systems.

The Senior Substation Commissioning Specialist will be self-directed on day-to-day work and receive high level instruction on new projects or assignments. Will execute commissioning and lead project teams and projects of complex scope. Will coordinate activities of other personnel.

The Senior Substation Commissioning Specialist will travel around the country to the different job locations at different times depending on status of project. The job does not constitute staying in one location for long periods of time.

This person will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals and values, as well as departmental objectives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Perform On-site Substation Commissioning Activities and Manage Projects (50%)

  • On-site inspection, validation, functional testing, verification and troubleshooting of electrical equipment such as transformers, switchgear, protection relays, and control systems
  • Participate in factory witness testing and observe startup activities
  • Use technical equipment to perform testing – Omicron test unit experience is a plus but not required
  • Direct vendors / contractors in the execution of the testing
  • Timely and effective management and delivery of projects
  • Identify potential project risks and aid in development of strategies to minimize impact and control deviations from estimated costs and project deadlines
  • Primary site contact for clients and build effective, long-term client relationships
  • Onboarding of project team for mobilization and provides ongoing updates

Develop Testing Plans and Procedures for Substation Projects (20%)

  • Development of commissioning plans
  • Prepare pre-functional checklists
  • Prepare functional performance test scripts

Review Substation Design Documents, Drawings and Specifications (15%)

  • Review shop drawings and submittals
  • Review sequence of operations
  • Lead and participate in commissioning focused design reviews

Reporting (15%)

  • Direct and assist with all project communication and reporting
  • Prepare and oversee development of project progress reports for internal and external stakeholders
  • Prepare and oversee the final commissioning report for submission to client
  • Manage personal hours and site team’s hours using company tools

Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget

Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned

POSITION REQUIREMENTS (ADVANCED LEVEL FOR ALL OF THE FOLLOWING)

  • Knowledge of substation system electrical equipment, protection, and control systems.
  • Knowledge of regulatory standards, including IEEE, NERC, and FERC compliance requirements.
  • Skilled in using power system analysis software, protection coordination tools, and SCADA integration
  • Skilled at using MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams), along with exceptional organizational skills for file management
  • Skilled in completing assignments accurately and with attention to detail
  • Ability to leverage AI and emerging technologies to streamline workflows, optimize operational processes, and contribute to company-wide innovation
  • Ability to work successfully in a remote environment thru effective communication and organizational skills, self-motivation, proactiveness and resourcefulness in a distraction free workspace
  • Ability to follow company and site safety requirements
  • Ability to analyze and prepare documents, reports and correspondence
  • Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written form (technical and non-technical information)
  • Ability to communicate effectively directly with clients and at times serve as primary point of client contact
  • Ability to work successfully as a member of a team and independently with moderate supervision
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet close deadlines
  • Ability to effectively plan and delegate the work of others
  • Ability to achieve certification for NFPA70E and / or OSHA training as / if required
  • Organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Frequently manipulating, moving or grasping small parts, devices or tools
  • Frequently required to remain in a stationary position
  • Frequently moving through office, critical facility and other environments (such as low temperatures, high temperatures and outdoor elements such as precipitation and wind), including tight and confined spaces
  • Frequently descending / ascending stairs and ladders to access equipment
  • On occasion the employee may be required to position self under or over equipment
  • On occasion the employee may move equipment weighing up to 50 pounds

TRAVEL / RELOCATION REQUIREMENTS

  • Must have a valid driver’s license and ability to rent vehicles.
  • Up to 75%, this may include travel to any or all 50 US states
  • Effective May 7, 2025, and in accordance with U.S. federal regulations for domestic air travel, a valid REAL ID (or an acceptable alternative, such as a passport) is required for travel associated with this position.  
  • Travel is defined as physically leaving home on behalf of business activities including but not limited to client sites, meetings with other employees, meetings for business development purposes, running errands on behalf of the business, attending industry conferences, etc. 
  • Travel may involve transportation by car or plane depending on the destination and nature of the business need. 
  • Potential relocation opportunities may exist per project needs. 
  • Potential international travel based on project needs and skillset development. 

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction or related discipline

OR

  • Two years’ experience with electrical substation commissioning, including testing and troubleshooting of transformers, protection relays, circuit breakers, and SCADA systems

PLUS

  • Minimum eight years’ additional experience with electrical substation commissioning, including testing and troubleshooting of transformers, protection relays, circuit breakers, and SCADA systems.
  • Experience working with utility companies or large-scale industrial electrical systems.

BENEFITS
