jobs.title: Group Chief Financial Officer
jobs.excerpt: Who We AreCatalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group - education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology - funded entirely from its own operating cash.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Catalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group - education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology - funded entirely from its own operating cash. We have never taken outside capital.

The cash engine is Decentralized Masters, a DeFi education business that went from zero to 150+ people, 4,500+ paying members and roughly $48.6M of FY26 revenue at ~25% earnings before tax in four years. That engine funds everything else on this page.

In build over the next 18 months

  • A lifestyle community membership - consumer membership economics, distinct from education.
  • A business mastermind on the Hampton model - high-net-worth peer community, recurring and relationship-led.
  • A regulated investment fund. The capstone. AUM reporting, investor relations, NAV calculation, fund administration, audit and regulatory infrastructure. At most companies this alone is a full-time CFO mandate.

Why This Role Exists

A single education business at this revenue and margin commands a private-market multiple in the mid single digits of earnings. A diversified group - education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and a regulated fund, each valued on its own sector methodology and connected by real shared-services and synergy architecture - is a fundamentally different asset.

Closing that gap is the job. Concretely, you will:

  • Build the sum-of-the-parts valuation framework across every business unit, with a defensible methodology and comparables set for each.
  • Structure each entity so that it maximises its own multiple, and structure the group so the whole is worth more than the parts.
  • Take the group from founder-run reporting to institutional-grade financials that survive a quality-of-earnings review and a full due diligence process.
  • Take the group to market early - deliberately ahead of a formal process - and convert what buyers and advisers tell us into operational change while there is still time to act on it.
  • Build the group equity story and the materials that put it in front of institutional buyers, and run the process alongside the CEO and advisers.
  • Design the employee incentive architecture at group level, so the people who carry each unit are aligned before a transaction rather than after it.
  • Stand up the regulated fund and the investor infrastructure behind it.
  • Protect and improve the economics of the cash engine while all of the above happens. If DM slows, none of the rest matters.

How This Role Is Resourced

You are not being hired to close the books. A Finance Manager reports to you and owns day-to-day financial operations - the monthly close, the accounting system, payroll, reconciliations, deferred revenue schedules and the chart of accounts. Beneath them sit a Financial Controller and an Accounting & Payroll Specialist.

What You Will Own

1. Enterprise Value & Capital Events (Primary)

  • Own the sum-of-the-parts valuation model: the methodology, comparables and defensible assumptions for each business unit, and the roll-up into a coherent group valuation.
  • Identify and drive the highest-value levers to increase group enterprise value - margin, retention, revenue quality, recurring mix, entity structure, and the synergy story between units.
  • Take the group to institutional readiness: three years of clean, comparable financials per entity, a quality-of-earnings-survivable position, a populated data room and a diligence-ready control environment.
  • Build the group equity story, the information memorandum and the management presentation, and be credible in the room with institutional buyers and their advisers.
  • Run the capital event process alongside the CEO and external advisers - buyer engagement, diligence management, negotiation support, and the post-transaction reporting obligations that follow.

2. Holdco Architecture, Systems & Synergy

  • Design the holding-company structure: which entities sit where, in which jurisdictions, and why - with counsel and tax advisers.
  • Select and implement the group ERP and consolidation platform. Own the selection criteria, the sequence and the delivery.
  • Build shared services where they create real margin and demonstrable synergy value, and resist them where they destroy unit-level clarity.
  • Set intercompany and transfer pricing policy across a group where one entity generates leads, another converts them, a third delivers the product and a fourth manages money - across the UAE, the US and potentially Europe.
  • Produce unit-level P&Ls that roll up cleanly and let leadership see which businesses earn their capital.

3. Capital Allocation Across Unlike Businesses

  • Own the framework that decides where the next dollar of operating cash goes - paid media, headcount, software build, fund seed capital, acquisitions or reserve - with an explicit hurdle rate and time horizon for each.
  • Allocate across assets with genuinely different return profiles, risk characteristics and payback periods, and defend the trade-offs to the CEO with a model behind them.
  • Own group headcount and cost strategy. Be the person who can say no, with numbers.

4. The Cash Engine - Direct-Response Economics

Required, not optional. The group is funded by performance marketing and will be for the foreseeable future.

  • Own CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC, ROAS, CPQC, contribution margin and cash payback by funnel, offer, channel and cohort.
  • Own the front-end versus back-end monetisation model, and the timing mismatch between media spend today and payment-plan collections over twelve months.
  • Improve pricing and offer-ladder economics across low, mid and high ticket.
  • Model cohort behaviour, renewals, churn, refunds, chargebacks and payment-plan default — and build them into the forecast rather than discovering them later.
  • Set the media spend guardrails that keep the group liquid in a bad month without capping a good one.

5. Fund Structuring, Regulation & Investor Infrastructure

  • Lead jurisdiction and structure selection for the investment fund with counsel - DIFC, ADGM or otherwise - and own the trade-offs.
  • Stand up the operating infrastructure: fund administration, NAV calculation, audit, fee and carry mechanics, subscription and redemption processes.
  • Build investor reporting infrastructure capable of serving hundreds of investors on a reliable cadence.
  • Own regulatory compliance across the group: UAE regimes including VARA and ADGM where applicable, FTC and advertising-claims compliance in marketing, securities considerations across the investment products, and the regulatory perimeter around the wealth and tax planning tools.

6. Treasury, Cash & Group Risk

  • Own rolling 13-week and 12-month cash forecasts at entity and group level, and the liquidity view across the whole structure.
  • Optimise working capital - processor reserves and holdbacks, refund provisions, receivable ageing on payment plans.
  • Own banking, merchant accounts and payment processors: redundancy, concentration risk, chargeback ratios and cost of processing.
  • Set treasury policy for digital asset exposure: custody, counterparty limits, stablecoin policy, valuation and controls.

7. Legal & Corporate Affairs

You are not expected to be a lawyer. You are expected to own the function so the CEO does not have to.

  • Own the relationship with, and the budget for, external counsel, auditors, tax advisers and transaction advisers across jurisdictions.
  • Own the corporate calendar across every entity - filings, licences, renewals, tax deadlines. Nothing lapses, particularly not during diligence.
  • Own commercial terms on major partnerships, vendor, affiliate and talent agreements; legal drafting stays with counsel.

Requirements

What You Must Bring

Required

  • 10-20 years in finance, including 3+ years as CFO, Group CFO or VP Finance with full P&L and balance sheet accountability.
  • Direct, hands-on experience of a transaction. You have been on a sell-side or minority sale process and can describe what you personally built - the model, the CIM, the data room, the diligence responses - and what went wrong.
  • Multi-entity holdco or portfolio experience. You have run finance across several unlike businesses, not one company with divisions, and you can explain how you consolidated and how you allocated between them.
  • Sum-of-the-parts fluency. You can value a software business, a subscription publishing business, a services business and a fee-earning investment business, and explain why each methodology is the right one.
  • Performance-marketing economics. You have owned unit economics in a business spending meaningful money on paid acquisition - CAC, LTV, payback, front end versus back end. Required. Not the defining filter, but a candidate who cannot do this cannot protect our cash engine.
  • Multi-jurisdiction experience with real consolidation, ideally including the UAE, the US and Europe.
  • Experience owning the relationship with external counsel, auditors and transaction advisers.
  • Fully conversant in both IFRS and US GAAP, and able to defend technical positions under scrutiny.
  • A prolific, demonstrable user of AI tools in finance work - you can show us what you have built or automated.

Strongly Preferred

  • Financial services depth - you have worked across at least two of publishing, education, software, wealth management or fund management.
  • You have structured or operated an investment fund: jurisdiction, administration, NAV, fee and carry mechanics, investor reporting.
  • PE-backed or PE operating experience - you understand how institutional buyers think and what they discount.
  • Crypto and digital asset exposure. You do not need to be a trader, but you cannot be squeamish about the asset class.
  • Subscription accounting and deferred revenue depth across high-ticket, payment plan and recurring products.

Do Not Apply If…

  • Your entire career has been in large corporate environments with no exposure to founder-led, high-growth or PE-backed businesses.
  • You have never been close to a transaction and would be learning the process on our timeline.
  • You have never treated paid acquisition as a strategic cost lever.
  • You need six months to ramp before you add value.
  • You prefer slow-moving, consensus-heavy environments, or you fold when a founder pushes back.
  • You do not want legal, regulatory and corporate affairs coordination in your remit.
  • You want to build a large team before you have personally fixed the numbers.
  • You are not actively using AI tools in your work today.

Personality & Cultural Fit

  • Direct communicator who challenges the founders with data, in the room, in real time.
  • Equally credible with a PE partner and with a media buyer. Both conversations happen in the same week here.
  • Entrepreneurial and comfortable in ambiguity - you build the answer rather than wait for the brief.
  • Zero tolerance for sloppy reporting, in your team or in yourself.
  • Builder mentality. Comfortable in the model and in the detail when it matters.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive base, depending on transaction and holdco experience.
  • Performance bonus tied to enterprise value creation, not just operating margin.
  • A transaction bonus on a successful capital event - the upside here is material and it is the point of the role.
  • Equity participation under the C-suite framework, structured so you have skin in the game before the event rather than after it.
  • UAE-based roles are tax-free, which materially changes take-home pay.
  • Direct access to the founders, a peer relationship with the Group COO, and genuine authority over how capital is deployed.
  • An inherited finance team, so you are building the architecture rather than clearing a backlog alone.

If you are a divisional CFO looking for a bigger version of the job you already have, this is not it.

If you have built the financial architecture that made a diversified group worth substantially more than the sum of its operating profits - and you want to do it again, from profitability, with your own mandate - we should talk.

jobs.excerpt: It's a great feeling to work for a company that does so much good for others around the world!
jobs.description:
It's a great feeling to work for a company that does so much good for others around the world!

About Us:

Innovative Network of Knowledge is a dynamic and rapidly growing virtual company in an emerging space of innovation in education. Our passion is to change education forever for the K-12 students (online) we serve. We are changing the way children learn and apply knowledge in the real world. Through our Project Based approach, supported by personal Educational Concierges, we strengthen the whole child through their educational experience. Through synchronous and asynchronous opportunities, co-teaching, and workshop labs, our students are immersed and challenged in a way not experienced in today’s educational landscape. In addition, staff and students will take part in weekly programs that promote character and citizenship opportunities to grow not only as a school but also as a community at large. We guarantee that you and your child become part of our family and will be engaged, excited, and prepared for college, career, and life.

Core Focus:

Innovative Network of Knowledge seeks to change education forever through innovation and technology. We offer a well of knowledge, a spring of possibilities and a place where your family becomes part of ours.

Key Benefits:

  • Educational Concierge: Every family has access to a dedicated Educational Concierge to assist with enrollment, course planning and ongoing academic guidance, ensuring each student finds their unique path to success.
    ● Goal-Oriented Tracking: We help students set meaningful milestones and track their progress, encouraging achievement and celebrating every accomplishment along the way.
    ● Community-Focused Learning: Our programs are structured to foster collaboration and connection, building confidence and social skills even within a virtual setting.

Technology:

Innovative Network of Knowledge will not provide this role with a company laptop, and the employee will secure and cover the cost for the operation of this job in the virtual landscape of his/her home office. (internet, telephone, home office setup, etc.).

Position Overview:
The PRN (as Needed) Instructional Content Specialist plays a key role in supporting high-quality instruction across our virtual school by collaborating with teachers and the Dean of Curriculum and Instruction to design engaging, standards-aligned lesson plans and instructional materials. This position focuses on developing clear, effective teaching slides and resources that promote student understanding, consistency, and strong instructional practices in a virtual learning environment.
The ideal candidate has experience in instructional coaching and a strong understanding of at least two core content areas. They are skilled in translating standards into practical classroom application, supporting teachers in planning rigorous and engaging lessons, and ensuring alignment with organizational expectations and best practices in online instruction.

Essential Responsibilities:

Instructional Content Development
● Collaborate with Dean of Curriculum and Instruction to design and develop high-quality, standards-aligned lesson plans
● Create engaging, student-friendly instructional slide decks that support clear learning

objectives

  • Ensure lesson materials include key instructional components such as warm-ups, guided practice, and checks for understanding
    ● Adapt and differentiate materials to meet diverse student needs in a virtual setting

Curriculum Alignment & Consistency

  • Ensure all instructional materials align with state standards and organizational expectations
    ● Promote vertical and horizontal alignment across grade levels and content areas
    ● Maintain consistency in instructional routines, structure, and expectations across courses
    ● Collaborate with leadership to refine scope and sequence documents and pacing guides

Virtual Learning Best Practices

  • Design materials that reflect best practices in virtual instruction, including student engagement and interaction
    ● Incorporate strategies that support gradual release of responsibility and active learning
    ● Ensure instructional resources are accessible, organized, and easy for teachers to implement
    ● Stay current on trends and tools that enhance virtual teaching and learning

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
● Work closely with instructional leaders to continuously improve content and delivery
● Participate in content development sessions and feedback cycles
● Revise and update materials based on teacher feedback and student performance data
● Support the overall mission of improving instructional quality and student outcomes across the virtual school

Qualifications:

Required:

● Valid Texas teaching certification

  • Minimum of 3–5 years of successful teaching experience

Preferred
● Master’s degree in Education or related field
● Previous experience in a virtual or online education environment
● Experience with Project-Based Learning (PBL) models

Skills and Abilities:

  • Excellent communication and organizational abilities

● Ability to analyze and act on data

  • High level of accountability and follow-through
    ● Collaborative mindset

● Knowledge of Google Suites Products

Work Conditions:

  • PRN (As Needed) No guarantee of continuous work or certain hours. PRNs complete work and tasks as assigned.
    ● Work is performed from a remote office environment.

Notice: Employment with Innovative Network of Knowledge will be on an at-will basis. As such, this position description is not a contract or guarantee of employment for a definite amount of time.

English (United States)

If you like to work with people that believe they can make a difference in the world, this is the company for you!

EEO Statement

In accordance with Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and other applicable federal and state laws (e.g., the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), it is our policy to provide equal employment opportunity and treat all employees equally regardless of race, religion, national origin, color, sex, or any other classification made unlawful or prohibited by federal, state and/or local laws, such as age, citizenship status, veteran or military status, or disability. About Visio Lending

Visio Lending is the nation’s leader in rental home financing. Founded in 2012 in Austin, Texas, Visio enables small- to medium- sized investors to grow their rental home and vacation rental portfolios. Headquartered in fantastic Austin, Texas, since late 2015, Visio has financed more than $1 billion in Rental360 loans. With more than $400 million in capital onboard, a proven record of investment grade bond issuance on Wall Street, and an outstanding 100+ team, Visio is poised for continued success.

Why We Love Working at Visio:

We at Visio are passionate about working together towards our goals to continually push this company forward. We innovate, collaborate, celebrate team successes, and recognize individual accomplishments. At Visio Lending, you’ll work on meaningful initiatives that directly support real estate investors nationwide. We offer a collaborative culture, growth opportunities, and flexibility with remote work options.

How to Apply?

To be considered for employment, please submit your application online. While we appreciate all the interest we receive, only candidates selected for phone screening, or an interview will be contacted directly. You will receive application status alerts via email so make sure your email address is accurate.

Note: Incomplete applications will not be considered. Unanswered application questions or responses indicating “see resume” will be considered incomplete and you will be removed from consideration.

Visio Financial Services, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer

The Opportunity:

As a Business Systems Analyst / UAT Lead, you will lead the planning, coordination, and execution of user acceptance testing (UAT) for Visio Lending's software solutions, while also independently owning business analysis for assigned initiatives. Working closely with other Business Systems Analysts, business stakeholders, and Engineering teams, you'll organize testing cycles, guide business users through the UAT process, track defects and approvals, and communicate testing progress and release readiness. On smaller initiatives, you'll also lead requirements discovery, documentation, and stakeholder facilitation from intake through business validation.

If you are an organized, analytical professional who enjoys coordinating cross-functional teams, translating business needs into clear requirements, and ensuring nothing falls through the cracks, this role is for you. You'll thrive if you're a strong communicator with exceptional attention to detail, comfortable owning ambiguous work, and passionate about delivering high-quality solutions that support the business.

What You'll Do

  • Own the planning, coordination, and execution of UAT across assigned releases and projects
  • Independently lead business analysis for assigned small to moderate initiatives, from requirements discovery through implementation and validation, filling remaining capacity around UAT priorities
  • Facilitate requirements workshops, discovery sessions, and cross-functional meetings with business, technology, and vendor stakeholders
  • Elicit, document, and drive approval of clear, complete, and testable requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria
  • Partner with Business Systems Analysts and stakeholders to translate requirements into UAT test plans and scenarios
  • Develop and maintain UAT plans, entry/exit criteria, readiness checklists, and schedules
  • Recruit, prepare, and guide business users who serve as UAT testers
  • Maintain traceability between requirements, acceptance criteria, UAT scenarios, defects, and business validation
  • Track UAT execution, defects, and resolution status, and report regularly on UAT health
  • Facilitate defect triage and communication between business testers, BSAs, and engineering
  • Manager UAT sign-off, approvals, and go/no-go recommendations
  • Coordinate test environment and test data readiness with technical teams
  • Demonstrate completed solutions to stakeholders and confirm delivered functionality meets business intent
  • Maintain UAT and requirements documentation, templates, and standards, driving continuous improvement
  • Contribute to agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, standups, and retrospectives
  • Other responsibilities and duties as assigned based on business needs
  • Authorized Remote Locations: AL, AR, AZ, FL, GA, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, MI, NC, SC, TX, UT
  • Salary Range: $85,000 - $115,000 (Exempt level position)

What We Are Looking For:

  • Bachelor's degree in business, information systems,technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • 3- 5 years of experience in a Business Systems Analyst, Business Analyst, Systems Analyst, or similar technology delivery role
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading requirements discovery and analysis for technology initiatives
  • Experience facilitating requirements workshops with cross-functional stakeholders
  • Strong experience translating business needs into clear, testable requirements and acceptance criteria
  • Experience supporting or coordinating User Acceptance Testing as part of the software development lifecycle
  • Strong understanding of the SDLC and the relationship between requirements, development, testing, UAT, and implementation
  • Experience working with requirements, test management, or defect tracking tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, TestRail
  • Strong meeting facilitation, stakeholder management, and communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives, priorities, and deadlines
  • Ability to independently own assigned work and drive activities and decisions to resolution

What We Prefer to Find:

jobs.description:
*CANDIDATES MUST BE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES OR CANADA**

About SafelyYou

SafelyYou’s passionate mission is to empower safer, more person-centered care across senior living through world-leading AI, industry-changing hardware, and remote expert clinicians, significantly improving outcomes for residents while increasing peace of mind for families and reducing costs for communities.

Originating in 2015 as the doctoral research of CEO George Netscher—and inspired by his own family's experience with Alzheimer's disease—SafelyYou was spun out of UC Berkeley’s Artificial Intelligence Research Lab, one of the top five AI research groups in the world. And today, our company is solving critical challenges in senior living, from resident falls and ER visits to staffing concerns, length of stay, and NOI. All helping ensure that communities can focus on improved care for residents while still reaching their financial goals.

SafelyYou is one of five most innovative fall technologies referenced in the Senate Falls Report (2019), a winner of the McKnight’s Tech Partner of the Year, and has been named to Fortune’s Impact 20 list, which recognizes companies making people’s lives better through innovation.

Your Role at SafelyYou

As a Data Integration Engineer at SafelyYou, you will be the subject matter expert behind how our internal systems communicate with the outside world. You will design, build, and operate robust integration pipelines that transform data between our internal event-based architecture and the diverse formats required by our third-party API partners. You will play a critical role in scaling our external data exchange capabilities, handling complex payload mappings, and ensuring that our systems gracefully manage failure modes at scale.

You will work closely with R&D architects, other data engineers, backend developers, and cross-functional teams to define and implement integration patterns for webhooks, external REST APIs, and partner platforms. Additionally, you will own technical communications for integrations, managing Go-Live data backfills and writing clear API specifications for customer-facing documents.

This is a fully remote role. You are expected to work with minimal guidance, act as a subject matter expert for integration patterns, and proactively identify opportunities for architectural improvement.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and operate robust integration pipelines to ingest data from and push data to third-party APIs, webhooks, and custom endpoints.

  • Transform, normalize, and map data payloads between SafelyYou’s internal schema and external partner specifications (e.g., JSON/XML schemas, third-party platforms).

  • Performing validation on data received from third-parties, segregating data that fails validation, and automating processes with third-parties to resolve anomalies.

  • Manage and execute complex data backfills and Go-Live integration pipelines for new customer rollouts.

  • Write and maintain clear, high-quality technical documentation and API specifications for both internal engineering teams and external partners.

  • Triage, troubleshoot, and gracefully handle integration failure modes, rate limits, and edge cases at scale, building resilient retry mechanisms.

  • Scale our ability to support 3rd party integrations by building systems and tooling to allow non-engineer users to configure, monitor, and perform backfills for third-party integrations.

  • Ensure data quality, consistency, and reliability by developing automated tests and validating payload outputs with ongoing pipeline monitoring.

  • Work in an Agile environment to plan, track, and improve the delivery of new integration features and products.

  • Collaborate with customer support, operations, and product teams to provide technical support and participate in on-call rotation as needed.

Requirements:

  • 5+ years of professional experience in software, backend, or data engineering, preferably in a startup environment.

  • Deep hands-on experience building, consuming, and operating integrations with REST APIs, webhooks, and third-party platforms.

  • Strong programming proficiency in Python and SQL for building reliable data transformation and integration pipelines.

  • Proven track record of handling complex data transformations, schema mapping, and payload normalization across disparate systems.

  • Experience encountering and solving API failure modes and operational challenges at scale (e.g., implementing exponential backoff, dead-letter queues, idempotency). Has seen where things fail and can recommend solutions to maintain a stable platform.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with specific experience writing technical documentation, ADRs, or API specs.

  • Proactive about anticipating and addressing data ingestion issues before they impact the business.

  • Prioritize quality over speed. When it is done, it is really done.

The Ideal Candidate:

  • Proficiency with modern data stack tools, such as dbt and PySpark.

  • Familiarity with workflow orchestration concepts and tools, such as Airflow.

  • Exposure to Terraform and Cloud Infrastructure, such as AWS (Athena, RDS, EKS).

  • Experience with electronic health records (EHR) and associated data privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA) is a strong plus.

  • Experience with HL7 data feeds and the FHIR API specification is a huge plus.

Job Description

Responsible for the preparation and review of the financial statements through the coordination of the month end close and reporting process. Responsible for gathering and analyzing complex financial information, evaluating accounting implications, and formulating recommendations for senior management based on findings. Provide technical guidance on accounting and fiscal procedures. Supports the implementation of projects to improve and/or facilitate accounting and reporting functions.   • May be responsible for setup and maintenance of accounting system, chart of account, or other reporting and accounting sub-systems.
  • Provide leadership, coaching, support & problem solving assistance, and knowledge transfer to others.
  • Research financial and operating data (including technical accounting pronouncements, promulgated regulatory bulletins, and benchmarked industry information), prepares financial analyses and reports of findings and prepares recommendations to management,
  • Perform due diligence reviews through detailed research of financial information. Review deal structures, evaluate accounting implications, and make recommendations as appropriate.
  • Initiate projects to improve processes/controls, partner with project teams to ensure resolution of project/post-project issues and participate on cross-functional projects as a finance representative.
  • Review financial statements and supporting documentation for GAAP/SAP monthly, quarterly, and annual reports for internal/external audiences.
  • Work closely with other BCBS plans and the BCBSA to resolve accounting and reporting issues.
  • Assist with audits by providing requested information to auditors and resolve issues and draft resolutions.
  • Maintain and enhance internal controls and perform self-testing.

What You Bring   

  • Bachelor's degree or advanced degree (where required)
  • 5+ years of experience in related field.
  • In lieu of degree, 7+ years of experience in related field.

Bonus Points 

  • Familiarity with insurance-specific accounting concepts, including premium accounting, loss reserves, claims accounting, and reinsurance transactions.
  • Advanced proficiency in ERP systems such as Oracle, SAP, Workday, or Microsoft Dynamics.
  • CPA designation or progress toward obtaining CPA certification.

What You’ll Get 

  • The opportunity to work at the cutting edge of health care delivery with a team that’s deeply invested in the community  
  • Work-life balance, flexibility, and the autonomy to do great work  
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage along with numerous health and wellness programs   
  • Parental leave and support plus adoption and surrogacy assistance
  • Career development programs and tuition reimbursement for continued education   
  • 401k match including an annual company contribution   
  • Learn more   

Where You’ll Work

Our Hybrid Flex approach is built on presence with a purpose – giving you flexibility to work remotely with intentional in-person connection – that supports a workplace that’s flexible, connected, and future focused.

In a Hybrid-Flex role, you’ll work in the office at least two days a week for collaboration and connection. In a Remote Flex role, you’ll work virtually, with a few in-office visits each year for meaningful moments that matter.

Whether your role is Hybrid Flex or Remote Flex depends on the nature of the work and distance from our Durham headquarters. We welcome candidates from outside the local area and in any states listed on this job posting. Onsite expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

At Blue Cross NC, we take great pride in a fair and equitable compensation package that reflects market-price and our starting salaries are typically planned near the middle of the range listed. Our base salary is part of a robust Total Rewards package that includes an Annual Incentive Bonus*, 401(k) with employer match, Paid Time Off (PTO), and competitive health benefits and wellness programs.

*Based on annual corporate goal achievement and individual performance.

Strategic Partners Account Manager

About Accruent
At Accruent, our mission is to transform the way organizations manage their built environment. Through data-led intelligence, we help people and systems work together more effectively, driving business forward. With over 4,000 customers across 149 countries, our cloud-based solutions enable organizations to optimize real estate, facilities, and asset management-delivering real value through efficiency, compliance, and performance.

The Role
As a Strategic Partners Account Manager, you will own and grow a portfolio of Accruent’s most important partner-led accounts. This is a revenue-owning role focused on driving pipeline, executing deals, and scaling the performance of Accruent’s partner ecosystem.

You are not a supporting resource to a sales team-you are the primary owner of the partner-led sales motion. You will lead everything from pipeline creation and deal strategy through closing opportunities and managing renewals, while enabling partners to sell and scale Accruent solutions.

Success in this role requires the ability to build partner capability, drive partner accountability, and continuously improve how partners operate with Accruent, resulting in faster deal cycles, stronger pipeline, and increased partner-led revenue.

What You’ll Do

  • Own and expand a portfolio of strategic partner-led accounts, driving revenue growth and expansion through joint account planning and execution

  • Drive structured pipeline creation with partners through target account mapping, new logos, and cross-sell/upsell identification

  • Influence deal strategy and pricing for partner-led opportunities

  • Conduct Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) with partners to assess performance, align on growth priorities, and drive accountability to targets

  • Drive forecast accuracy and revenue predictability with partners, with a strong focus on bookings and ARR growth, retention, and pipeline conversion

  • Build and continuously improve parter selling capability, ensuring partners can independently position, scope, and progress Accruent deals efficiently

  • Develop and manage a partner recruitment pipeline, aligned to Accruent’s growth priorities and target profiles

  • Recruit new, strategic partners to expand our partner ecosystem with a focus on partners with SaaS capabilities

  • Scale partner motions regionally, adapting GTM approaches, messaging, and enablement to local market conditions

  • Own partner onboarding and enablement outcomes, ensuring partners are successfully activated, certified, and able to sell Accruent solutions

  • Drive accountability for partner enablement through onboarding, including training completion and certifications post-onboarding

  • Track and manage partner performance through daily visual management, ensuring clear visibility into pipeline, progress against targets, and risks

  • Apply the Fortive Business System (FBS) to identify inefficiencies and proactively improve the partner experience and internal processes

  • Accountable for partner deal execution, including quoting and order processes

  • Spend time “at gemba” (where the work is done) by meeting in-person with partners and customers to understand their challenges, and uncover new opportunities

  • Drive cross-functional action across Sales, Product, Enablement, Services, Marketing, Deal Desk and other cross-functional teams to improve our partner channel

  • Track record of exceeding quota targets (directly or through partners)

  • Proven ability to own or drive the full sales cycle: pipeline creation, deal strategy, pricing, quoting, and close

  • Strong commercial and deal acumen, including pricing strategy, negotiation, and balancing partner incentives with company growth

  • Executive presence and influencing skills, with the ability to engage partner executives to align on strategy, address performance gaps, and drive accountability

  • Experience in Salesforce owning opportunities, accounts, activities, and reporting

  • Ability to travel up to 20% for QBRs, customer visits, kaizens

Nice to have:

  • Prior experience managing partners in at least 2+ EMEA countries or regions, with demonstrated success adapting strategy across markets

  • Knowledge of Accruent’s solutions

  • Experience working with resellers, facilities/asset management providers, or industrial solution companies

  • Familiarity with continuous improvement methodologies (FBS, Lean, or similar) and applying them to partner or sales performance

What We Offer

  • A dynamic, international team environment with colleagues across the globe.

  • Opportunities to develop, grow, and build your success in a fast-moving SaaS company.

  • Competitive remuneration and benefits package.

  • An inclusive culture where new ideas and initiatives are welcomed, and your work has real impact.

Fortive's essential technology makes the world safer and more productive. We accelerate transformation in high-impact fields like workplace safety, build environments, and healthcare.

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Global Category Lead, Full-Service CRO - Associate Director, Global Procurement R&D


What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. We are seeking an individual who thrives in ambiguity, capable of driving category management initiatives with strategic vision and precision.

You will serve as the Global Category Manager and lead the global category strategy for Full-Service CRO. This includes developing multi-year category strategies that address business needs while achieving best practice outcomes, building enterprise-wide business partnerships, and activating Procurement resources to drive strategic sourcing results to reduce costs and enable top-line performance.

Your responsibilities will include analyzing internal demand (using Business Partner Management processes), external market data, spend & specifications to produce category plans aligned with Business objectives and cost reduction / sourcing initiates. As a Category Manager, you will play a pivotal role in managing the innovation agenda of Procurement. This role will drive supplier performance, manage risk, and deliver sustained value across a complex global professional services landscape.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead category management for Full-Service CRO, supporting all phases of fully outsourced clinical trials, including ClinPharm, Ph I-IV, Observational Research, and inherited studies resulting from M&A activity.
  • Partner with R&D, Clinical, Regulatory, and Compliance teams to ensure alignment with FDA, EMA, HIPAA, and GCP standards.
  • Negotiate contracts, amendments, and competitive commercial terms, rates, and discounts with vendors supporting fully outsourced clinical trials, balancing innovation with compliance & risk, while positioning Amgen and stakeholders for success.
  • Partner with Program Leads, Study Teams, and R&D Supplier Governance to enable supplier governance frameworks, drive high-quality delivery and performance, and ensure effective & timely issue resolution.
  • Monitor market trends & intelligence, including the evolving digital health regulations, and integrate compliance, quality, and risk mitigation into sourcing strategies.
  • Provide strategic oversight as the lead for the Full-Service CRO category and sourcing, ensuring alignment between category strategies and Amgen’s evolving business needs. Act as a trusted advisor to ensure that procurement initiatives are aligned with broader organizational objectives.
  • Guide and facilitate collaboration across cross-functional teams and regional stakeholders, ensuring that procurement strategies meet the diverse needs of the organization and are implemented effectively.
  • Ensure that all procurement activities in support of Full-Service CRO are managed in compliance with regulatory, contractual, and operational risk requirements. Partner with Legal, Compliance, Data Privacy, and Cybersecurity teams to maintain oversight of risk mitigation strategies and ensure alignment with best practices.
  • Collaborate with Global Procurement colleagues and relevant stakeholders to oversee the strategic approach to complex negotiations for CRO MSAs, Amendments, including support as necessary for Study-Level Agreements & Purchase Orders, providing guidance and ensuring appropriate processes and frameworks are in place for RFPs, supplier evaluations, and contract development.
  • Maturity to activate procurement resources and facilitate delegation of sourcing activities to drive category priorities while managing expectations with stakeholders and mitigating risk on behalf of Amgen.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The strategic procurement leader we seek is a collaborative and influential business partner with these qualifications.

Doctorate degree and 3 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

Master’s degree and 5 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

Bachelor’s degree and 7 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

Associate’s degree and 12 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

OR

High school diploma / GED and 14 years of Global Strategic Sourcing, Procurement experience

  • Familiarity with procurement platforms such as Ariba, as well as ERP systems and advanced analytics tools to support decision-making and process automation.
  • Excellent problem solving and organizational skills
  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to analyze large datasets, identify trends, and derive actionable insights
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing complex global projects in a matrixed environment.
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks (21 CFR Part 11, GxP, HIPAA, GDPR).
  • Extensive experience with and knowledge of the global vendor landscape in support of all phases of clinical trials, specifically Contract Research Organizations (CRO) and Site Management Organizations (SMO), Academic Medical Centers (AMC), and CRO-adjacent vendors.
  • Global Category Mgmt. with proven record of executive business partnering leading change and enterprise activation of sourcing initiatives driven from expert knowledge of marketplace capabilities
  • Deep understanding of category management principles, supplier relationship management, and contract lifecycle management.
  • Strong financial, legal, and contractual fluency to navigate sales services agreements and deliver business-aligned outcomes.

  • Understanding of regulatory landscapes with the ability to navigate and manage compliance requirements.

  • Strong contractual and regulatory navigation skills for healthcare technology agreements.

What to expect:

The Production Support Analyst keeps the member scheduling and access platform running reliably. The platform is the front door of the member journey, covering scheduling for in-home health assessments and primary care visits. The role works closely with the Senior Product Owner, the scheduling platform engineering team, the central Data and Quality Assurance (QA) teams, IT Service Desk, and external scheduling and health plan partners.

  • Resolve scheduling data errors, duplicate or orphaned appointments, and member access cases using SQL and approved tooling, following PHI handling controls.
  • Serve as first contact for health plan and scheduling partner integration issues. Track partner SLAs and open items to closure.
  • Validate production releases, run smoke tests with QA, and watch for post-release regressions.

  • 2+ years of technical support experience in a corporate environment, including operational support for production systems.
  • 1+ year writing SQL queries to diagnose and resolve data issues.
  • Experience with incident management and an IT service management or ticketing tool.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA and PHI handling, or ability to complete training before receiving production access.
  • Understanding of API and system integration concepts sufficient to troubleshoot integration failures.
  • Strong troubleshooting, decision-making, and written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, changing environment, and to work independently or on a team with good judgment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting healthcare scheduling, contact center, or EHR integration technology.
  • Experience with monitoring and alerting tools and log analysis.
  • Experience with Jira or Azure DevOps.
  • Experience with SQL Reporting Services and Internet Information Services (IIS).
  • Experience reading or debugging Java or VB/.NET code.

Education

Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent experience in an application or production support role with SQL troubleshooting, ideally in healthcare.

jobs.excerpt: Senior Creative Strategist – Paid Social (Meta Ads) | RemotePosition Type: Full-Time, Remote Working Hours: EST Hours About the RoleAt Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Senior Creative Strategist – Paid Social (Meta Ads) to lead creative-first performance marketing across Facebook and Instagram.
jobs.description:
Senior Creative Strategist – Paid Social (Meta Ads) | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: EST Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Senior Creative Strategist – Paid Social (Meta Ads) to lead creative-first performance marketing across Facebook and Instagram.

This is not a traditional media buying role focused primarily on dashboards, bids, and campaign settings. Your biggest impact will come from developing winning ad concepts, compelling hooks, conversion-focused messaging, strong creative briefs, and stories that turn attention into revenue.

You’ll own the creative-performance cycle from idea → creative strategy → launch → testing → optimization → scale.

If you understand why an ad converts — and can consistently turn those insights into better creative — this role is built for you.

What You’ll Own

Creative Strategy – Primary Focus

  • Develop original ad angles, hooks, messaging frameworks, and campaign narratives
  • Generate new creative concepts based on audience pain points, desires, objections, and buying behavior
  • Write detailed, conversion-focused creative briefs for designers, video editors, and UGC creators
  • Develop UGC concepts, scripts, storytelling structures, and video direction
  • Create concepts for static, video, and short-form paid social ads
  • Continuously develop and test new creative variations
  • Turn performance insights into the next generation of creative concepts

Meta Ads Campaign Management

  • Own and scale Facebook and Instagram advertising campaigns
  • Manage campaigns from launch through optimization and scaling
  • Work across multiple client accounts simultaneously
  • Manage monthly ad budgets ranging from $10K to $250K+
  • Maintain accountability for:
    • CPL
    • CPA
    • ROAS
    • Conversion rates
    • Revenue performance
  • Identify opportunities to scale while maintaining efficiency

Creative Testing & Performance Optimization

  • Review campaign and creative performance daily
  • Identify winning creatives, hooks, formats, and messaging angles
  • Build structured creative testing plans
  • Test variations across:
    • Hooks
    • Offers
    • Messaging
    • Visual concepts
    • UGC formats
    • CTAs
    • Audiences
  • Scale winning concepts and quickly replace creative fatigue
  • Pause or iterate underperforming concepts based on data

Creative + Data Feedback Loop

  • Use performance data to understand why creatives succeed or fail
  • Translate CTR, CPL, CPA, ROAS, and conversion data into creative decisions
  • Identify patterns across winning and losing ads
  • Refine messaging, storytelling, positioning, and offers based on campaign insights
  • Build a repeatable system for turning performance data into better creative
  • Maintain a consistent pipeline of fresh concepts for testing

UGC & Performance Creative

  • Develop UGC strategies designed specifically for paid acquisition
  • Write scripts and creative direction for creators
  • Coordinate concepts across designers, editors, and UGC creators
  • Understand pacing, hooks, storytelling, visual hierarchy, and CTAs for short-form ads
  • Repurpose winning concepts into multiple creative formats and variations

Collaboration & Ownership

  • Work closely with designers, editors, creators, and internal marketing teams
  • Provide clear creative direction and actionable feedback
  • Keep creative production aligned with campaign priorities
  • Connect creative strategy directly to revenue and growth objectives
  • Operate independently with strong ownership over performance outcomes

Must-Have Experience & Skills

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience running Facebook and Instagram Ads
  • Proven experience managing $10K+ in monthly ad spend, preferably significantly higher
  • Experience managing multiple advertising accounts simultaneously; 5+ accounts preferred
  • Strong hands-on experience with:
    • Creative strategy
    • Ad concept development
    • Messaging and positioning
    • Creative brief writing
    • Paid social storytelling
    • UGC concepts
    • Static and video ad concepts
  • Strong command of Meta Ads Manager
  • Experience with Facebook Business Suite, Meta Pixel, conversion tracking, and campaign optimization
  • Strong copywriting ability across hooks, CTAs, headlines, and ad messaging
  • Ability to interpret campaign data and translate it into creative decisions
  • Strong written and verbal English communication
  • Ability to work independently during EST hours

Important: Candidates whose experience is limited to operational campaign management or media buying — without direct ownership of creative strategy, messaging, ad concepts, and creative direction — will not be a fit for this role.

What Separates Top Candidates

  • Portfolio of proven winning creatives across UGC, static ads, and short-form video
  • Experience managing $50K–$250K+ monthly Meta ad budgets
  • Ability to clearly explain what they personally contributed to winning campaigns
  • Deep understanding of creative psychology, consumer behavior, conversion flows, and offer positioning
  • Experience managing UGC workflows and creator coordination
  • Experience directing video production and performance creative
  • Strong understanding of creative fatigue and testing velocity
  • Daily use of ChatGPT or other AI tools for creative research, ideation, iteration, and production workflows

Tools & Platforms

Meta Ads Manager | Facebook Business Suite | Meta Pixel | UGC & Creative Tools | Analytics & Conversion Tracking | ChatGPT | AI Creative Tools

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You think creative-first, not dashboard-first
  • You understand the relationship between creative → offer → conversion
  • You can explain why an ad worked — not simply report that it worked
  • You combine strong creative instincts with analytical decision-making
  • You test aggressively and learn quickly
  • You proactively bring new concepts rather than waiting for briefs
  • You care about revenue and conversion performance, not vanity metrics
  • You thrive in fast-paced, performance-driven environments

What a Typical Day Looks Like

You may start by reviewing Meta campaign performance and identifying winning and fatigued creatives. From there, you’ll develop new hooks and ad angles, write briefs for designers and UGC creators, launch new tests, and analyze CPL, CPA, CTR, and ROAS.

You’ll continuously move between creative ideation, campaign execution, performance analysis, and iteration.

In short: you drive paid social growth by combining exceptional creative strategy with performance-focused Meta Ads execution.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Improvement in CPL, CPA, and ROAS
  • Revenue generated through paid social
  • Number and consistency of winning creatives
  • Creative testing velocity
  • Speed from insight → concept → launch
  • Campaign scalability
  • Conversion performance across accounts
  • Ability to maintain performance as spend increases
  • Quality and consistency of creative output

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Creative-first performance marketing role
  • Ownership across both strategy and execution
  • Direct impact on growth and revenue
  • Opportunity to shape messaging and creative direction at scale
  • Exposure to paid social, UGC systems, performance creative, and growth marketing
  • Growth opportunities into Creative Director, Head of Paid Social, or Growth Marketing leadership

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Video Interview
  3. Recruiter Interview
  4. Client Interview
  5. Offer & Background Verification

Apply Now

If you understand how creative drives paid social performance, can consistently develop winning ad concepts, and know how to use Meta campaign data to build better creative, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now and take ownership of creative-driven growth across high-performing Meta campaigns.

jobs.description:
Type: High-agency individual contributor
Products: Single Brain + API Gateway
Location: Full-time, remote (Los Angeles a plus, not required)
Comp: $120,000–$150,000 USD / year

One-liner

Own what gets built and why across Single Brain and API Gateway — turn build → build → build into build → measure → iterate.

About the role

Single Grain combines marketing services, software, and AI. This seat owns product judgment for Single Brain and the API Gateway: which metrics matter, what is blocking them, and what engineering should build next.

Engineering owns how we build. You own what we build and why.

You work daily with a ~6-person engineering team. You do not manage that team as a people manager; you create clarity so their effort lands on the highest-leverage outcomes.

You should be an advanced AI user. Use AI for research, interview synthesis, analytics, specs, prototypes, experiment design, and competitive work so your product decisions get faster and better.

What you will own

  • Identify the highest-leverage product metrics across Single Brain and API Gateway (activation, usage, retention, expansion, revenue, time-to-value, Gateway/integration adoption).

  • Diagnose what is limiting those metrics.

  • Decide what engineering should build next, with clear hypotheses and success criteria.

  • Run strong weekly sprint kickoffs so the team leaves knowing: what metric are we moving, what are we doing to move it, and how will we know it worked.

  • Own customer discovery — talk to customers often; separate loud requests from high-leverage opportunities.

  • Own product analytics and instrumentation quality; no major initiative ships without a measurement plan.

  • Review launches against real results and choose iterate, expand, revert, or move on.

  • Keep the integration / Gateway roadmap intentionally prioritized.

  • Protect the team from low-impact or poorly defined work.

What success looks like

  • By day 30: deep product understanding; customer discovery underway; core journeys/funnels mapped; analytics audited; clear view of which metrics matter and where the biggest opportunities are.

  • By day 60: you own weekly sprint kickoffs; major initiatives have metrics and measurement plans; core funnels instrumented and visible.

  • By day 90: prioritized roadmap tied to measurable outcomes; multiple complete build → measure → iterate cycles; measurable improvement in at least one meaningful product metric. Failure = features still shipping without hypotheses, instrumentation, or post-launch learning.

  • By 6–12 months: durable product OS (Metric → Diagnosis → Hypothesis → Build → Measure → Learn → Iterate); customer discovery and post-launch measurement are standard; CTO is no longer the primary person deciding what engineering builds next; key product/business metrics improved materially.

Evidence we want to see

  • Experience owning a technical software product (APIs, integrations, auth, data fluency).

  • Metrics you personally owned and improved — with diagnosis, not feature lists.

  • Sprint leadership / prioritization with engineering teams.

  • Product analytics and instrumentation ownership (PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel, or similar).

  • Advanced daily AI workflows for product work.

  • High-agency ownership: you set roadmap direction; you are not a conduit or Jira admin.

  • Ideal: early-stage / growth-stage; developer tools, API, infrastructure, or AI products.

What this role is not

Not a project manager, not a backlog clerk, not “collect feature requests,” not “feature shipped = success,” not waiting for the CTO to dictate the roadmap.

How the process works

Application and evidence review → our standard six-question AI prescreen for selected candidates → live discussion / working session (metric → diagnose → propose build → mock sprint kickoff → measurement) → paid exercise if substantial work is required → references.

Benefits

Medical, dental, and vision; life insurance; 401(k) with 4% match; unlimited PTO; monthly UberEats; MacBook; home-office stipend/setup. Subject to plan terms and eligibility.

Apply

Apply with your resume/profile.

jobs.title: Sales Enablement Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Harbor is seeking a Sales Enablement Specialist to join our growing team.
jobs.description:
Harbor is seeking a Sales Enablement Specialist to join our growing team. The Sales Enablement Specialist turns Harbor’s market insights, solution expertise, sales priorities, and operating tools into practical guidance that Client Engagement (CE) teams can use in client conversations. This role is the orchestration layer between Insights/Product/Solutions Marketing, Sales Leadership, Sales and Marketing Operations, and Delivery subject matter experts.

Harbor sells complex services that can span Enterprise Solutions, Business Operations Solutions (BOS), AI, and advisory. The role helps sellers recognize multi-dimensional client needs, lead effective discovery, bring the right Harbor experts together, and progress opportunities with a coherent client approach. It combines strong learning design with analytical judgment: using pipeline and performance evidence to identify capability gaps, prioritize enablement, and assess whether field behaviors are changing.

This is a remote position that can be worked from anywhere in the United States (CST/EST normal business hours).

Cross-Functional Operating Model:

The Specialist makes partner teams’ expertise usable in the field while keeping ownership clear:

Insights / Product / Solutions Marketing

  • Primary ownership: Positioning, value propositions, customer and market insight, competitive messaging, market-facing content, campaigns, and buyer-journey assets. (Marketing Led)
  • Enablement contribution: Translate approved insights and assets into playbooks that show sellers when, why, and how to use them.

Sales Leadership / GEO Leads

  • Primary ownership: Commercial priorities, seller performance, field coaching, and accountability.
  • Enablement contribution: Equip leaders with coaching guides, practice tools, and data-informed views of capability needs.

Sales / Marketing Operations

  • Primary ownership: CRM, process, data, forecasting, systems, and reporting.
  • Enablement contribution: Enable consistent use of tools and processes; interpret validated data to target enablement.

Delivery / Subject Matter Experts

  • Primary ownership: Technical expertise, client experience, delivery realities, and proof.
  • Enablement contribution: Turn expertise, use cases, and outcomes into credible discovery prompts, proof points, and handoffs.

Sales Enablement

  • Primary ownership: Field adoption and practical application of the above.
  • Enablement contribution: Orchestrate the inputs into repeatable conversations, playbooks, training, and reinforcement.

Key Responsibilities:

Orchestrate Field-Ready Enablement

  • Partner with Marketing to understand the approved positioning, value proposition, customer insight, competitive context, and buyer-journey assets for Harbor solutions.
  • Convert those inputs into practical sales playbooks: opportunity signals, discovery questions, value narratives, proof points, likely objections, adjacent-solution paths, and examples of effective client conversations.
  • Explain how and when to use marketing assets at each stage of the buyer journey; do not own market positioning, messaging strategy, campaigns, or market-facing content.
  • Coordinate enablement across solution lines so sellers can connect Enterprise Solutions, BOS, AI, and advisory where client needs call for a multidisciplinary response.

Enable Complex Discovery and Solution Orchestration

  • Build guidance that helps CEs identify client problems, assess business impact, map stakeholders and buying processes, qualify opportunities, and agree on next steps.
  • Create cross-solution discovery frameworks and handoff practices that help CEs assemble the right Delivery and SME support and maintain a clear, coordinated client conversation.
  • Develop practical talk tracks, call plans, account-planning tools, objection responses, case examples, and role-play scenarios grounded in Harbor’s services and delivery experience.

Use Data to Prioritize Enablement

  • Partner with Sales/Marketing Operations to analyze validated pipeline and performance data, including pipeline creation and coverage, stage conversion, win/loss patterns, sales-cycle length, slippage, forecast movement, opportunity source, and solution-line mix.
  • Identify patterns that may indicate a skill, process, or adoption gap; recommend targeted playbooks, training, coaching resources, or reinforcement rather than applying generic training across the team.
  • Use Salesforce, Clari, Power BI, learning-system data, and field feedback to assess participation, adoption, proficiency, and business indicators. Distinguish correlation from causation and validate definitions with Operations.
  • Turn analysis into clear recommendations for GEO Leads and enablement partners while leaving forecast ownership, CRM administration, data definitions, and performance accountability with their respective owners.

Support Sales Methodology and Field Coaching

  • Translate Harbor’s sales methodology into repeatable workflows for prospecting, discovery, qualification, stakeholder alignment, solution design, opportunity progression, and close planning.
  • Partner with GEO Leads to identify coaching priorities and provide manager guides, observation tools, practice sessions, and reinforcement resources. GEO Leads retain accountability for seller performance and coaching.
  • Facilitate workshops, onboarding, deal simulations, call reviews, knowledge checks, and ongoing reinforcement that help CEs apply the approach in live opportunities.

Design, Launch, and Improve Learning

  • Own assigned enablement initiatives from needs assessment through design, development, launch, and evaluation; manage scope, timelines, contributors, reviews, and dependencies.
  • Apply adult-learning and instructional-design principles across instructor-led, virtual, digital, and on-the-job learning. Develop facilitator guides, learner materials, job aids, exercises, and reinforcement plans.
  • Use feedback from wins, losses, objections, client needs, Delivery, and the field to continuously improve enablement and inform partner teams.

Enable Tools and Processes

  • Help CEs apply Salesforce, Clari, Workday Learning, and related sales tools as part of their day-to-day workflows; coordinate system or process changes with Operations.
  • Work with Operations and Marketing to align enablement resources with CRM stages, campaign activity, pipeline reviews, and forecast routines without duplicating system ownership.

Measures of Success

  • CEs can consistently recognize target client needs, conduct effective discovery, connect relevant Harbor capabilities, and use proof points appropriately.
  • Enablement resources are adopted and used in the field, with GEO Lead feedback showing improved coaching consistency and application.
  • Learning participation, proficiency, and readiness improve for priority topics and audiences.
  • Pipeline and sales indicators—such as coverage, stage conversion, slippage, opportunity quality, sales-cycle progression, and cross-solution activity—are monitored with Operations to evaluate where enablement may be contributing to improvement.
  • Enablement initiatives are delivered on agreed timelines, with clear ownership, measurable objectives, and ongoing refinement based on evidence.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in sales enablement, revenue operations and strategy, marketing, learning and development, instructional design, analytics, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of relevant experience in sales enablement, sales effectiveness, revenue operations, instructional design, or a related business-facing role; experience enabling complex services, consulting, or professional-services sales is strongly preferred.
  • Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability to interpret pipeline, conversion, activity, and learning data; advanced Excel skills and experience with Power BI or similar analytics tools preferred.
  • Experience with CRM and sales execution tools such as Salesforce and Clari; familiarity with Workday Learning or a comparable LMS and Articulate 360 or similar content tools preferred.
  • Ability to translate complex service offerings and SME input into practical seller guidance; strong facilitation, communication, consulting, and project-management skills across functions.
  • Uses AI-enabled tools responsibly; stays organized and adapts to shifting priorities in a client-focused environment.

About Us:

Harbor is the preeminent provider of expert services across strategy, legal technology, operations, and intelligence. Our globally integrated team of 900+ strategists, technologists, and specialists navigate alongside our clients – leading law firms, corporations, and their law departments – to provide essential resources and invaluable insights. Anchored in a rich heritage of deep knowledge, steadfast relationships, and mutual respect, our unwavering dedication lies in shaping the future of the legal industry and fostering enduring partnerships within our community and ecosystem.

Role Summary

The Customer Success Coordinator (CSC) combines hands-on case resolution with direct ownership of the plays that turn platform access into real adoption. Acting as an extension of the Customer Success Manager (CSM) who owns the account relationship, the CSC runs day-to-day adoption and support activities — resolving support tickets and case-level issues affecting end users and providers, while also executing structured onboarding and go-live readiness work for new users and services. The CSC provides coverage continuity for their assigned CSM(s) and is often the team member closest to an account's day-to-day workflow reality.

Key Responsibilities

  • Adoption & Activation Plays: Runs defined adoption plays in coordination with the account's CSM, supporting go-live readiness for new users or services and following up to confirm new capacity is actually being used, not just enabled.
  • End-User Training & Enablement: Delivers or coordinates end-user training tied to onboarding and platform rollouts, helping turn system access into day-to-day usage.
  • Ticket Management: Manages incoming support tickets from internal teams and end users via email and ticketing systems, ensuring timely acknowledgment, routing, and resolution.
  • Issue Resolution: Investigates and resolves escalated inquiries and support requests by identifying root cause and implementing the best resolution path.
  • Customer Growth & Lead Routing: Supports customer growth by surfacing and routing qualified leads identified through account relationships to the sales organization, ensuring lead information is communicated clearly and followed through to resolution.
  • CSM & Account Team Support: Assists the CSM(s) they support with account-related needs and requests, providing timely follow-through and coordination across relevant internal teams.

  • Data & Reporting: Assists with tracking and reporting on Customer Success metrics, data integrity, and operational performance to support team visibility and decision-making.
  • Early Risk Flagging: Surfaces account health or utilization risk signals observed through day-to-day casework to the account's CSM, acting as an early warning system.
  • Cross-Functional Support: Acts as a support resource for internal teams and the accounts they support, addressing a broad range of operational and account-related requests.
  • Provider Escalation: Works with CSMs and internal teams to resolve provider escalations that impact end-user care.
  • Ad Hoc Project Support: Contributes to ad hoc Customer Success projects and initiatives as assigned, supporting broader team goals and organizational priorities.

  • Comfort working with data and CRM tools to support tracking, reporting, and issue resolution

  • Prior experience supporting a Customer Success, Account Management, or customer-facing team
